title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Overview
text: Research The maximal-parabolic Eisenstein realization, its irreducible compact-type ladder, and rotation covariance. Lattice Eisenstein series and representations Discussion Varying a four-dimensional lattice turns the elliptic coefficients into automorphic functions on a special linear group. We identify both their inducing data and the irreducible module they generate. This is a different group action from the Möbius action on the ball.

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Lemma EI1 · Harmonic numerators in every derivative order
text: EI1 Lemma EI1. Harmonic numerators in every derivative order For ν ∈ ℕ₀³ , r = |ν| , and N(q) = |q|² , there is a quaternion-valued homogeneous polynomial H_(ν) of degree r + 1 , with harmonic real components, such that G_(ν)(q) = (H_(ν)(q))/(N(q)^(r + 2)). It obeys H₀ = q̄ and H_(ν + eⱼ) = N∂ⱼH_(ν) − 2(r + 2)xⱼH_(ν) . Start with H₀ = q̄ . Differentiation gives the recurrence , H_(ν + eⱼ) = N∂ⱼH_(ν) − 2(r + 2)xⱼH_(ν)., (E3) It is polynomial and has degree r + 2 . If H_(ν) is harmonic of degree r + 1 , then Δ (N∂ⱼH_(ν)) = (4r + 8)∂ⱼH_(ν), Δ (xⱼH_(ν)) = 2∂ⱼH_(ν), so (E3) is harmonic. This proves the lemma for every order.

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Construction EI-C1 · The lattice Eisenstein function
text: EI-C1 Construction EI-C1. The lattice Eisenstein function For w > 4 and f ∈ I_(w) , form ℰ_(f)(g) = ∑_(m ∈ ℤ⁴ ∖ {0})f(mg).

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Theorem EI2 · A maximal-parabolic Eisenstein series
text: EI2 Theorem EI2. A maximal-parabolic Eisenstein series cf. [2, §§2.4–2.5, Lemma 2.9] For w > 4 , ℰ_(f) is smooth, left Γ -invariant, of moderate growth with all right derivatives, and satisfies ℰ_(R(h)f)(g) = ℰ_(f)(gh) . Moreover ℰ_(f)(g) = 2ζ(w)∑_(γ ∈ (P ∩ Γ ) \ Γ)F_(f)(γg). The section law is F_(f)(pg) = |d|^(− w)F_(f)(g) . In normalized left-equivariant/right-translation induction, with δ_(P)(p) = |d|^(− 4) , the inducing character is χ(p) = |d|^(2 − w) . For an odd derivative order r ≥ 3 , the scalar components of G_(ν) give w = r + 3 and χ = |d|^(− (r + 1)) . The sum and all its g -derivatives converge uniformly on compact subsets of G₄ : differentiation preserves degree − w , and |mg|≫_(C)|m| on a compact set C . Hence ℰ_(f) is smooth, left Γ -invariant, and , ℰ_(R(h)f)(g) = ℰ_(f)(gh)., (E6) Each scalar component of G_(ν) is such an f , so EI-C1 includes the original coefficient sums. The bound |ℰ_(f)(g)| ≤ C_(f)‖g^(− 1)‖^(w)∑_(m ≠ 0)|m|^(− w) , and the same bound for right derivatives, gives moderate growth. Let P be the maximal parabolic consisting of matrices p = (A, b; 0, d), det (A)d = 1, which stabilizes the row line ℝe₄ . Put F_(f)(g) = f(e₄g) . Then , F_(f)(pg) = |d|^(− w)F_(f)(g), δ_(P)(p) = |d|^(− 4)., (E7) Every primitive integral row occurs as e₄γ , and the stabilizer of the primitive line is P ∩ Γ . Grouping a nonzero row by its positive gcd and then identifying opposite primitive rows gives , ℰ_(f)(g) = 2ζ(w)∑_(γ ∈ (P ∩ Γ ) \ Γ)F_(f)(γg)., (E8) This is a maximal-parabolic Eisenstein series in its region of absolute convergence. In the left-equivariant/right-translation convention F(pg) = δ_(P)(p)^(1/2)χ(p)F(g) , its normalized inducing character is , χ(p) = |d|^(2 − w) = |d|^(− (r + 1))., (E9) Specifying the section law removes any ambiguity from authors who use the inverse character or opposite parabolic.

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Definition EI-D2 · The Vanishing-Moment Subspace
text: EI-D2 Definition EI-D2. The Vanishing-Moment Subspace For even w ≥ 6 , the vanishing-moment subspace of I_(w) is , ℳ_(w) = {f ∈ I_(w) : ∫_(S³)f(ω)p(ω)dσ(ω) = 0 for every p ∈ P_(d)}., (E10)

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Proposition EI3 · Moment kernel and finite-dimensional quotient
text: EI3 Proposition EI3. Moment kernel and finite-dimensional quotient For even w ≥ 6 , the moment map gives an equivariant exact sequence 0 → ℳ_(w) → I_(w) → P_(w − 4)^(∨) → 0. Its compact-finite kernel is ⨁_(j ≥ 0)Y_(w − 2 + 2j) . Every scalar derivative kernel of order r = w − 3 lies in its minimal compact type Y_(w − 2) . The pairing is bilinear, not Hermitian. Since the product has degree − 4 , angular change of variables under g ∈ SL₄ shows ∫_(S³)f(ωg)p(ωg)dσ(ω) = ∫_(S³)f(ω)p(ω)dσ(ω). Indeed for η = ωg/|ωg| , dσ(η) = |ωg|^(− 4)dσ(ω) . Thus (E10) is invariant, and the pairing induces an exact sequence , 0 ⟶ ℳ_(w) ⟶ I_(w) ⟶ P_(w − 4)^(∨) ⟶ 0., (E11) Surjectivity follows from the nondegenerate spherical pairing on the finite-dimensional polynomial space. Harmonic decomposition of P_(w − 4) gives , (ℳ_(w))_(K₄) = ⨁_(j ≥ 0)Y_(w − 2 + 2j),, (E12) where the subscript means K₄ -finite vectors. The low harmonics Y₀,Y₂,…,Y_(w − 4) constitute the finite-dimensional quotient. By EI1, every scalar Fueter kernel derivative of order r = w − 3 belongs to the minimal compact type Y_(w − 2) of this kernel.

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Theorem EI4 · Irreducibility and harmonic transitions
text: EI4 Theorem EI4. Irreducibility and harmonic transitions cf. [1] The (sl₄,SO(4)) -module (ℳ_(w))_(K₄) is irreducible for every even w ≥ 6 . Its compact types are ⨁_(j ≥ 0)Y_(w − 2 + 2j) ≃ ⨁_(j ≥ 0)V_(w − 2 + 2j) ⊠ V_(w − 2 + 2j). For a symmetric trace-free real matrix A , write Q_(A)(x) = xAx^(t), D_(A)H = (xA) ⋅ ∇ H, T_(A)H = ∑ᵢⱼAᵢⱼ∂ᵢ∂ⱼH. Represent a compact type H ∈ Yₗ by f_(H)(x) = |x|^(− w − l)H(x) . On S³ the infinitesimal action is , dR(A)H = D_(A)H − (w + l)Q_(A)H., (E13) It has harmonic degrees l + 2,l,l − 2 . Its projection onto degree l − 2 is exactly , pr_(l − 2) dR(A)H = (l + 2 − w)/(4l(l + 1))T_(A)H., (E14) To see this, Δ D_(A)H = 2T_(A)H and Δ²(Q_(A)H) = 8T_(A)H . Harmonic decomposition therefore gives degree- l − 2 terms T_(A)H/(2l) in D_(A)H|_(S³) and T_(A)H/[4l(l + 1)] in (Q_(A)H)|_(S³) , yielding (E14). The degree- l + 2 term is − (w + l) times the top harmonic part of Q_(A)H . The lowering map vanishes precisely at l = w − 2 and is nonzero at every subsequent degree in (E12); the raising map is nonzero at every degree. Nonzeroness can be seen over the complexified Lie algebra by taking H = (x₁ + ix₂)^(l) and quadratic forms (x₁ ± ix₂)² : the plus choice raises harmonically, the minus choice gives a nonzero T_(A)H when l ≥ 2 . Each Yₗ is an irreducible K₄ -module of multiplicity one. Any nonzero submodule contains a compact type; successive nonzero lowering and raising maps then give all of (E12). This proves irreducibility. The identification Yₗ ≃ Vₗ ⊠ Vₗ follows from the usual Spin (4) harmonic-polynomial representation; ( − 1, − 1) acts trivially.

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Theorem EI5 · The coefficient-generated automorphic module
text: EI5 Theorem EI5. The coefficient-generated automorphic module For odd r ≥ 3 , the scalar components of g ↦ E_(ν)(ℤ⁴g) , |ν| = r , generate an automorphic (sl₄,SO(4)) -module isomorphic to (ℳ_(r + 3))_(K₄) . The Eisenstein map is injective on this module. Its minimal compact type is Y_(r + 1) . An intertwining sum could conceivably vanish on the entire module, so this needs a proof. Choose H ∈ Y_(w − 2) with H(e₄) ≠ 0 , and put gₐ = diag (a,a,a,a^(− 3)), a → ∞, f_(H)(x) = |x|^(− 2w + 2)H(x). The rows (0,0,0,k) contribute exactly 2ζ(w)a^(3w)H(e₄) . All other rows satisfy |f_(H)(x)| ≤ C|x|^(− w) . For m^(′) ≠ 0 , ∑_(k ∈ ℤ)(a²|m^(′)|² + a^(− 6)k²)^(− w/2) ≪ a^(− w)|m^(′)|^(− w) + a^(4 − w)|m^(′)|^(1 − w). Both sums over m^(′) ∈ ℤ³ ∖ 0 converge for w > 4 . Consequently , ℰ_(f_(H))(gₐ) = 2ζ(w)a^(3w)H(e₄) + O(a^(4 − w))., (E15) The Eisenstein map is nonzero on the minimal type, hence injective on the irreducible module (E12). The scalar components of the order- r kernel derivatives contain a nonzero element of that type: for example ∂ₓ^(r)G(ix) = − i( − 1)^(r)(3)ᵣx^(− r − 3) for x > 0 . Its compact orbit spans the type and its enveloping-algebra orbit spans (E12).

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Corollary EI6 · The first nonzero derivative order
text: EI6 Corollary EI6. The first nonzero derivative order For r = 3 , the inducing degree is − 6 , the normalized character is |d|^(− 4) , the minimal compact type is V₄ ⊠ V₄ of dimension 25 , and the finite-dimensional quotient of I₆ is P₂^(∨) of dimension 10 . Insert w = 6 in EI3–EI5. The dimensions are (4 + 1)² = 25 and ((2 + 4 − 1)/(3)) = 10 .

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Proposition EI7 · The coefficient action descends to the rotation group
text: EI7 Proposition EI7. The coefficient action descends to the rotation group Let U_(− r − 3) be the right- ℍ span of the order- r kernel derivatives, with r > 1 , and let ρ(a,b)f(q) = bf(a^(− 1)qb) for unit quaternions a,b . Set α_(L)(f) = ∑_(λ ≠ 0)f(λ) . Then (σ(a,b)α)(f) = bα(ρ(a,b)^(− 1)f), α_(aLb^(− 1)) = σ(a,b)α_(L). This is a genuine real representation on right- ℍ -linear functionals and factors through SO(4) . The identity G(a^(− 1)qb) = b^(− 1)G(q)a follows directly from the kernel formula. Differentiate it in any real coordinate directions. The chain rule expresses rotated order- r derivatives using all four real derivative directions, with constant right quaternion factors. The kernel is also right regular: direct differentiation gives ∂ₜG + ∂ₓG i + ∂_(y)G j + ∂_(z)G k = 0 . This identity, and its derivatives, eliminate every time derivative in favor of spatial derivatives with right coefficients. Thus U_(− r − 3) is invariant under ρ . The formula for ρ gives its group law and right- ℍ linearity. Reindexing the absolutely convergent sum gives the displayed identity. For composition, the two output factors multiply as b₁b₂ , and the precomposition is ρ(k₂^(− 1))ρ(k₁^(− 1)) = ρ((k₁k₂)^(− 1)) . At ( − 1, − 1) , the input representation is − 1 , while the output also gets − 1 , so σ( − 1, − 1)α(f) = − α( − f) = α(f) . The kernel of Spin (4) → SO(4) therefore acts trivially.

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Harmonic numerators of the kernel derivatives
text: Harmonic numerators of the kernel derivatives Lemma EI1. Harmonic numerators in every derivative order For ν ∈ ℕ₀³ , r = |ν| , and N(q) = |q|² , there is a quaternion-valued homogeneous polynomial H_(ν) of degree r + 1 , with harmonic real components, such that G_(ν)(q) = (H_(ν)(q))/(N(q)^(r + 2)). It obeys H₀ = q̄ and H_(ν + eⱼ) = N∂ⱼH_(ν) − 2(r + 2)xⱼH_(ν) . Discussion The lattice sums E_(ν)(L) and their relation to derivatives of the regular part of ℘_(L,j) are established in N1–N3. They converge for r > 1 , and even r gives zero. We therefore focus on odd r ≥ 3 . Ordinary Taylor coefficients include the multi-index factorials.

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Homogeneous sections and Eisenstein summation
text: Homogeneous sections and Eisenstein summation Set G₄ = SL₄(ℝ) , Γ = SL₄(ℤ) , and K₄ = SO(4) . Vectors act on the right, and L_(g) = ℤ⁴g . For real w > 4 , write I_(w) for the space of smooth functions f : ℝ⁴ ∖ {0} → ℂ such that f(tx) = |t|^(− w)f(x) (x ≠ 0, t ∈ ℝ^(×)). The condition with t = − 1 makes every f ∈ I_(w) even. The action of G₄ is (R(g)f)(x) = f(xg). Homogeneity is preserved because (tx)g = t(xg) , and R(g)R(h) = R(gh) follows from (xg)h = x(gh) . Construction EI-C1. The lattice Eisenstein function For w > 4 and f ∈ I_(w) , form ℰ_(f)(g) = ∑_(m ∈ ℤ⁴ ∖ {0})f(mg). Let e₄ = (0,0,0,1) and P = {(A, b; 0, d) : det (A)d = 1}, F_(f)(g) = f(e₄g). Theorem EI2. A maximal-parabolic Eisenstein series cf. [2, §§2.4–2.5, Lemma 2.9] For w > 4 , ℰ_(f) is smooth, left Γ -invariant, of moderate growth with all right derivatives, and satisfies ℰ_(R(h)f)(g) = ℰ_(f)(gh) . Moreover ℰ_(f)(g) = 2ζ(w)∑_(γ ∈ (P ∩ Γ ) \ Γ)F_(f)(γg). The section law is F_(f)(pg) = |d|^(− w)F_(f)(g) . In normalized left-equivariant/right-translation induction, with δ_(P)(p) = |d|^(− 4) , the inducing character is χ(p) = |d|^(2 − w) . For an odd derivative order r ≥ 3 , the scalar components of G_(ν) give w = r + 3 and χ = |d|^(− (r + 1)) .

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: The irreducible module selected by the coefficients
text: The irreducible module selected by the coefficients For even w ≥ 6 put d = w − 4 , and let P_(d) be the homogeneous degree- d polynomials on ℝ⁴ , with action p(x) ↦ p(xg) . Let dσ be Euclidean surface measure on S³ . Definition EI-D2. The Vanishing-Moment Subspace For even w ≥ 6 , the vanishing-moment subspace of I_(w) is , ℳ_(w) = {f ∈ I_(w) : ∫_(S³)f(ω)p(ω)dσ(ω) = 0 for every p ∈ P_(d)}., (E10) Write Yₗ for complex harmonic homogeneous polynomials of degree l restricted to S³ ; Vₗ = Sym^(l) ℂ² . Proposition EI3. Moment kernel and finite-dimensional quotient For even w ≥ 6 , the moment map gives an equivariant exact sequence 0 → ℳ_(w) → I_(w) → P_(w − 4)^(∨) → 0. Its compact-finite kernel is ⨁_(j ≥ 0)Y_(w − 2 + 2j) . Every scalar derivative kernel of order r = w − 3 lies in its minimal compact type Y_(w − 2) . Theorem EI4. Irreducibility and harmonic transitions cf. [1] The (sl₄,SO(4)) -module (ℳ_(w))_(K₄) is irreducible for every even w ≥ 6 . Its compact types are ⨁_(j ≥ 0)Y_(w − 2 + 2j) ≃ ⨁_(j ≥ 0)V_(w − 2 + 2j) ⊠ V_(w − 2 + 2j).

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Nonvanishing and the automorphic realization
text: Nonvanishing and the automorphic realization Theorem EI5. The coefficient-generated automorphic module For odd r ≥ 3 , the scalar components of g ↦ E_(ν)(ℤ⁴g) , |ν| = r , generate an automorphic (sl₄,SO(4)) -module isomorphic to (ℳ_(r + 3))_(K₄) . The Eisenstein map is injective on this module. Its minimal compact type is Y_(r + 1) . Discussion The fixed-order coefficients occupy the minimal compact type. General SL₄ transformations generate the larger space (E12); they do not preserve the flat Fueter equation or act within the finite tuple of coefficients. This specifies an irreducible real-place Harish-Chandra module. It does not assert a unitary L²(Γ \ G₄) realization or a discrete series of SL₄ . The proof concerns the algebraic module of K -finite automorphic functions; a choice of globalization/topology or an adelic classification with finite-place constituents is additional work. A coefficient can vanish at a particular symmetric lattice even though the automorphic function is nonzero. For example cubic-lattice symmetries force numerous components to vanish. Corollary EI6. The first nonzero derivative order For r = 3 , the inducing degree is − 6 , the normalized character is |d|^(− 4) , the minimal compact type is V₄ ⊠ V₄ of dimension 25 , and the finite-dimensional quotient of I₆ is P₂^(∨) of dimension 10 .

title: Lattice Eisenstein series and representations
heading: Rotation covariance of the coefficient tuple
text: Rotation covariance of the coefficient tuple Proposition EI7. The coefficient action descends to the rotation group Let U_(− r − 3) be the right- ℍ span of the order- r kernel derivatives, with r > 1 , and let ρ(a,b)f(q) = bf(a^(− 1)qb) for unit quaternions a,b . Set α_(L)(f) = ∑_(λ ≠ 0)f(λ) . Then (σ(a,b)α)(f) = bα(ρ(a,b)^(− 1)f), α_(aLb^(− 1)) = σ(a,b)α_(L). This is a genuine real representation on right- ℍ -linear functionals and factors through SO(4) . Discussion The arithmetic quotient is Γ \ G₄/K₄ ; lattice stabilizers give the usual orbifold interpretation. The scalar-component model above avoids choosing local frames. The underlying induced representations are part of the theory studied by [1]; the proofs here specify our conventions directly. For the standard primitive-vector identity compare [2], §2.5. The next article establishes the theta and special-value interpretation, including the cubic example.

title: Classical Harmonic Theta Modularity
heading: Overview
text: Expository Established results and their sources, separate from the project research construction. Classical Harmonic Theta Modularity Use the theta normalizations and the weight-six form.

title: Classical Harmonic Theta Modularity
heading: Theorem TH2 · Modularity and cuspidality of the coset vector
text: TH2 Theorem TH2. Modularity and cuspidality of the coset vector [3]; [1, Ch. 14] For an even integral positive-definite rank-four lattice and homogeneous harmonic H of even degree ℓ > 0 , the coset vector is a holomorphic cusp form of weight k = 2 + ℓ for the lattice Weil representation. Explicitly, Θ_(μ)(τ + 1) = e^(2πiQ(μ))Θ_(μ)(τ), Θ_(μ)( − 1/τ) = − (τ^(k))/(√(|D|))∑_(η ∈ D)e^(− 2πi(μ,η))Θ_(η)(τ). The pairings and Q(μ) in the phases are taken modulo ℤ . The series and its derivatives converge locally uniformly in the upper half-plane by Gaussian decay. Integrality gives Q(λ + μ) ≡ Q(μ) (mod ℤ) for λ ∈ L , proving the first transformation. For the Fourier transform ϕ̂(y) = ∫_(ℝ⁴)ϕ(x)e^(− 2πi(x,y))dx , the Gaussian identity and harmonicity give H(x)e^(πiτN(x)) [ˆ](y) = ( − iτ)^(− 2)τ^(− ℓ)H(y)e^(− πiN(y)/τ). Indeed multiplication by H(x) becomes H( − (2πi)^(− 1)∂_(y)) on the Gaussian transform. All contracted lower-degree terms contain a Laplacian of H and vanish; the highest-degree term is τ^(− ℓ)H(y) . Apply this identity with − 1/τ and use the shifted-lattice Poisson formula. The volume factor is vol (ℝ⁴/L)^(− 1) = |D|^(− 1/2) , and ( − i( − 1/τ))^(− 2)( − 1/τ)^(− ℓ) = − τ^(2 + ℓ) . Poisson initially gives the phase with a plus sign; replacing η by − η gives the displayed sign since H is even and Θ_(− η) = Θ_(η) . Each component has zero constant term: the only possible norm-zero vector is zero and H(0) = 0 . All other terms decay exponentially at infinity. The two transformations generate the modular group and express every cusp transform as a finite linear combination of components. They therefore prove holomorphy and vanishing at every cusp. These are the harmonic theta transformation laws of [3]; see also [1], Chapter 14, for the general framework.

title: Classical Harmonic Theta Modularity
heading: Corollary TH6 · The modular representation attached to the example
text: TH6 Corollary TH6. The modular representation attached to the example [2, §§3–6] The newform f determines a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(A_(ℚ)) of conductor four and trivial central character. Its real factor is the weight-six discrete series; its holomorphic component has lowest weight six on SL₂(ℝ) . TH4 establishes a normalized new eigenform of exact level four and trivial nebentypus. Apply the standard adelization and newform correspondence: the finite conductor is the new level, the central character is the nebentypus, and the holomorphic weight specifies the archimedean discrete series. This correspondence is an external representation-theoretic input, not a consequence of the numerical Fourier expansion. In the unitary automorphic normalization, L(f,s) = L(π_(f),s − 5/2) ; hence the value here is L(π_(f),5/2) . See the published reference to [2] for the correspondence.

title: Classical Harmonic Theta Modularity
heading: Harmonic Theta Transformation
text: Harmonic Theta Transformation Theorem TH2. Modularity and cuspidality of the coset vector [3]; [1, Ch. 14] For an even integral positive-definite rank-four lattice and homogeneous harmonic H of even degree ℓ > 0 , the coset vector is a holomorphic cusp form of weight k = 2 + ℓ for the lattice Weil representation. Explicitly, Θ_(μ)(τ + 1) = e^(2πiQ(μ))Θ_(μ)(τ), Θ_(μ)( − 1/τ) = − (τ^(k))/(√(|D|))∑_(η ∈ D)e^(− 2πi(μ,η))Θ_(η)(τ). The pairings and Q(μ) in the phases are taken modulo ℤ .

title: Classical Harmonic Theta Modularity

The modular representation attached to the example [2, §§3–6] The newform f determines a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(A_(ℚ)) of conductor four and trivial central character. Its real factor is the weight-six discrete series; its holomorphic component has lowest weight six on SL₂(ℝ) . title: Harmonic theta series and special L-values
heading: Overview
text: Research Mellin formulas, harmonic theta modularity, and an explicit quaternionic coefficient equal to a critical value of a weight-six newform. Harmonic theta series and special L-values Discussion The coefficients of quaternionic elliptic functions can be converted into Mellin transforms of harmonic theta series. On the cubic lattice this leads to a specific newform and an exact, nonzero special value. The normalizations below distinguish the general even-lattice convention from the cubic example.

title: Harmonic theta series and special L-values
heading: Definition TH-D1 · Harmonic Theta Functions
text: TH-D1 Definition TH-D1. Harmonic Theta Functions The harmonic theta function is θ_(L,H)(it) = ∑_(λ ∈ L)H(λ)e^(− πtN(λ)) (t > 0). If the Euclidean bilinear form is integral on L and N(λ) is even for every λ ∈ L , the coset theta functions are Θ_(μ)(τ) = ∑_(λ ∈ L + μ)H(λ)e^(2πiτQ(λ)), Θ_(L,H) = Θ₀, Im τ > 0.

title: Harmonic theta series and special L-values
heading: Theorem TH1 · A convergent Mellin formula for each elliptic coefficient
text: TH1 Theorem TH1. A convergent Mellin formula for each elliptic coefficient Let ν ∈ ℕ₀³ have odd order r ≥ 3 , and let H be any real component of the numerator H_(ν) . For every full Euclidean lattice L , E_(ν,H)(L) : = ∑_(λ ≠ 0)(H(λ))/(N(λ)^(r + 2)) = (π^(r + 2))/(Γ (r + 2))∫₀^(∞)t^(r + 1)θ_(L,H)(it) dt. Both the lattice sum and the interchange of summation and integration are absolutely convergent. The numerator has degree r + 1 . Thus each absolute summand is bounded by a constant times |λ|^(− r − 3) , whose exponent exceeds the lattice dimension four. The gamma integral gives, for s = r + 2 , ∑_(λ ≠ 0)|H(λ)|∫₀^(∞)t^(s − 1)e^(− πtN(λ))dt = (Γ (s))/(π^(s))∑_(λ ≠ 0)(|H(λ)|)/(N(λ)^(s)) < ∞. Fubini's theorem now gives the formula. The argument also applies to any homogeneous harmonic numerator of degree r + 1 , including linear combinations of the kernel numerators.

title: Harmonic theta series and special L-values
heading: Corollary TH3 · Critical values with all normalizing factors fixed
text: TH3 Corollary TH3. Critical values with all normalizing factors fixed Under TH1's hypotheses, if L is even integral, then E_(ν,H)(L) = 2^(− (r + 2))L(Θ_(L,H),r + 2). The theta form has weight k = r + 3 , and the evaluation point is k − 1 . In particular the first potentially nonzero coefficients, of order r = 3 , evaluate weight-six cusp forms at s = 5 . Group the absolutely convergent lattice sum by m = Q(λ) and use N(λ) = 2m . This gives exactly the factor 2^(− (r + 2)) . TH2 gives the weight. The usual critical integers for the weight- k holomorphic cusp-form L -function are 1,…,k − 1 , from the archimedean gamma factors in the functional equation; hence this is the upper critical value in the classical normalization. No Hecke-eigenform hypothesis is required for the identity.

title: Harmonic theta series and special L-values
heading: Theorem TH4 · The exact harmonic theta identity
text: TH4 Theorem TH4. The exact harmonic theta identity [2, Chs. 5, 7, 14]; [4, Thms. 1.64–1.65]; [1, Thms. 2.4–2.5, p. 835] One has ϑ(τ) = 4η(2τ)¹², ∑_(m ∈ ℤ⁴ ∖ {0})(H₄(m))/(|m|¹⁰) = 4L(f,5). The normalized eta product f is the unique newform in S₆(Γ₀(4)) , with trivial character. First Δ ∑ xⱼ⁴ = 12N and Δ (N²) = 24N , so H₄ is harmonic. To use TH2 without changing the Fourier convention, take the even Euclidean lattice √(2)L₀ , of Gram matrix 2I₄ . Its theta series with numerator H₄ is 4ϑ , because H₄(√(2)m) = 4H₄(m) . Its level is four, its determinant is sixteen, and the scalar theta transformation theorem gives weight 2 + 4 = 6 and character (16/ ⋅ ) = 1 on Γ₀(4) . Hence ϑ ∈ S₆(Γ₀(4)) . This scalar specialization of the Weil transformation law is a standard theta theorem; [2], Chapter 14, is a published reference. For the eta product use the standard eta-quotient criterion and cusp-order formula in [4], Chapter 1. For ∏_(δ|N)η(δτ)^(r_(δ)) the weight is (1)/(2) ∑ r_(δ) , the congruences are ∑ δr_(δ) ≡ ∑ (N/δ)r_(δ) ≡ 0 (mod 24) , and the character is the Kronecker symbol associated to ( − 1)^(k) ∏ δ^(r_(δ)) . Here N = 4 , r₂ = 12 , and both sums equal 24 . The character is trivial since 2¹² is a square. At a cusp of denominator c|4 the order is (4)/(24)∑_(δ|4)(gcd (c,δ)²r_(δ))/(gcd (c,4/c)cδ) = 1 (c = 1,2,4). Thus f is a nonzero cusp form of the same weight, level, and character. For completeness the dimension calculation uses the standard Riemann–Roch formula, for even k > 2 , dim Sₖ(Γ ) = (k − 1)(g − 1) + (k/2 − 1)c + ⌊ k/4 ⌋ e₂ + ⌊ k/3 ⌋ e₃. For Γ₀(4) the index is six, there are three cusps, no elliptic points, and genus zero. The formula gives − 5 + 2 ⋅ 3 = 1 . For level one the data (g,c,e₂,e₃) = (0,1,1,1) give dimension zero in weight six; for level two the data (0,2,1,0) also give zero. Therefore there is no oldspace at level four. These dimension formulas are standard inputs, treated in [2], Chapters 5 and 7. The eight shortest lattice vectors have H₄ = 1/2 , so the first coefficient of ϑ is four. The first coefficient of f is one. Equality follows from the one-dimensional cusp space. Its normalized generator is a Hecke eigenform and is new because the oldspace is zero. Finally group the absolutely convergent harmonic lattice sum by |m|² to obtain L(ϑ,5) = 4L(f,5) ; TH1's convergence estimate applies to any harmonic quartic.

title: Harmonic theta series and special L-values
heading: Theorem TH5 · An individual quaternionic elliptic coefficient
text: TH5 Theorem TH5. An individual quaternionic elliptic coefficient With G(q) = q̄/|q|⁴ , spatial derivative ∂ₓ in the i direction, and the cubic lattice L₀ , E_((3,0,0))(L₀) = ∑_(λ ≠ 0)∂ₓ³G(λ) = 192 i L(η(2τ)¹²,5) ≠ 0. For the elliptic function ℘_(L₀,1) of E-C1, the coefficient of x² in the real Taylor expansion of its regular part ℘_(L₀,1) − G₁ at zero is 96iL(f,5) . Differentiate the i component − x/N² of G three times. It gives (12N² − 144x²N + 192x⁴)/(N⁵). The real, j , and k components have a coordinate of odd parity and vanish after summation over the sign-symmetric lattice. Absolute convergence justifies these cancellations and coordinate permutations. Average the displayed numerator over the four coordinate positions; its lattice sum is unchanged, while its value becomes 12N² − 36N² + 48(t⁴ + x⁴ + y⁴ + z⁴) = 48H₄. TH4 therefore gives E_((3,0,0)) = 48i ⋅ 4L(f,5) . The Mellin identity L(f,5) = ((2π)⁵)/(Γ (5))∫₀^(∞)f(it)t⁴dt follows by the same absolute integration argument as TH1 (the harmonic coefficient sum converges at five). Every factor of η(2it)¹² is positive for t > 0 , so this value is strictly positive. Finally N1 with μ = (2,0,0) gives the second derivative of the regular part. Division by 2 ! gives its ordinary Taylor coefficient.

title: Harmonic theta series and special L-values
heading: Harmonic theta series and Mellin integration
text: Harmonic theta series and Mellin integration Let L ⊂ ℝ⁴ be a full Euclidean lattice, H a scalar homogeneous harmonic polynomial of even degree ℓ > 0 , and N(x) = |x|² . In this article, L^(∗) denotes the Euclidean dual lattice. For an even integral lattice put Q = N/2 and D = L^(∗)/L . In this case μ ranges over D , and L + μ denotes the corresponding coset in L^(∗) . Definition TH-D1. Harmonic Theta Functions The harmonic theta function is θ_(L,H)(it) = ∑_(λ ∈ L)H(λ)e^(− πtN(λ)) (t > 0). If the Euclidean bilinear form is integral on L and N(λ) is even for every λ ∈ L , the coset theta functions are Θ_(μ)(τ) = ∑_(λ ∈ L + μ)H(λ)e^(2πiτQ(λ)), Θ_(L,H) = Θ₀, Im τ > 0. Since Q is integral on L , the zero component has integral exponents; for Θ_(L,H) = ∑_(m ≥ 1)aₘe^(2πimτ) put L(Θ_(L,H),s) = ∑_(m ≥ 1)aₘm^(− s) wherever absolutely convergent. Theorem TH1. A convergent Mellin formula for each elliptic coefficient Let ν ∈ ℕ₀³ have odd order r ≥ 3 , and let H be any real component of the numerator H_(ν) . For every full Euclidean lattice L , E_(ν,H)(L) : = ∑_(λ ≠ 0)(H(λ))/(N(λ)^(r + 2)) = (π^(r + 2))/(Γ (r + 2))∫₀^(∞)t^(r + 1)θ_(L,H)(it) dt. Both the lattice sum and the interchange of summation and integration are absolutely convergent. Corollary TH3. Critical values with all normalizing factors fixed Under TH1's hypotheses, if L is even integral, then E_(ν,H)(L) = 2^(− (r + 2))L(Θ_(L,H),r + 2). The theta form has weight k = r + 3 , and the evaluation point is k − 1 . In particular the first potentially nonzero coefficients, of order r = 3 , evaluate weight-six cusp forms at s = 5 .

title: Harmonic theta series and special L-values
heading: The cubic lattice and a weight-six newform
text: The cubic lattice and a weight-six newform Let L₀ = ℤ + ℤi + ℤj + ℤk and put H₄(t,x,y,z) = t⁴ + x⁴ + y⁴ + z⁴ − (1)/(2)(t² + x² + y² + z²)². In this example the Fourier exponent uses Q₀(m) = |m|² , rather than N/2 : ϑ(τ) = ∑_(m ∈ ℤ⁴)H₄(m)e^(2πiτ|m|²), f(τ) = η(2τ)¹². Here u = e^(2πiτ) and η(τ) = u^(1/24)∏_(n ≥ 1)(1 − uⁿ) . Expanding the product gives f(τ) = u∏_(n ≥ 1)(1 − u²ⁿ)¹² = u − 12u³ + 54u⁵ − 88u⁷ − 99u⁹ + ⋯. For this Fourier convention L(f,s) = ∑_(m ≥ 1)aₘm^(− s) when f = ∑ aₘu^(m) . Theorem TH4. The exact harmonic theta identity [2, Chs. 5, 7, 14]; [4, Thms. 1.64–1.65]; [1, Thms. 2.4–2.5, p. 835] One has ϑ(τ) = 4η(2τ)¹², ∑_(m ∈ ℤ⁴ ∖ {0})(H₄(m))/(|m|¹⁰) = 4L(f,5). The normalized eta product f is the unique newform in S₆(Γ₀(4)) , with trivial character. Theorem TH5. An individual quaternionic elliptic coefficient With G(q) = q̄/|q|⁴ , spatial derivative ∂ₓ in the i direction, and the cubic lattice L₀ , E_((3,0,0))(L₀) = ∑_(λ ≠ 0)∂ₓ³G(λ) = 192 i L(η(2τ)¹²,5) ≠ 0. For the elliptic function ℘_(L₀,1) of E-C1, the coefficient of x² in the real Taylor expansion of its regular part ℘_(L₀,1) − G₁ at zero is 96iL(f,5) .

title: Harmonic theta series and special L-values
heading: How the representations fit together
text: How the representations fit together Discussion Object varied Group Result established here A regular function on the ball, with its point moved by Möbius transformations Sp(1,1) Discrete series for compatible spinors; the Hardy limit for one quaternionic value. The lattice in a kernel-derivative sum SL₄(ℝ) An irreducible module of Eisenstein functions. The modular variable of the cubic harmonic theta form GL₂ , or the classical modular group TH4–TH6 identify a weight-six newform and its critical value. The theta and Mellin formulas provide the stated numerical bridge. An equivalence or functorial correspondence between the first two representations has not been established. An arbitrary lattice theta form need not be an eigenform and may vanish; the cubic example succeeds because its cusp space has dimension one. Its newform data also agree with [3, 4.6.a].

title: Harmonic theta series and special L-values
heading: Questions opened by the example
text: Questions opened by the example Discussion Which other arithmetic lattices and individual quaternionic coefficients select a single newform? Can lattice symmetries predict vanishing or isolate Hecke constituents? What algebraic periods normalize the resulting critical values, and how do these values interact with quaternionic multiplication? These questions remain open here. At derivative order r = 1 , the predicted theta weight is four and the evaluation point is three. TH1 does not apply: the original lattice sum is at the boundary of absolute convergence. Cuspidality still makes the theta Mellin integral meaningful on an even integral lattice, but comparison with a specified regularization or with elliptic quasi-periods needs a separate proof.

title: Regular functions and differential forms
heading: Overview
text: Expository Closed mixed-regular pairings, conformal pullbacks, and the hypotheses needed for automorphic quotient questions. Regular functions and differential forms Discussion Regular functions produce closed three-forms through a left/right pairing. The local identities and their conformal factors can be proved explicitly. A separate linear two-form construction gives flat coefficients and injective cohomology maps; the bilinear pairings below have their own quotient questions.

title: Regular functions and differential forms
heading: Theorem DF1 · The mixed regular closed three-form
text: DF1 Theorem DF1. The mixed regular closed three-form [2, §4, eq. (4.1)] For C¹ quaternion-valued scalar functions u,f , d(uΩ f) = ((Dᵣu)f + u(Dₗf))dv, Dᵣu = uₜ + uₓi + u_(y)j + u_(z)k. If f,g are left Fueter-regular on U , then g^(∗) is right regular on Ū , and g^(∗)Ω f is closed on U ∩ Ū . The same identity and conclusion hold entrywise for rows f,g , producing a matrix of three-forms. Expand the exterior products in the specified orientation. The four terms of du ∧ Ω give (Dᵣu)dv , while Ω ∧ df = − (Dₗf)dv . Since deg Ω = 3 , the Leibniz rule supplies another minus sign in d(uΩ f) , proving the formula with a plus between the two derivatives. For g^(∗)(t,x,y,z) = overline(g(t, − x, − y, − z)) , differentiate the reflection. Conjugating Dₗg reverses quaternion multiplication and changes i,j,k to their negatives. The result is exactly Dᵣg^(∗) = (Dₗg)^(∗) , hence zero. Apply the identity with u = g^(∗) , entry by entry for rows.

title: Regular functions and differential forms
heading: Proposition DF2 · Nonzero pairs and exactness on the ball
text: DF2 Proposition DF2. Nonzero pairs and exactness on the ball [1, §§8, 15] If f,g are nonzero left-regular rows on the connected ball B , the matrix-valued form g^(∗)Ω f is not identically zero. Nevertheless every component is exact on B . Choose a nonzero component of g^(∗) . It is nonzero on some open set. If the matrix form vanished identically, its dx ∧ dy ∧ dz coefficient would force that component multiplied by each component of f to be zero there. Quaternions have no zero divisors, so f vanishes on the open set. Regular functions are harmonic by D̄ₗDₗ = Δ , hence real analytic; unique continuation would force f = 0 on the ball, a contradiction. Exactness follows from DF1 and the Poincaré lemma on a contractible ball, applied to each real component. Nonvanishing as a differential form is therefore distinct from nonvanishing of a cohomology class.

title: Regular functions and differential forms
heading: Proposition DF3 · The one-, two-, and three-form pullbacks
text: DF3 Proposition DF3. The one-, two-, and three-form pullbacks One has s(q^(′)) = s(q)/r² , |A| = r^(− 1) , and γ^(∗)dq = A dq J^(− 1), γ^(∗)(dq̄ ∧ dq) = r^(− 2)J̄^(− 1)(dq̄ ∧ dq)J^(− 1), γ^(∗)Ω = r^(− 4)AΩ J^(− 1). The relations defining Sp(1,1) give |cq + d|² − |aq + b|² = 1 − |q|² . They prove the formula for s(q^(′)) . Differentiation in the correct quaternion order gives dq^(′) = (a − q^(′)c)dqJ^(− 1). Using the same group relations, a − q^(′)c = (ā + qb̄)^(− 1) = A and |ā + qb̄| = |J| , yielding the first pullback and the norm of A . Conjugate it to get dq̄^(′) = J̄^(− 1)dq̄Ā . The middle product ĀA = r^(− 2) proves the second formula. The derivative is an orientation-preserving similarity of length factor r^(− 2) . For such a similarity in dimension four, pullback of the Hodge star on a one-form is its Hodge star after pullback multiplied by the square of the length factor. Apply this to dq to get the third formula. Left and right constant quaternion multiplication commute with the Hodge star on the differential-form part.

title: Regular functions and differential forms
heading: Proposition DF4 · Covariance with the scalar weights accounted for
text: DF4 Proposition DF4. Covariance with the scalar weights accounted for Fix n ≥ 1 , put C(u) = S_(n − 1)(ι(u))^(t) , and let f,g be quaternionic rows of length n . For an element γ suppose f(γq) = r²Jf(q)C(J), g^(∗)(γq) = r²C(a + bq̄)^(∗)g^(∗)(q)A^(− 1). Then the matrix-valued forms η = s²g^(∗)dqf, ω = g^(∗)Ω f satisfy γ^(∗)η = C(a + bq̄)^(∗)ηC(J), γ^(∗)ω = C(a + bq̄)^(∗)ωC(J). Separately, if both f and g obey the unreflected row law h(γq) = r²Jh(q)C(J) , then θ = s ḡ^(,t)(dq̄ ∧ dq)f, γ^(∗)θ = C(J)^(∗)θC(J). If f,g are regular, ω is closed. Insert the two assumed row laws and DF3. The raw product g^(∗)dqf picks up the scalar r⁴ : the adjacent A^(− 1)A and J^(− 1)J cancel. Multiplication by s(q^(′))² = s(q)²/r⁴ removes it. The raw three-form has the additional r^(− 4) from DF3 and needs no scalar correction. The remaining matrix factors have exactly the displayed order. For the second assertion, conjugate transpose of the unreflected law gives overline(g(γq))^(,t) = r²C(J)^(∗)ḡ(q)^(t)J̄ . DF3 then cancels J̄J̄^(− 1) and J^(− 1)J , leaving the scalar r² . The factor s(q^(′)) = s(q)/r² cancels it. Closedness of ω is DF1. These computations are conditional on the stated transformation laws; they do not construct automorphic functions or a flat coefficient system.

title: Regular functions and differential forms
heading: Proposition DF5 · Reflection changes the subgroup
text: DF5 Proposition DF5. Reflection changes the subgroup Let W = (0, 1; 1, 0) , γ^(†) = WγW and Γ^(†) = WΓ W . Then γ^(†)q = overline(γq̄). If g obeys the unreflected row law for Γ^(†) , its g^(∗) obeys the reflected law of DF4 for Γ . In particular a same-subgroup pairing is available under the additional hypothesis Γ^(†) = Γ . Otherwise one may pair the two indicated subgroups or restrict both to their intersection. The block relations in γ^(∗)diag (1, − 1)γ = diag (1, − 1) and its inverse imply (dq + c)(bq + a)^(− 1) = (qc̄ + d̄)^(− 1)(qā + b̄), which is the asserted reflected fractional transformation. Also W normalizes the group because it negates the preserved diagonal form. For γ ∈ Γ apply the automorphy law for g at q̄ with element γ^(†) . Its denominator is bq̄ + a , of norm r . Conjugate and transpose the resulting row identity. The rightmost scalar becomes overline(a + bq̄) = ā + qb̄ = A^(− 1) , and the leftmost matrix becomes C(a + bq̄)^(∗) . The result is precisely the assumed reflected law in DF4. This establishes both the formula and the subgroup qualification.

title: Regular functions and differential forms
heading: Proposition DF6 · Full-ball Hilbert vectors are not automorphic sections
text: DF6 Proposition DF6. Full-ball Hilbert vectors are not automorphic sections Let n ≥ 2 , and let Γ ⊂ Sp(1,1) be an infinite discrete subgroup. The full-ball Hilbert space ℋₙ has no nonzero Γ -fixed vectors. A fixed vector has a Γ -invariant norm density ‖h(q)‖²s^(n − 2)dv by the pointwise change-of-variables calculation in DS2. If h ≠ 0 , choose a small open set on which the norm integral is positive, away from nontrivial stabilizers of the effective action. Proper discontinuity gives a smaller open set with pairwise disjoint translates indexed by the quotient of Γ by its finite ineffective center. One can choose this set where h ≠ 0 since that is an open set. Every translate has the same positive integral. There are infinitely many translates, contradicting the finite full-ball norm. Finite stabilizers do not affect the argument.

title: Regular functions and differential forms
heading: A closed pairing of regular functions
text: A closed pairing of regular functions Use q = t + ix + jy + kz and dv = dt ∧ dx ∧ dy ∧ dz . The Euclidean Hodge star acts on the real differential-form part, leaving quaternion coefficients in place. Applying the Euclidean Hodge star to each coordinate one-form gives Ω = ∗ dq = dx ∧ dy ∧ dz − i dt ∧ dy ∧ dz + j dt ∧ dx ∧ dz − k dt ∧ dx ∧ dy. Products of quaternion-valued forms use exterior multiplication and the displayed coefficient order. For a quaternion-valued row g , write g^(∗)(q) = overline(g(q̄))^(,t) for its reflected conjugate-transpose column. In contrast, overline(g(q))^(,t) involves no argument reflection. For a constant matrix, a superscript ∗ always means ordinary conjugate transpose. Theorem DF1. The mixed regular closed three-form [2, §4, eq. (4.1)] For C¹ quaternion-valued scalar functions u,f , d(uΩ f) = ((Dᵣu)f + u(Dₗf))dv, Dᵣu = uₜ + uₓi + u_(y)j + u_(z)k. If f,g are left Fueter-regular on U , then g^(∗) is right regular on Ū , and g^(∗)Ω f is closed on U ∩ Ū . The same identity and conclusion hold entrywise for rows f,g , producing a matrix of three-forms. Proposition DF2. Nonzero pairs and exactness on the ball [1, §§8, 15] If f,g are nonzero left-regular rows on the connected ball B , the matrix-valued form g^(∗)Ω f is not identically zero. Nevertheless every component is exact on B .

title: Regular functions and differential forms
heading: Pullback under ball automorphisms
text: Pullback under ball automorphisms Here γ = (a, b; c, d) ∈ Sp(1,1) itself acts by q^(′) = γq = (aq + b)(cq + d)^(− 1) . Put J = cq + d, r = |J|, A = (ā + qb̄)^(− 1), s = 1 − |q|². This differs from the inverse-element convention used to define a left action on functions; the pullback below is always along q ↦ γq . Proposition DF3. The one-, two-, and three-form pullbacks One has s(q^(′)) = s(q)/r² , |A| = r^(− 1) , and γ^(∗)dq = A dq J^(− 1), γ^(∗)(dq̄ ∧ dq) = r^(− 2)J̄^(− 1)(dq̄ ∧ dq)J^(− 1), γ^(∗)Ω = r^(− 4)AΩ J^(− 1).

title: Regular functions and differential forms
heading: Conditional automorphic pairings
text: Conditional automorphic pairings Proposition DF4. Covariance with the scalar weights accounted for Fix n ≥ 1 , put C(u) = S_(n − 1)(ι(u))^(t) , and let f,g be quaternionic rows of length n . For an element γ suppose f(γq) = r²Jf(q)C(J), g^(∗)(γq) = r²C(a + bq̄)^(∗)g^(∗)(q)A^(− 1). Then the matrix-valued forms η = s²g^(∗)dqf, ω = g^(∗)Ω f satisfy γ^(∗)η = C(a + bq̄)^(∗)ηC(J), γ^(∗)ω = C(a + bq̄)^(∗)ωC(J). Separately, if both f and g obey the unreflected row law h(γq) = r²Jh(q)C(J) , then θ = s ḡ^(,t)(dq̄ ∧ dq)f, γ^(∗)θ = C(J)^(∗)θC(J). If f,g are regular, ω is closed. The proposition asserts closedness for ω ; the covariance identities for η and θ do not establish their closedness. Proposition DF5. Reflection changes the subgroup Let W = (0, 1; 1, 0) , γ^(†) = WγW and Γ^(†) = WΓ W . Then γ^(†)q = overline(γq̄). If g obeys the unreflected row law for Γ^(†) , its g^(∗) obeys the reflected law of DF4 for Γ . In particular a same-subgroup pairing is available under the additional hypothesis Γ^(†) = Γ . Otherwise one may pair the two indicated subgroups or restrict both to their intersection.

title: Regular functions and differential forms
heading: Passing from the ball to a quotient
text: Passing from the ball to a quotient Proposition DF6. Full-ball Hilbert vectors are not automorphic sections Let n ≥ 2 , and let Γ ⊂ Sp(1,1) be an infinite discrete subgroup. The full-ball Hilbert space ℋₙ has no nonzero Γ -fixed vectors. Discussion A quotient construction needs spaces of sections on Γ \ B , automorphic realizations on Γ \ G , or appropriate distribution vectors. DF6 excludes identifying these with ordinary fixed vectors in the full-ball Hilbert space. DF1–DF5 supply local identities and conditional covariance for the bilinear pairings. Their further period theory still requires a specified flat coefficient bundle and a nonzero quotient class. The separate linear construction AC3–AC7 now supplies those steps for a different two-form associated to a single regular automorphic spinor. A varying transition matrix does not itself define a flat local system, and componentwise closedness in one chart does not settle those questions. This remains a research direction, linked to period relations. For the underlying left/right quaternionic analysis see [2]. The representation norm used here is developed in the discrete-series article.

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Overview
text: Research From regular spinors to closed two-forms with flat coefficients, periods, and injective cohomology maps. Regular automorphic forms and cohomology Discussion A regular automorphic spinor on the quaternionic ball determines a closed two-form with values in a finite-dimensional flat bundle. On a compact quotient, a positive pairing proves that a nonzero spinor gives a nonzero cohomology class. At the lowest weight, the construction is simply the correspondence with anti-self-dual harmonic two-forms. The classical model is [7]: a holomorphic automorphic form of weight k gives the closed one-form f(z)(z,1)^(⊙ (k − 2))dz with coefficients in Sym^(k − 2) ℂ² . Here the base has real dimension four, the differential form has degree two, and the coefficient representation uses ℂ⁴ . The formulas below prove this quaternionic construction directly. Discussion The definitions on this page use ball coordinates. For cusp calculations, the half-space formulation gives the group, lift and constant terms directly; CP-H1 states the exact coordinate and coefficient conversion.

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Definition AC-D1 · Regular Automorphic Spinors
text: AC-D1 Definition AC-D1. Regular Automorphic Spinors For n ≥ 1 , a regular automorphic spinor of weight n is a smooth f : B → Vₙ satisfying, for every q ∈ B and γ ∈ Γ , , Dₗ(f_(X) − j_(ℍ)f_(Y)) = 0, f(γq) = r²τₙ(j)f(q)., (1)

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Proposition AC1 · Bundle interpretation and automorphic lift
text: AC1 Proposition AC1. Bundle interpretation and automorphic lift The factor r²τₙ(j) is a cocycle and defines a rank- n + 1 vector bundle on Γ \ B . For g = (a, b; c, d) , the lift , F_(f)(g) = |d|^(− 2)τₙ(ι(d)^(− 1))f(g0), (3) is left Γ -invariant and satisfies F_(f)(gk) = τₙ(ι(k_(R))^(− 1))F_(f)(g) for k = diag (k_(L),k_(R)) ∈ K . At σ(q) = s^(− 1/2)(1, q; q̄, 1) one has F_(f)(σ(q)) = s^((n + 2)/2)f(q) . The density defining ‖f‖_(Γ ,n) is Γ -invariant. The denominator satisfies J(g₁g₂,q) = J(g₁,g₂q)J(g₂,q) . Quaternion norm multiplicativity and the representation law for τₙ prove the cocycle identity and left invariance of (3). Right multiplication by k replaces d by dk_(R) and leaves g0 fixed, proving right equivariance. Substitution of d = s^(− 1/2) proves the section formula. Finally, τₙ(j) multiplies norms by rⁿ , s(γq) = s/r² , and the real Jacobian is r^(− 8) . Thus the density changes by r^(2n + 4)r^(− 2n + 4)r^(− 8) = 1 .

The moving spinor subbundle inside the flat bundle For every γ ∈ G , , Z(γq)j = R(γ)Z(q), Z(q)^(∗)HZ(q) = − sI₂., (4) For f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) , sZₙf is a section of ℰₙ , lying in its moving rank- n + 1 subbundle Zₙ(Vₙ) . title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Theorem AC3 · Regularity becomes closedness with flat coefficients
text: AC3 Theorem AC3. Regularity becomes closedness with flat coefficients For every smooth f : B → Vₙ , n ≥ 2 , , dΩ_(f) = 0 ⟺ Dₗ(f_(X) − j_(ℍ)f_(Y)) = 0., (6) The map f ↦ Ω_(f) is pointwise injective and Ω_(f) is anti-self-dual in the orientation dt ∧ dx ∧ dy ∧ dz . If f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) , then , γ^(∗)Ω_(f) = Rₘ(γ)Ω_(f)., (7) Consequently Ω_(f) descends to a closed two-form with values in the flat bundle ℰₘ . Set ω₁ = dt ∧ dx − dy ∧ dz, ω₂ = dt ∧ dy + dx ∧ dz, ω₃ = dt ∧ dz − dx ∧ dy. All three are anti-self-dual. Direct multiplication gives , S = ( − 2ω₂ + 2iω₃, − 2iω₁; − 2iω₁, − 2ω₂ − 2iω₃)., (8) Thus Φₙ , and hence Ω_(f) , is anti-self-dual. Its vanishing implies f_(XY) = 0 , f_(XX) + f_(YY) = 0 , and f_(XX) − f_(YY) = 0 . All second derivatives vanish, so a homogeneous polynomial of degree n ≥ 2 must be zero. Injectivity of Zₘ completes the pointwise assertion. For closedness, first take n = 2 and f = aX² + 2bXY + cY² . The four regularity residuals in (2), after division by 2 , are E₁, = aₜ + iaₓ + b_(y) + ib_(z),, E₂, = − a_(y) + ia_(z) + bₜ − ibₓ,; E₃, = bₜ + ibₓ + c_(y) + ic_(z),, E₄, = − b_(y) + ib_(z) + cₜ − icₓ. In the ordered basis (dt ∧ dx ∧ dy,dt ∧ dx ∧ dz,dt ∧ dy ∧ dz,dx ∧ dy ∧ dz) the coefficients of dΦ₂(f) are ( − 2iE₁ + 2iE₄, − 2E₁ − 2E₄, 2iE₂ + 2iE₃, − 2E₂ + 2E₃). This invertible change of variables proves equivalence with regularity. For general n , apply all auxiliary derivatives of total order n − 2 . They commute with base differentiation, and ∂^(α)Φₙ(f) = (2)/(n(n − 1))Φ₂(∂^(α)f). The quadratic case proves dΦₙ(f) = 0 if and only if every such derivative of the regularity residual vanishes. That residual is homogeneous of degree n − 1 , so this is equivalent to its vanishing. It remains to differentiate the moving inclusion Zₘ . The required identity is algebraic, not a flatness assumption. For each row α = 1,2 of dQ , expansion of (8) gives , dQ_(α1) ∧ S₁₁, = 0,, dQ_(α2) ∧ S₂₂, = 0,; dQ_(α2) ∧ S₁₁ + 2dQ_(α1) ∧ S₁₂, = 0,, dQ_(α1) ∧ S₂₂ + 2dQ_(α2) ∧ S₁₂, = 0., (9) Equivalently, dQ_(α(i) ∧ Sⱼₖ₎ = 0 . Every term of dZₘ ∧ Φₙ(f) contracts this identity with three symmetric indices of f . Thus dZₘ ∧ Φₙ(f) = 0 for every f , and dΩ_(f) = Zₘ dΦₙ(f). Because Zₘ is injective, this proves (6). For covariance, DF3 gives γ^(∗)(dQ^(∗) ∧ dQ) = r^(− 4)j(dQ^(∗) ∧ dQ)j^(− 1). Since det j = r² and ϵj = (det j)j^(− t)ϵ , it follows that , γ^(∗)S = r^(− 2)j^(− t)Sj^(− 1)., (10) Contract this with f(γq) = r²j^(⊙ n)f(q) . The two contracted tensor factors and the scalar weights cancel, leaving γ^(∗)Φₙ(f) = τₘ(j)Φₙ(f). Finally apply (4) in degree m to obtain (7). The Hodge star on two-forms in dimension four is conformally invariant, so the same anti-self-duality holds for the ball's hyperbolic metric.

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Theorem AC4 · The cohomology map and its positivity on compact quotients
text: AC4 Theorem AC4. The cohomology map and its positivity on compact quotients [1, §§8, 15] For n ≥ 2 , (5) defines a linear map , ℳₙ(Γ ) ⟶ H_(dR)²(Γ \ B,ℰ_(n − 2)) ≃ H²(Γ ,E_(n − 2)), f ⟼ [Ω_(f)]., (11) If Γ \ B is compact, this map is injective. More precisely, let m = n − 2 and let P_(Hₘ)(α,β) denote the wedge pairing which applies Hₘ conjugate-linearly to coefficients of α and linearly to coefficients of β . Then , P_(Hₘ)(Ω_(f),Ω_(f)) = 16( − 1)^(m + 1)s^(m)‖f(q)‖ₙ² dv., (12) AC3 establishes descent and closedness. The ball is contractible and Γ acts freely and properly, so its quotient is a classifying space for Γ . The de Rham theorem with local coefficients gives the displayed identification. The induced Hermitian form on Zₘ(Vₘ) is ( − s)^(m) times the standard positive form, by (4). With Euclidean norms on two-forms, , ‖Φₙ(f)‖² = 16‖f‖ₙ²., (13) To verify the constant, the contraction in (5) is equivariant for SU(2) acting on Vₙ , Vₘ , and the anti-self-dual forms. Its induced Hermitian form on the irreducible Vₙ is a scalar multiple of the standard one. On f = Xⁿ , its image is X^(m)S₁₁ ; (8) and ‖ωᵢ‖² = 2 give ‖S₁₁‖² = 16 . Anti-self-duality now converts the norm identity into (12). If Ω_(f) = d_(∇)β on a compact quotient, parallelness of Hₘ and d_(∇)Ω_(f) = 0 imply P_(Hₘ)(Ω_(f),Ω_(f)) = dP_(Hₘ)(β,Ω_(f)). Its integral is zero by Stokes. But (12) has a fixed sign and is strictly nonzero after integration when f ≠ 0 . Therefore [Ω_(f)] ≠ 0 .

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Proposition AC5 · A group cocycle from triangle periods
text: AC5 Proposition AC5. A group cocycle from triangle periods [2, Thm. I.7.5, §§III.1, III.8] Fix q₀ ∈ B . For f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) define, in the constant flat trivialization on B , c_(f)(γ₁,γ₂) = ∫_([q₀,γ₁q₀,γ₁γ₂q₀])Ω_(f), where brackets denote oriented geodesically straightened simplices. This is an E_(n − 2) -valued group two-cocycle representing (11). Changing q₀ changes it by a coboundary. The four faces of the straightened tetrahedron with vertices q₀,γ₁q₀,γ₁γ₂q₀,γ₁γ₂γ₃q₀ give Rₘ(γ₁)c_(f)(γ₂,γ₃) − c_(f)(γ₁γ₂,γ₃) + c_(f)(γ₁,γ₂γ₃) − c_(f)(γ₁,γ₂) = 0. The first face uses (7); the sum is zero by Stokes and closedness. Integrating over the prism homotopy between two choices of vertices proves the coboundary assertion. This is the simplex integration realization of the de Rham comparison in AC4.

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Theorem AC6 · Harmonic representatives in reduced square-integrable cohomology
text: AC6 Theorem AC6. Harmonic representatives in reduced square-integrable cohomology [3]; [6, §2.2, pp. 5–6] Give Γ \ B the complete hyperbolic metric s^(− 2)|dq|² . On E , let h_(q) be − H on the negative plane Z(q)ℂ² and + H on its H -orthogonal complement. Let hₘ be the induced positive metric on Eₘ . These metrics descend to ℰₘ . For n ≥ 2 and f ∈ ℳₙ²(Γ ) , Ω_(f) is a square-integrable harmonic form for the flat differential and the metric hₘ , and ‖Ω_(f)‖_(L²(hₘ))² = 16‖f‖_(Γ ,n)². Consequently f ↦ [Ω_(f)] is injective into reduced L² cohomology H̄₍₂₎²(Γ \ B,ℰₘ,hₘ) . The negative-plane splitting is G -equivariant by (4), proving descent. If one argument lies in Zₘ(Vₘ) , the coefficient pairings satisfy hₘ = ( − 1)^(m)Hₘ : in the symmetric tensor decomposition, the all-negative summand is orthogonal to every summand containing a positive factor. Thus (13), Z^(∗)HZ = − sI , and conformal invariance of the product of the squared two-form norm with volume prove the norm identity. For every compactly supported one-form β , the hₘ inner product of d_(∇)β with Ω_(f) is, up to a constant sign, the integral of P_(Hₘ)(d_(∇)β,Ω_(f)) . Closedness and parallelness of Hₘ make this integral zero by Stokes. Therefore d_(∇)^(∗)Ω_(f) = 0 weakly, hence smoothly. Also d_(∇)Ω_(f) = 0 . On this complete manifold compactly supported forms are a core for the closed differential, using cutoffs with gradients tending uniformly to zero. Hence Ω_(f) is orthogonal to the closure of exact L² forms. A nonzero such harmonic form gives a nonzero reduced cohomology class.

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Corollary AC7 · Arithmetic cusp forms give ordinary cohomology classes
text: AC7 Corollary AC7. Arithmetic cusp forms give ordinary cohomology classes [4, §1.2] Suppose Γ is a torsion-free arithmetic lattice in a rational form of Sp(1,1) of rational rank one. Let Sₙ(Γ ) consist of the regular automorphic spinors in AC-D1 whose lifts (3) have scalar components in the smooth cuspidal L² automorphic space, satisfying the quantified moderate-growth and central-finiteness conditions (MG) and (ZF) of CP-D0. For n ≥ 2 , the map Sₙ(Γ ) ⟶ H²(Γ ,E_(n − 2)), f ⟼ [Ω_(f)] is injective, and its image lies in the cuspidal subspace defined by the comparison map in cuspidal cohomology. In the homogeneous K -frame, the map (5) is a fixed K -equivariant linear map from Vₙ to Eₘ ⊗ Λ²p^(∗) . This follows either from (7) for G or by evaluating the construction at q = 0 and translating. The flat-coefficient homogeneous frame uses Rₘ(g) ; its moving-frame differential is exactly the usual relative Lie algebra differential on coefficients twisted by Eₘ . Thus the form determined by F_(f) belongs to the cuspidal relative Lie algebra cochain complex. It is closed by AC3. If it were a coboundary in that complex, its primitive would give a square-integrable one-form on the quotient: the homogeneous-frame coefficient norm is fixed and positive, and all scalar coefficients of the primitive are smooth vectors in L_(cusp)² . This contradicts AC6 for f ≠ 0 . The cuspidal class is therefore nonzero. The external theorem says the natural map from this finite-coefficient cuspidal cohomology into ordinary cohomology is injective. Apply it to obtain the conclusion.

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Corollary AC8 · Weight two is the anti-self-dual Maxwell model
text: AC8 Corollary AC8. Weight two is the anti-self-dual Maxwell model For n = 2 the coefficient bundle is trivial. The map , f = aX² + 2bXY + cY² ⟼ Ω_(f) = − 4ib ω₁ − 2(a + c) ω₂ + 2i(a − c) ω₃, (14) is a bijection from ℳ₂(Γ ) to the smooth complex closed anti-self-dual two-forms on Γ \ B . On a compact quotient these are the anti-self-dual harmonic forms and inject into ordinary H² . On a complete noncompact quotient the finite-norm correspondence is with square-integrable anti-self-dual harmonic two-forms. For n = 2 , m = 0 and Z₀ = 1 , so (14) is (5) expanded using (8). It is an invertible linear map onto the three-dimensional complex space of anti-self-dual two-forms at each point. AC3 makes closedness equivalent to regularity. Covariance, applied to the inverse pointwise map, makes invariance of the two-form equivalent to the automorphy law for f . For an anti-self-dual form, closedness implies coclosedness since ∗ Ω = − Ω . On compact manifolds harmonic forms are closed and coclosed; on complete manifolds the same holds for L² harmonic forms in the Hilbert-complex sense. AC4 and AC6 give the cohomology and norm assertions.

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Regular automorphic spinors
text: Regular automorphic spinors Let B = {q = t + ix + jy + kz : |q| < 1} , s = 1 − |q|² , and Q(q) = ι(q) = (t + ix, y + iz; − y + iz, t − ix), Vₙ = Symⁿ ℂ² = ℂ[X,Y]ₙ. If M = (a, b; c, d) , the symmetric-power action is τₙ(M)p(X,Y) = p(aX + cY,bX + dY). Let Γ be a discrete torsion-free subgroup of G = Sp(1,1) . For γ = (a, b; c, d) put γq = (aq + b)(cq + d)^(− 1), J = cq + d, j = ι(J), r = |J|. The integer n is positive. We use Dₗ = ∂ₜ + i∂ₓ + j_(ℍ)∂_(y) + k∂_(z), where j_(ℍ) is the quaternion unit, distinct from the matrix j ; subscripts X,Y denote derivatives in the polynomial variables. Definition AC-D1. Regular Automorphic Spinors For n ≥ 1 , a regular automorphic spinor of weight n is a smooth f : B → Vₙ satisfying, for every q ∈ B and γ ∈ Γ , , Dₗ(f_(X) − j_(ℍ)f_(Y)) = 0, f(γq) = r²τₙ(j)f(q)., (1) Write ℳₙ(Γ ) for the vector space of regular automorphic spinors of weight n . Regularity is equivalent to , (∂ₜ + i∂ₓ, ∂_(y) + i∂_(z); − ∂_(y) + i∂_(z), ∂ₜ − i∂ₓ)(f_(X); f_(Y)) = 0., (2) Indeed, if A and B₀ are the two entries on the left of (2), expansion using ij_(ℍ) = k and j_(ℍ)i = − k gives Dₗ(f_(X) − j_(ℍ)f_(Y)) = A − j_(ℍ)B₀ . A quaternion of this form vanishes exactly when both complex entries vanish.

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Norms
text: Norms For f = ∑ cₐX^(n − a)Y^(a) , set ‖f‖ₙ² = ∑_(a = 0)ⁿ(|cₐ|²)/(((n)/(a))), ‖f‖_(Γ ,n)² = ∫_(ℱ)‖f(q)‖ₙ²s^(n − 2) dv, where ℱ is a fundamental domain and dv = dt dx dy dz . The finite-norm subspace is ℳₙ²(Γ ) . The invariance proved in AC1 makes the integral independent of the fundamental domain. Discussion The space ℳₙ imposes regularity and the transformation law. Growth, infinitesimal finiteness, and cuspidality are additional conditions, defined explicitly in CP-D0–CP-D1. Proposition AC1. Bundle interpretation and automorphic lift The factor r²τₙ(j) is a cocycle and defines a rank- n + 1 vector bundle on Γ \ B . For g = (a, b; c, d) , the lift , F_(f)(g) = |d|^(− 2)τₙ(ι(d)^(− 1))f(g0), (3) is left Γ -invariant and satisfies F_(f)(gk) = τₙ(ι(k_(R))^(− 1))F_(f)(g) for k = diag (k_(L),k_(R)) ∈ K . At σ(q) = s^(− 1/2)(1, q; q̄, 1) one has F_(f)(σ(q)) = s^((n + 2)/2)f(q) . The density defining ‖f‖_(Γ ,n) is Γ -invariant. Discussion For arithmetic Γ , the usual automorphic conditions can be imposed on the scalar components of F_(f) : moderate growth, finiteness under the center of the enveloping algebra, and, for cusp forms, vanishing of every constant term ∫_((Γ ∩ N_(P)) \ N_(P))F_(f)(ug) du = 0 for each proper rational parabolic P . Right K -finiteness follows from AC1. These are conditions on the automorphic lift; CP-D1 and CP1 give the precise definition and prove its equivalence with finite Petersson norm for regular automorphic spinors in the stated arithmetic setting. The arithmetic theorem below assumes the lift is a smooth vector in the cuspidal L² space, as well as an automorphic form in this sense.

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Embedding into a genuine flat bundle
text: Embedding into a genuine flat bundle Let E = ℂ⁴ , with the block representation R(g) = (ι(a), ι(b); ι(c), ι(d)), H = diag (I₂, − I₂). For ℓ ≥ 0 write E_(ℓ) = Sym^(ℓ) E , R_(ℓ) = Sym^(ℓ) R , and Z(q) = (Q(q); I₂), Z_(ℓ)(q) = Sym^(ℓ) Z(q). For ℓ ≥ 0 , let ℰ_(ℓ) be the flat bundle associated to R_(ℓ)|_(Γ) on Γ \ B : the quotient of B × E_(ℓ) by (q,v) ↦ (γq,R_(ℓ)(γ)v) , with connection induced by ordinary differentiation on B . The bundle has rank ((ℓ + 3)/(3)) . The Hermitian form H_(ℓ) is the symmetric tensor power of H , with the tensor-induced normalization. It is invariant because R(g)^(∗)HR(g) = H for g ∈ Sp(1,1) , and this identity passes to symmetric powers. The connection descends because the transition matrices R_(ℓ)(γ) are constant. The rank formula follows by counting the degree- ℓ monomials in four variables. Proposition AC2. The moving spinor subbundle inside the flat bundle For every γ ∈ G , , Z(γq)j = R(γ)Z(q), Z(q)^(∗)HZ(q) = − sI₂., (4) For f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) , sZₙf is a section of ℰₙ , lying in its moving rank- n + 1 subbundle Zₙ(Vₙ) . The map f ↦ sZₙf is injective. Discussion This already supplies the vector-bundle realization. The ambient bundle is flat, while its moving spinor subbundle need not be parallel. Differentiating sZₙf gives an exact flat-bundle-valued one-form. To obtain interesting periods, we instead use the following two-form.

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: The closed two-form
text: The closed two-form For n ≥ 2 , put m = n − 2 and ϵ = (0, 1; − 1, 0), S = ϵ(dQ^(∗) ∧ dQ). Here dQ^(∗) means the differential of the conjugate transpose. Matrix multiplication includes exterior multiplication of forms. The matrix S is symmetric by the explicit calculation (8) in the proof of AC3. Construction AC-C1. A Linear Two-Form with Symmetric-Power Coefficients For a smooth f : B → Vₙ , define , Φₙ(f) = (S₁₁f_(XX) + 2S₁₂f_(XY) + S₂₂f_(YY))/(n(n − 1)), Ω_(f) = ZₘΦₙ(f). , (5) Then Φₙ(f) is a Vₘ -valued two-form, and Ω_(f) takes values in Eₘ . Auxiliary variables represent symmetric tensors: Zₘ replaces each of their ℂ² tensor factors by its image under Z . Theorem AC3. Regularity becomes closedness with flat coefficients For every smooth f : B → Vₙ , n ≥ 2 , , dΩ_(f) = 0 ⟺ Dₗ(f_(X) − j_(ℍ)f_(Y)) = 0., (6) The map f ↦ Ω_(f) is pointwise injective and Ω_(f) is anti-self-dual in the orientation dt ∧ dx ∧ dy ∧ dz . If f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) , then , γ^(∗)Ω_(f) = Rₘ(γ)Ω_(f)., (7) Consequently Ω_(f) descends to a closed two-form with values in the flat bundle ℰₘ .

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Cohomology and periods
text: Cohomology and periods Theorem AC4. The cohomology map and its positivity on compact quotients [1, §§8, 15] For n ≥ 2 , (5) defines a linear map , ℳₙ(Γ ) ⟶ H_(dR)²(Γ \ B,ℰ_(n − 2)) ≃ H²(Γ ,E_(n − 2)), f ⟼ [Ω_(f)]., (11) If Γ \ B is compact, this map is injective. More precisely, let m = n − 2 and let P_(Hₘ)(α,β) denote the wedge pairing which applies Hₘ conjugate-linearly to coefficients of α and linearly to coefficients of β . Then , P_(Hₘ)(Ω_(f),Ω_(f)) = 16( − 1)^(m + 1)s^(m)‖f(q)‖ₙ² dv., (12) Proposition AC5. A group cocycle from triangle periods [2, Thm. I.7.5, §§III.1, III.8] Fix q₀ ∈ B . For f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) define, in the constant flat trivialization on B , c_(f)(γ₁,γ₂) = ∫_([q₀,γ₁q₀,γ₁γ₂q₀])Ω_(f), where brackets denote oriented geodesically straightened simplices. This is an E_(n − 2) -valued group two-cocycle representing (11). Changing q₀ changes it by a coboundary.

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: Square integrability and cusp forms
text: Square integrability and cusp forms Theorem AC6. Harmonic representatives in reduced square-integrable cohomology [3]; [6, §2.2, pp. 5–6] Give Γ \ B the complete hyperbolic metric s^(− 2)|dq|² . On E , let h_(q) be − H on the negative plane Z(q)ℂ² and + H on its H -orthogonal complement. Let hₘ be the induced positive metric on Eₘ . These metrics descend to ℰₘ . For n ≥ 2 and f ∈ ℳₙ²(Γ ) , Ω_(f) is a square-integrable harmonic form for the flat differential and the metric hₘ , and ‖Ω_(f)‖_(L²(hₘ))² = 16‖f‖_(Γ ,n)². Consequently f ↦ [Ω_(f)] is injective into reduced L² cohomology H̄₍₂₎²(Γ \ B,ℰₘ,hₘ) . Corollary AC7. Arithmetic cusp forms give ordinary cohomology classes [4, §1.2] Suppose Γ is a torsion-free arithmetic lattice in a rational form of Sp(1,1) of rational rank one. Let Sₙ(Γ ) consist of the regular automorphic spinors in AC-D1 whose lifts (3) have scalar components in the smooth cuspidal L² automorphic space, satisfying the quantified moderate-growth and central-finiteness conditions (MG) and (ZF) of CP-D0. For n ≥ 2 , the map Sₙ(Γ ) ⟶ H²(Γ ,E_(n − 2)), f ⟼ [Ω_(f)] is injective, and its image lies in the cuspidal subspace defined by the comparison map in cuspidal cohomology. Discussion For general noncuspidal forms on a noncompact quotient, AC4 still defines an ordinary cohomology class, and AC6 proves a nonzero reduced L² class when the norm is finite. These two facts alone do not prove injectivity into ordinary cohomology. AC7 supplies that step under its arithmetic cuspidal hypotheses. CP5 identifies the full parabolic image, using both chiralities and additional spectral inputs; it does not assert surjectivity onto all ordinary cohomology.

title: Regular automorphic forms and cohomology
heading: The lowest weight and the Maxwell equation
text: The lowest weight and the Maxwell equation Corollary AC8. Weight two is the anti-self-dual Maxwell model For n = 2 the coefficient bundle is trivial. The map , f = aX² + 2bXY + cY² ⟼ Ω_(f) = − 4ib ω₁ − 2(a + c) ω₂ + 2i(a − c) ω₃, (14) is a bijection from ℳ₂(Γ ) to the smooth complex closed anti-self-dual two-forms on Γ \ B . On a compact quotient these are the anti-self-dual harmonic forms and inject into ordinary H² . On a complete noncompact quotient the finite-norm correspondence is with square-integrable anti-self-dual harmonic two-forms. Example. A local seed The constant spinor f = X² gives Ω_(f) = − 2ω₂ + 2iω₃ . It is nonzero, closed, and anti-self-dual. This is a local seed on B ; it need not be automorphic for a specified lattice. The same periodization idea gives a Poincaré-series construction at weights n ≥ 5 . At weight two, compact quotients supply harmonic examples. Discussion. Further directions The construction starts at n = 2 . At n = 1 , the exponent n − 2 is negative, so it gives no finite-dimensional symmetric-power coefficient system for the Hardy limit. This is a limitation of this construction, not an impossibility theorem for other endpoint cohomology theories. [5, (1,1)] already places cohomological discrete series in degree two. The cuspidal correspondence now identifies (5) with the corresponding cohomological generator and supplies the opposite chirality. The Hecke comparison and algebraicity theorem supply a number-field structure on the sum of both chiralities and prove that simultaneous Hecke eigenvalues lie in a number field. The similitude extension constructs an integral coefficient lattice and proves algebraic-integrality for the specified Hecke semigroup. Specific arithmetic examples and triangle periods remain to develop from the available constructions. The bilinear three-forms in Regular functions and differential forms remain a separate construction.

title: Constructing regular automorphic forms
heading: Construction AS-C1 · Periodizing a constant regular spinor
text: AS-C1 Construction AS-C1. Periodizing a constant regular spinor Let Γ ⊂ G be discrete and torsion-free, n ≥ 5 , and v ∈ Vₙ . Write γ = (a_(γ), b_(γ); c_(γ), d_(γ)) . Define , P_(Γ ,n,v)(q) = ∑_(γ ∈ Γ)|c_(γ)q + d_(γ)|^(− 2)τₙ(ι((c_(γ)q + d_(γ))^(− 1)))v., (1)

title: Constructing regular automorphic forms
heading: Theorem AS1 · Convergence, regularity, and arithmetic cuspidality
text: AS1 Theorem AS1. Convergence, regularity, and arithmetic cuspidality [1, Lemma 4-2(i)] Under AS-C1's hypotheses, (1) converges absolutely, locally uniformly with every derivative, and defines an element of ℳₙ(Γ ) . If Γ is a congruence lattice in a rational form of G , its automorphic lift is cuspidal, square-integrable, and satisfies the usual automorphic growth and finiteness conditions. Thus (1) supplies regular cusp forms, possibly zero. For a nonzero quaternion J , the coefficient norm gives ‖ |J|^(− 2)τₙ(ι(J^(− 1)))v‖ₙ = |J|^(− (n + 2))‖v‖ₙ. The relation |d_(γ)|² − |c_(γ)|² = 1 implies, for |q| ≤ r < 1 , |c_(γ)q + d_(γ)| ≥ (1 − r)|d_(γ)|. For the hyperbolic metric s^(− 2)|dq|² , write t_(γ) = d(0,γ0) . Then |d_(γ)| = cosh t_(γ) . Discreteness and torsion-freeness give a separated orbit of 0 : the stabilizer is trivial, and every bounded displacement set contains finitely many group elements. Packing disjoint small balls around the orbit gives #{γ : t_(γ) ≤ T} = O(e^(6T)), since the radial volume density is a constant multiple of sinh³ (2t) dt . Consequently , ∑_(γ ∈ Γ)|d_(γ)|^(− (n + 2)) < ∞ (n > 4)., (2) This proves local uniform absolute convergence. For derivatives, factor cq + d = d(1 + d^(− 1)cq) . The quaternion d^(− 1)c lies in the unit ball. After taking out the factor |d|^(− (n + 2)) , every derivative of the summand is bounded uniformly for |q| ≤ r , independently of γ ; the inverse denominator stays away from zero. Equation (2) therefore proves convergence with every derivative. Each summand is the corrected translate πₙ(γ^(− 1))v , hence regular. The denominator cocycle J(γδ,q) = J(γ,δq)J(δ,q) and reindexing the sum give the required automorphy law. For cuspidality, set k_(n,v)(g) = |d_(g)|^(− 2)τₙ(ι(d_(g)^(− 1)))v. By the constant-vector matrix-coefficient identity in the discrete-series model, its scalar components are smooth, K -finite matrix coefficients and are finite under the center of the enveloping algebra. Their absolute values are bounded by a constant times (cosh t)^(− (n + 2)) . The Cartan integral ∫₀^(∞)(cosh t)^(− (n + 2))sinh³ (2t) dt is finite precisely for n > 4 . The lift of (1) is ∑_(γ)k_(n,v)(γg) . Muić's stated Poincaré-series theorem applies componentwise to these integrable matrix coefficients and gives the cusp and automorphic conditions. Square integrability is the standard cusp-form conclusion, also stated in his Lemma 4-1(e). This last paragraph uses that external theorem; the preceding convergence and regularity arguments are direct.

title: Constructing regular automorphic forms
heading: Theorem AS2 · Deep levels and high weights
text: AS2 Theorem AS2. Deep levels and high weights Define T_(Γ ,n) = ∑_(γ ≠ 1)|d_(γ)|^(− (n + 2)). If T_(Γ ,n) < 1 , the linear map v ↦ P_(Γ ,n,v) is injective. In particular it produces n + 1 linearly independent regular automorphic spinors. This criterion holds in each of the following situations: Fix n ≥ 5 and a decreasing sequence Γⱼ ⊂ Γ₀ of discrete torsion-free groups with ⋂ⱼΓⱼ = {1} . It holds for all sufficiently large j . Fix a discrete torsion-free Γ . It holds for every sufficiently large integer n . For congruence lattices these are cusp forms by AS1. In particular every fixed n ≥ 5 occurs at sufficiently deep level in a separating congruence tower. The identity term at q = 0 is v , and the other terms give ‖P_(Γ ,n,v)(0) − v‖ₙ ≤ T_(Γ ,n)‖v‖ₙ. Thus T < 1 makes evaluation of the Poincaré series an invertible linear map on Vₙ . In the first case, dominate the sum by the convergent series for Γ₀ . Each nonidentity element eventually leaves Γⱼ , so dominated convergence gives T_(Γⱼ,n) → 0 . In the second case, |d_(γ)| > 1 for γ ≠ 1 : equality would put γ in the compact stabilizer of 0 , whose intersection with a torsion-free discrete group is trivial. Each term tends to zero as n → ∞ , and the convergent n = 5 series dominates. Again T → 0 .

title: Constructing regular automorphic forms

text: Poincaré series from constant spinors Construction AS-C1. Periodizing a constant regular spinor Let Γ ⊂ G be discrete and torsion-free, n ≥ 5 , and v ∈ Vₙ . Write γ = (a_(γ), b_(γ); c_(γ), d_(γ)) . Define , P_(Γ ,n,v)(q) = ∑_(γ ∈ Γ)|c_(γ)q + d_(γ)|^(− 2)τₙ(ι((c_(γ)q + d_(γ))^(− 1)))v., (1) The seed v is regular because its derivatives in the ball coordinates vanish. Theorem AS1. Convergence, regularity, and arithmetic cuspidality [1, Lemma 4-2(i)] Under AS-C1's hypotheses, (1) converges absolutely, locally uniformly with every derivative, and defines an element of ℳₙ(Γ ) . If Γ is a congruence lattice in a rational form of G , its automorphic lift is cuspidal, square-integrable, and satisfies the usual automorphic growth and finiteness conditions. Thus (1) supplies regular cusp forms, possibly zero.

title: Constructing regular automorphic forms
heading: Ensuring that the series is nonzero
text: Ensuring that the series is nonzero Theorem AS2. Deep levels and high weights Define T_(Γ ,n) = ∑_(γ ≠ 1)|d_(γ)|^(− (n + 2)). If T_(Γ ,n) < 1 , the linear map v ↦ P_(Γ ,n,v) is injective. In particular it produces n + 1 linearly independent regular automorphic spinors. This criterion holds in each of the following situations: Fix n ≥ 5 and a decreasing sequence Γⱼ ⊂ Γ₀ of discrete torsion-free groups with ⋂ⱼΓⱼ = {1} . It holds for all sufficiently large j . Fix a discrete torsion-free Γ . It holds for every sufficiently large integer n . For congruence lattices these are cusp forms by AS1. In particular every fixed n ≥ 5 occurs at sufficiently deep level in a separating congruence tower. Discussion The bound n ≥ 5 is the convergence range of this simple periodization argument. It is not a nonexistence result at smaller weights. Nor does AS2 promise a nonzero form at every prescribed weight and level. Torsion and the center also matter: if − I ∈ Γ , the transformation law forces every odd-weight spinor to vanish. Passing to a torsion-free level removes that particular obstruction.
