title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Overview
text: Research Regular cusp spinors on quaternionic half-space, their Mellin period cocycles, an explicit weight-fourteen example, and arithmetic cohomology. Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology Discussion A regular quaternionic cusp form produces a closed two-form with flat coefficients. Its periods over triangles therefore form a group two-cocycle. Mellin transforms enter these surface periods through a primitive whose coefficients are incomplete Mellin integrals. Their compatibility is expressed by cocycle and inversion identities.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Definition CP-H2 · Regular Spinors
text: CP-H2 Definition CP-H2. Regular Spinors Let n ≥ 1 be an integer. A smooth function f : ℋ → Vₙ is a regular spinor of weight n if , (∂_(y)I_(2 × 2) + ∑_(a = 1)³Iₐ∂_(xₐ))(f_(X); f_(Y)) = 0., (HS1) Here f_(X) = ∂f/∂X and f_(Y) = ∂f/∂Y are derivatives in the auxiliary polynomial variables.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Definition CP-H0 · Regular Automorphic Forms
text: CP-H0 Definition CP-H0. Regular Automorphic Forms Let n ≥ 1 be an integer and let Γ ⊂ G be a discrete subgroup. A regular automorphic form of weight n for Γ is a smooth function f : ℋ → Vₙ satisfying both conditions: f is regular. f|ₙγ = f for every γ ∈ Γ .

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Definition CP-D0 · Growth and Finiteness Conditions
text: CP-D0 Definition CP-D0. Growth and Finiteness Conditions Let V be a finite-dimensional complex normed vector space and let F : G → V be smooth. Moderate growth. The function F has moderate growth if there are an integer A ≥ 0 and a constant C > 0 such that , ‖F(g)‖ ≤ CH(g)^(A) (g ∈ G)., (MG) Z -finiteness. The function F is Z -finite if , dim_(ℂ) span {D(z)F : z ∈ Z} < ∞., (ZF) Uniform moderate growth. The function F has uniform moderate growth if there is an integer A ≥ 0 such that, for every u ∈ U(g_(ℂ)) , there is a constant Cᵤ > 0 with , ‖D(u)F(g)‖ ≤ CᵤH(g)^(A) (g ∈ G)., (UMG) Right K -finiteness. The function F is right K -finite if dim_(ℂ) span {g ↦ F(gk) : k ∈ K} < ∞.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-Z1 · A Finite Differential Test for Central Finiteness
text: CP-Z1 Proposition CP-Z1. A Finite Differential Test for Central Finiteness [7, 0.2.7–0.2.9] Let V be a finite-dimensional complex vector space, let F : G → V be smooth, and choose algebra generators C₂,C₄ of Z . Write Dⱼ = D(Cⱼ) . Then F is Z -finite if and only if there are nonzero polynomials p₂,p₄ ∈ ℂ[t] such that p₂(D₂)F = 0, p₄(D₄)F = 0. In particular, a joint eigenfunction of D₂,D₄ is Z -finite. For type C₂ , the Weyl group acts by signed permutations of two Cartan coordinates. Its invariant polynomials are the symmetric polynomials in λ₁²,λ₂² , generated by their sum and product. The Harish-Chandra isomorphism therefore gives Z = ℂ[C₂,C₄] . If the central orbit of F spans a finite-dimensional space, both operators preserve that space. Their characteristic polynomials annihilate it by Cayley–Hamilton. Conversely, let dⱼ = deg pⱼ . If either polynomial is constant, the corresponding equation forces F = 0 . Otherwise polynomial division and commutation show that the central orbit is spanned by {D₂^(a)D₄^(b)F : 0 ≤ a < d₂, 0 ≤ b < d₄}. This is a finite set. Linear polynomials give the eigenfunction case.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Definition CP-D1 · Regular Automorphic Cusp Forms
text: CP-D1 Definition CP-D1. Regular Automorphic Cusp Forms Let Γ be a torsion-free congruence lattice in the rational-rank-one group fixed above. For n ≥ 2 , a regular automorphic cusp form of weight n is a form f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) whose lift satisfies all three conditions: F_(f) has moderate growth, measured using ‖ ⋅ ‖ₙ . F_(f) is Z -finite. At every rational cusp its constant term vanishes: , ∫_((Γ ∩ N_(ξ)) \ N_(ξ))F_(f)(ug) du = 0 (g ∈ G)., (2)

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP0 · Growth in a Cusp Frame
text: CP0 Proposition CP0. Growth in a Cusp Frame Let Γ ⊂ G be discrete, let n ≥ 1 , and let f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) have a group lift F_(f) of moderate growth with exponent A . Choose s_(ξ) ∈ G with s_(ξ)∞ = ξ and set f_(ξ) = f|ₙs_(ξ) . Then , F_(f)(s_(ξ)nₓa_(y)) = y^((n + 2)/2)f_(ξ)(y + x)., (HF) For every compact Q₀ ⊂ Im ℍ there is C_(ξ,Q₀) > 0 with , ‖f_(ξ)(y + x)‖ₙ ≤ C_(ξ,Q₀)y^((A − n − 2)/2) (x ∈ Q₀, y ≥ 1)., (H) The slash composition law gives F_(f_(ξ))(g) = F_(f)(s_(ξ)g) . Since J(nₓa_(y),1) = y^(− 1/2) , homogeneity of τₙ gives (HF). The height H is submultiplicative, H(a_(y)) = √(y) for y ≥ 1 , and H(nₓ) is bounded on Q₀ . Hence H(s_(ξ)nₓa_(y)) ≤ C√(y) . Substitute this bound in (MG) and divide (HF) by y^((n + 2)/2) .

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP1 · Cuspidality and the Petersson Norm
text: CP1 Proposition CP1. Cuspidality and the Petersson Norm [5, Thm. A, Thms. 2.23–2.24] Let G/ℚ be a simply connected semisimple group of rational rank one with G(ℝ) ≃ Sp(1,1) , and let Γ ⊂ G(ℚ) be a torsion-free congruence lattice. Let n ≥ 2 and let f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) have a group lift of moderate growth that is Z -finite. Then f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) if and only if , ‖f‖_(Γ ,n)² : = ∫_(Γ \ ℋ)y^(n − 2)‖f(y + x)‖ₙ² dx₁dx₂dx₃dy < ∞., (3) For each rational cusp ξ , choose s_(ξ) ∈ G with s_(ξ)∞ = ξ , set f_(ξ) = f|ₙs_(ξ) , and let Λ_(ξ) ⊂ Im ℍ be the lattice giving s_(ξ)^(− 1)(Γ ∩ N_(ξ))s_(ξ) = {n_(λ) : λ ∈ Λ_(ξ)} . Its average A_(ξ)(y) = (1)/(vol (ℝ³/Λ_(ξ)))∫_(ℝ³/Λ_(ξ))f_(ξ)(y + x) dx is independent of y . Finite norm implies A_(ξ) = 0 at every cusp. For a cusp form and every L ≥ 0 there is C_(ξ,L) such that , ‖f_(ξ)(y + x)‖ₙ ≤ C_(ξ,L)y^(− L − (n + 2)/2) (x in a fixed translation cell, y ≥ Y_(ξ))., (RD) The height formula Re (gz) = y/|J(g,z)|² , the norm of τₙ(Q(J)) , and the real Jacobian |J(g,z)|^(− 8) show that the density in (3) is invariant. Equivalently it is the squared invariant spinor norm y^(n + 2)‖f‖ₙ² times the invariant measure y^(− 4)dx dy . Average HS1 over the translation torus. Its spatial derivatives integrate to zero, so ∂_(X)A_(ξ)^(′) = ∂_(Y)A_(ξ)^(′) = 0 . Euler's identity for degree n > 0 gives A_(ξ)^(′) = 0 . Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the norm of the average by the mean squared norm. Thus finite (3) implies ‖A_(ξ)‖ₙ²∫_(Y_(ξ))^(∞)y^(n − 2) dy < ∞, which forces A_(ξ) = 0 for n ≥ 2 . In (HF), averaging over translations gives precisely the constant term at nₓa_(y) . Every element of G is nₓa_(y)k , and compact equivariance gives its vanishing at every g . Passing to the translation cover handles finite cusp holonomy. Conversely, the scalar components of F_(f) are smooth, left Γ -invariant, Z -finite, of moderate growth, right K -finite and cuspidal. Miller–Schmid's Theorem A gives rapid decrease on each cusp Siegel set. The comparison H(s_(ξ)nₓa_(y)) ≍ √(y) on a fixed translation cell converts it to ‖F_(f)(s_(ξ)nₓa_(y))‖ₙ ≤ C_(L)y^(− L) . Equation (HF) proves (RD), and then y^(n − 2)‖f_(ξ)(y + x)‖ₙ² ≤ C_(L)²y^(− 4 − 2L). This is integrable in each cusp. There are finitely many cusps, and smoothness gives integrability on the compact core.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-C2 · The Closed Covariant Two-Form
text: CP-C2 Proposition CP-C2. The Closed Covariant Two-Form Let n ≥ 2 and let f : ℋ → Vₙ be smooth. For regular f , dΩ_(f) = 0 and ∗ Ω_(f) = − Ω_(f) , in the orientation dy ∧ dx₁ ∧ dx₂ ∧ dx₃ . For smooth f and g ∈ G , , Ω_(f|ₙg) = ρ(g)^(− 1)g^(∗)Ω_(f)., (HS4) In particular γ^(∗)Ω_(f) = ρ(γ)Ω_(f) for f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) . The coefficients of S are constant two-forms. The direct exterior differentiation and auxiliary-variable contraction in AC3 give dΩ_(f) = 0 if and only if HS1, and give anti-self-duality. This is a local coordinate identity on the quaternionic variable, so the same computation applies on ℋ . For j = Q(J(g,z)) and r = |J(g,z)| , matrix multiplication and differentiation give Z(gz)j = R(g)Z(z), g^(∗)S = r^(− 2)j^(− t)Sj^(− 1). One may check the second identity on the translations, positive dilations, compact rotations and inversion generating G ; the denominator composition law then preserves it under products. Substituting HS2 cancels the scalar factor and the two contracted tensor factors, leaving HS4. Since Zₘ is injective and AC3's closedness criterion is an equivalence, HS4 also proves preservation of regularity.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-H1 · Exact Comparison with Ball Conventions
text: CP-H1 Proposition CP-H1. Exact Comparison with Ball Conventions Let q ∈ B = {|q| < 1} , z = Cq = (1 + q)(1 − q)^(− 1) , and let f_(B) be a ball-model spinor of weight n . Its half-space representative is , f(z) = 2^(− (n + 2)/2)|1 − q|²τₙ(Q(1 − q))f_(B)(q)., (4) For Γ = CΓ_(B)C^(− 1) this gives an isomorphism of regular automorphic cusp spaces with the transported rational structure. It satisfies , C^(∗)Ω_(f) = ρ(C)Ω_(f_(B)), ‖f‖_(Γ ,n)² = 2^(2 − n)‖f_(B)‖_(Γ_(B),n)²,, (5) where the ball norm is ∫_(Γ_(B) \ B)(1 − |q|²)^(n − 2)‖f_(B)(q)‖ₙ²dv(q) . If h^(B) is the coefficient metric of AC6, its transported half-space metric is h_(z)^(ℋ)(v₁,v₂) = h_(C^(− 1)z)^(B)(ρ(C)^(− 1)v₁,ρ(C)^(− 1)v₂), v₁,v₂ ∈ Eₘ. The inverse Cayley denominator is (z + 1)/√(2) ; its inverse is (1 − q)/√(2) . Applying the slash formula to this change of basis gives (4). The identities for Z,S in CP-C2 also hold for this Cayley matrix between the two realizations, proving the two-form identity and regularity. The group lifts satisfy F_(f)(g) = 2^(− (n + 2)/2)F_(f_(B))(C^(− 1)gC). Conjugation transports parabolics, coefficient actions, growth and central finiteness; changing variables in the normalized constant term preserves its vanishing. Finally y = (1 − |q|²)/(|1 − q|²), dv(z) = 16|1 − q|^(− 8)dv(q), ‖f(z)‖ₙ² = 2^(− (n + 2))|1 − q|^(2n + 4)‖f_(B)(q)‖ₙ². Their product proves the norm factor in (5).

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-M1 · Polarized Fourier Expansion
text: CP-M1 Proposition CP-M1. Polarized Fourier Expansion cf. [3, §3.1, Lemmas 1–3] Let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) , and assume infinity is a rational cusp with translation lattice Λ ⊂ ℝ³ . Put w = n + 2 and Λ^(∗) = {λ ∈ ℝ³ : ⟨ λ,μ ⟩ ∈ ℤ for every μ ∈ Λ }. There are vectors A_(λ) ∈ Vₙ such that , f(y + x) = ∑_(0 ≠ λ ∈ Λ^(∗))A_(λ)e^(− 2π|λ|y)e^(2πi ⟨ λ,x ⟩)., (M1) If (a_(λ),b_(λ))^(t) spans the positive eigenspace of the Hermitian matrix i Q(λ₁i + λ₂j + λ₃k) , then A_(λ) is a scalar multiple of (a_(λ)X + b_(λ)Y)ⁿ . Moreover , ‖f(y + x)‖ₙ ≤ C_(f)y^(− w/2), ‖A_(λ)‖ₙ ≤ C_(f)^(′)|λ|^(w/2)., (M2) The Fourier series and all its derivatives converge locally uniformly for y > 0 . The invariant norm of the lift is bounded on a compact core and tends to zero in every cusp by (RD). Thus it is bounded globally on Γ \ G . Equation (HF) gives the first bound in M2. Applying the conjugate quaternionic differential operator to HS1 gives the Euclidean Laplace equation for f_(X),f_(Y) . Euler's identity then gives Δ f = 0 . A Fourier coefficient a_(λ)(y) therefore satisfies a_(λ)^(′ ′) − (2π|λ|)²a_(λ) = 0. Rapid decrease excludes the growing solution, and CP1 excludes the zero mode. Substitution of a_(λ)(y) = A_(λ)e^(− 2π|λ|y) into HS1 yields (i Q(λ) − |λ|I_(2 × 2))((A_(λ))_(X); (A_(λ))_(Y)) = 0. The matrix has a one-dimensional kernel, since Q(λ)² = − |λ|²I . Equality of mixed partial derivatives and homogeneity force the stated power of a linear polynomial. Evaluate the Fourier coefficient at y = |λ|^(− 1) and apply the first bound in M2 to obtain the second. Polynomial coefficient growth combined with e^(− 2π|λ|y) proves convergence with every derivative on compact subsets.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-M2 · The Height Mellin Transform
text: CP-M2 Proposition CP-M2. The Height Mellin Transform Let n ≥ 2 and let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) be a regular automorphic cusp form. Suppose 0 and ∞ are rational cusps of Γ . Let Λ be the translation lattice at infinity, let A_(λ) be the Fourier coefficients in the polarized expansion, and put w = n + 2 . Define Λ_(f)(s) = ∫₀^(∞)f(y)y^(s − 1) dy, D_(f)(s) = ∑_(0 ≠ λ ∈ Λ^(∗))A_(λ)|λ|^(− s). The first integral is entire in s ∈ ℂ . The series converges absolutely for Re s > w/2 + 3 , and in that half-plane , Λ_(f)(s) = (2π)^(− s)Γ (s)D_(f)(s)., (M3) Here Γ (s) = ∫₀^(∞)e^(− t)t^(s − 1)dt for Re s > 0 . With W = (0, 1; 1, 0) , one has , Λ_(f)(s) = Λ_(f|ₙW)(w − s), (M4) and , Λ_(f)(s) = ∫₁^(∞)(f(y)y^(s − 1) + (f|ₙW)(y)y^(w − s − 1)) dy., (M5) The lattice has O(R³) points of length at most R , so M2 gives absolute convergence of the series in the stated half-plane. There one may integrate M1 term by term, obtaining M3. At infinity the Fourier expansion decays exponentially. On the positive real axis, (f|ₙW)(y) = y^(− w)f(1/y). The form f|ₙW is cuspidal at infinity for the conjugated lattice, because 0 is a cusp of the original group. This gives exponential decay at the other endpoint after y ↦ 1/y , up to a power of y . Both estimates are uniform on compact sets of s and remain integrable after multiplication by any power of log y . They prove entire dependence. Substitution in the two halves of the integral proves M4–M5.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-M3 · Directional Complete Transforms
text: CP-M3 Proposition CP-M3. Directional Complete Transforms Let n ≥ 2 and let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) be a regular automorphic cusp form, where 0 and ∞ are rational cusps of Γ . Write Λ for the translation lattice at infinity, A_(λ) for its Fourier coefficients, and w = n + 2 . Let ω = ω₀ + ω be a unit quaternion with ω₀ > 0 . Then ℳ_(f)(s;ω) = ∫₀^(∞)f(rω)r^(s − 1) dr is entire. For Re s > w/2 + 3 , , ℳ_(f)(s;ω) = (2π)^(− s)Γ (s)∑_(λ ≠ 0)A_(λ)(|λ|ω₀ − i ⟨ λ,ω ⟩ )^(− s)., (M6) The complex power uses the logarithm in the right half-plane. Its inversion law is , ℳ_(f|ₙW)(s;ω) = τₙ(Q(ω^(− 1)))ℳ_(f)(w − s;ω^(− 1))., (M7) Insert M1 on the ray rω ; its exponential has real decay rate 2π|λ|ω₀ > 0 . Absolute convergence in the stated half-plane permits the gamma integral, proving M6. At zero, inversion takes the ray to r^(− 1)ω^(− 1) ; the cusp estimates and periodicity in a translation frame give integrable decay. The slash factor is r^(− w)τₙ(Q(ω^(− 1))) . Substitution gives M7. The same bounds with logarithmic factors prove entire dependence, uniformly for ω in compact subsets of the open hemisphere.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-MC1 · The Incomplete-Mellin Primitive
text: CP-MC1 Proposition CP-MC1. The Incomplete-Mellin Primitive Let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) and assume infinity is a rational cusp. The integral M8 is entire in s , and dα_(f) = Ω_(f) . It has the Fourier expression , M_(f)(s;x;y) = ∑_(λ ≠ 0)A_(λ)e^(2πi ⟨ λ,x ⟩)(2π|λ|)^(− s)Γ (s,2π|λ|y),, (M10) where Γ (s,u) = ∫ᵤ^(∞)e^(− t)t^(s − 1)dt for u > 0 . The positive lower endpoint and exponential decay at infinity prove convergence, entire dependence and M10 by termwise integration. Write Ω_(f) = dy ∧ A(y,x) + B(y,x) with horizontal forms A of degree one and B of degree two. Since S(∂_(y),∂_(xₐ)) = 2ϵIₐ , the expression M9 is exactly − ∫_(y)^(∞)A(t,x)dt . Closedness of Ω_(f) gives ∂_(y)B = dₓA . Its polynomial coefficient factors and cusp decay imply B(t,x) → 0 . Thus ∂_(y)α_(f) = A, dₓα_(f) = − ∫_(y)^(∞)dₓA(t,x)dt = B(y,x). The integrals can be differentiated on compact sets by the Fourier estimates. These two identities prove dα_(f) = Ω_(f) .

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-M4 · Triangle Periods and Their Relations
text: CP-M4 Proposition CP-M4. Triangle Periods and Their Relations Assume infinity is a rational cusp. Fix o ∈ ℋ and let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) . For g,k ∈ Γ , let [o,go,gko] be the oriented geodesic triangle and put , c_(f,o)(g,k) = ∫_([o,go,gko])Ω_(f) = ∫_(∂[o,go,gko])α_(f)., (M11) It satisfies , ρ(g)c_(f,o)(k,l) − c_(f,o)(gk,l) + c_(f,o)(g,kl) − c_(f,o)(g,k) = 0., (M12) Changing the base point changes c_(f,o) by a coboundary (δa)(g,k) = ρ(g)a(k) − a(gk) + a(g). Its class in H²(Γ ,Eₘ) is the class of Ω_(f) and determines f uniquely in Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) . Stokes proves M11. Apply it to the geodesic tetrahedron [o,go,gko,gklo] . Its first face is g[o,ko,klo] ; covariance converts its integral to ρ(g)c_(f,o)(k,l) . The other three faces give M12 with their boundary signs. A prism between the two equivariant choices of vertices gives the base-point coboundary. Integration is the de Rham/group-cohomology comparison for the contractible universal cover. Finally the cuspidal injectivity theorem AC7, transported by CP-H1, says that [Ω_(f₁)] = [Ω_(f₂)] implies f₁ = f₂ .

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-M5 · A Function-Valued Period Cocycle
text: CP-M5 Proposition CP-M5. A Function-Valued Period Cocycle cf. [1, Thm. I.7.5, §§III.1, III.8]; [2, Thm. B] Let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) , assume infinity is a rational cusp, take α_(f) from CP-MC1, and fix o ∈ ℋ . Put A = C^(∞)(ℋ,Eₘ) with left action (T_(g)F)(z) = ρ(g)F(g^(− 1)z), and regard Eₘ as its submodule of constant functions. Define , b_(g)(z) = ∫_([o,z])(g^(∗)α_(f) − ρ(g)α_(f)), B_(g)(z) = b_(g)(g^(− 1)z), B̄_(g) = B_(g) mod Eₘ., (M13) The first integral is path-independent and the functions are real-analytic in the interior. They satisfy , b_(gk)(z) = b_(g)(kz) + ρ(g)bₖ(z) − b_(g)(ko),, (M14) , B̄_(gk) = B̄_(g) + T_(g)B̄ₖ., (M15) The constants κ_(f)(g,k) = b_(g)(ko) form an Eₘ -valued two-cocycle and , c_(f,o) = δa_(f) + κ_(f), a_(f)(g) = ∫_([o,go])α_(f)., (M16) For the connecting map of 0 → Eₘ → A → A/Eₘ → 0 , , ∂[B̄] = [κ_(f)] = [Ω_(f)]., (M17) The class [B̄] is independent of the primitive and its normalization, is zero after restriction to each cusp stabilizer, and determines f uniquely in the cusp space. The one-form β_(g) = g^(∗)α_(f) − ρ(g)α_(f) is closed by covariance of Ω_(f) . Contractibility makes its integral path-independent. For the integer moments in M9, the identity Γ (j + 1,u) = j ! e^(− u)∑_(a = 0)^(j)(u^(a))/(a !) and the polynomial coefficient bound in M2 give locally convergent analytic Fourier series. Hence α_(f) , and local primitives of β_(g) , are real-analytic. Pullbacks reverse composition, giving β_(gk) = k^(∗)β_(g) + ρ(g)βₖ . Integrating and imposing b_(g)(o) = 0 proves M14. Substitution gives T_(g)Bₖ − B_(gk) + B_(g) = κ_(f)(g,k), which proves M15 and M17. The group coboundary squared is zero, so κ_(f) is a two-cocycle. Integrating the three edges in M11 gives M16: the translated edge contributes ρ(g)a_(f)(k) + b_(g)(ko) . If α_(f) is replaced by α_(f) + dψ , then B̄_(g) changes by ψ − T_(g)ψ modulo constants, a coboundary. All primitives on ℋ differ this way. A change of the normalization of b_(g) only adds constants. For the primitive based at infinity and p ∈ Γ_(∞) , the form p^(∗)α_(f) − ρ(p)α_(f) is horizontal and closed. Since p acts by (y,x) ↦ (λy,λRx + t) , its coefficients tend to zero as y → ∞ . Closedness makes these horizontal coefficients independent of y , so the form vanishes. Thus Bₚ = 0 . At another cusp choose the primitive obtained in its own half-space chart. It differs from α_(f) by an exact one-form, so the restriction of B̄ is a coboundary there. Finally M17 and CP-M4 prove injectivity.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-M6 · Moving the Vertices to Cusps
text: CP-M6 Proposition CP-M6. Moving the Vertices to Cusps Let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) . For a rational cusp η set , c_(f,η)(g,k) = ∫_([η,gη,gkη])Ω_(f),, (M19) with value zero on degenerate triangles. This integral converges absolutely and satisfies M12. If a_(η,o)(g) = ∫_([η,o,go])Ω_(f) − ∫_([η,gη,go])Ω_(f), then c_(f,o) − c_(f,η) = δa_(η,o) . Moreover c_(f,η)(g,k) = 0 if either g or k fixes η . Near each ideal vertex, move that cusp to infinity. The triangle then lies in a vertical plane with bounded horizontal width near infinity. The spinor decays faster than every inverse power of height, while the fixed coefficient embedding and the coordinate transports contribute only polynomial factors. This proves integrability and makes the truncation edges, and the truncation faces of three-simplices, tend to zero. Stokes therefore proves the cocycle identity for ideal simplices as for compact ones. The prism between the vertex maps g ↦ go and g ↦ gη has the displayed one-cochain as its two-dimensional term, yielding the coboundary formula. Finally, if gη = η or kη = η , two of the triangle's vertices coincide.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-M7 · The Mellin Transform of an Ideal Triangle
text: CP-M7 Proposition CP-M7. The Mellin Transform of an Ideal Triangle Let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) and suppose 0,∞,au are cusps of Γ , where a > 0 and u is a unit imaginary quaternion. Orient T_(a,u) = [0,∞,au] by dy ∧ dt in z = y + tu . Put P_(f,a,u)(s) = ∫_(T_(a,u))(|z|/a)^(s)Ω_(f). This is entire and P_(f,a,u)(0) = ∫_(T_(a,u))Ω_(f) . Set ω_(θ) = cos θ + u sin θ, Zₘ(rω) = ∑_(j = 0)^(m)r^(j)Bⱼ(ω), Kᵤ = 2ϵQ(u), ℳ_(f)(v;ω;l,b) = ∫ₗ^(b)f(rω)r^(v − 1)dr. Then , P_(f,a,u)(s) = a^(− s)∑_(j = 0)^(m)∫₀^(π/2)Bⱼ(ω_(θ))Φ_(Kᵤ)(ℳ_(f)(s + j + 2;ω_(θ);a sin θ,a/ sin θ)) dθ., (M20) For a unit imaginary v perpendicular to u , put g_(a,u) = (0, av; a^(− 1)v, 0). It belongs to G , and the transforms satisfy , P_(f|ₙg_(a,u),a,u)(s) = − ρ(g_(a,u))^(− 1)P_(f,a,u)( − s)., (M21) In the vertical plane the triangle has 0 < t < a and y² + t² > at . With y = r cos θ and t = r sin θ , this becomes 0 < θ < π/2, a sin θ < r < a/ sin θ. The pullback of S on (∂ᵣ,∂_(θ)) is rKᵤ . Expanding Zₘ and integrating gives M20. Cusp decay proves absolute convergence; the factor (|z|/a)^(s) and its derivatives in s have at most polynomial-logarithmic growth near zero and infinity and are bounded near the third vertex on compact sets of s . This proves entire dependence. One checks g_(a,u)^(∗)H₀g_(a,u) = H₀ and g_(a,u)² = − I . On the indicated plane it acts as rω_(θ) ⟼ a²r^(− 1)ω_(θ). It preserves the triangle, interchanges its radial bounds and reverses its orientation. Apply HS4 and change variables; the weight changes from (r/a)^(s) to (r/a)^(− s) , giving M21.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Construction CP-E0 · The Colored Reflection Group
text: CP-E0 Construction CP-E0. The Colored Reflection Group Let L = diag ( − 1,1,1,1,1) and ℍ_(L)⁴ = {v ∈ ℝ⁵ : v^(t)Lv = − 1, v₀ > 0}. Write e₀,…,e₄ for the coordinate vectors. For ν^(t)Lν = 1 , put r_(ν) = I − 2νν^(t)L . Set Aᵢ = r_(eᵢ), Bᵢⱼ = r_(e₀ + eᵢ + eⱼ) (1 ≤ i < j ≤ 4), W₂ = ⟨ Aᵢ,Bᵢⱼ ⟩ . Let ē₁,…,ē₄ be the basis of F₂⁴ . Define χ : W₂ → F₂⁴ by χ(Aᵢ) = ēᵢ and Pair (i,j) Color χ(Bᵢⱼ) (1,2) ē₁ (1,3) ē₃ (1,4) ē₄ (2,3) ē₂ (2,4) ē₁ + ē₂ + ē₃ (3,4) ē₁ + ē₂ + ē₄ Put Γ_(L) = ker χ . Identify v ∈ ℍ_(L)⁴ with the ball point q = (v₁ + v₂i + v₃j + v₄k)/(v₀ + 1), and then with z = Cq ∈ ℋ . Let Γ ⊂ G/{ ± I} be the resulting group acting on ℋ .

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-E1 · Geometry and Congruence of the Example Group
text: CP-E1 Proposition CP-E1. Geometry and Congruence of the Example Group [4, §4, pp. 9–10] The color map in CP-E0 is a homomorphism. Its kernel is orientation-preserving, torsion-free, and has index 16 in W₂ . It contains the principal level-four subgroup W₄ = {g ∈ W₂ : g ≡ I (mod 4)}, [Γ_(L) : W₄] = 64. A fundamental domain is the regular ideal 24-cell obtained from the chamber P = {v ∈ ℍ_(L)⁴ : vᵢ ≥ 0, vᵢ + vⱼ ≤ v₀ (i < j)} by all sixteen spatial coordinate-sign changes. The boundary points 0,∞,i/2 are cusps of Γ . The cited reflection-group theorem identifies W₂ with the time-orientation-preserving integral Lorentz group congruent to I modulo two, with chamber P . Its Coxeter relations are that the ten reflections have order two and perpendicular-wall reflections commute. All colors satisfy these relations, and the four Aᵢ prove surjectivity. Every color has odd coordinate sum. Thus zero color implies even reflection parity and orientation preservation. To check torsion, the maximal sets of mutually perpendicular walls are: the four Aᵢ ; for each three-element index set {i,j,k} , the set {Bᵢⱼ,Bᵢₖ,Bⱼₖ,Aₗ} with l complementary; for each i , the three Bᵢⱼ with j ≠ i ; and the six sets {Aᵢ,Aⱼ,Bₖₗ} with complementary pairs. Substituting the displayed colors gives independent columns over F₂ in each of these fifteen cases. A finite subgroup fixes a hyperbolic point; after moving it to P , its stabilizer is generated by the walls through that point. The color map is injective on such a stabilizer, so its kernel has no torsion. The coordinate-sign subgroup supplies sixteen coset representatives; the union of their chambers is the ideal 24-cell. For the congruence assertion, set D_(g) = (g − I)/2 (mod 2) . Matrix multiplication adds these matrices modulo two. Put βᵢⱼ = (D_(g))ᵢⱼ, αᵢ = (D_(g))ᵢᵢ + ∑_(j ≠ i)β_(min (i,j),max (i,j)). Then χ(g) = ∑ᵢαᵢēᵢ + ∑_(i < j)βᵢⱼχ(Bᵢⱼ), as is checked on the ten generators. Their ten D_(g) -matrices are independent: the six off-diagonal spatial entries detect the Bᵢⱼ , then the four diagonal entries detect the Aᵢ . Hence |W₂/W₄| = 2¹⁰ , proving the indices and congruence inclusion. The points q = 1, − 1 are rational isotropic boundary lines and hence cusps; their half-space images are ∞,0 . The element a below sends 0 to i/2 , proving the last assertion.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-E2 · An Explicit Nonzero Poincaré Series
text: CP-E2 Proposition CP-E2. An Explicit Nonzero Poincaré Series [6, Lemma 4-2(i)] For v ∈ V₁₄ define the half-space seed and its periodization by , ϕᵥ(z) = 2⁸|z + 1|^(− 2)τ₁₄(Q((z + 1)^(− 1)))v, hᵥ(z) = ∑_(γ ∈ Γ)(ϕᵥ|₁₄γ)(z)., (E1) For either lift γ = (a_(γ), b_(γ); c_(γ), d_(γ)) , this is , hᵥ(z) = 2⁸∑_(γ ∈ Γ)|L_(γ)(z)|^(− 2)τ₁₄(Q(L_(γ)(z)^(− 1)))v, L_(γ)(z) = (a_(γ) + c_(γ))z + b_(γ) + d_(γ)., (E2) The series converges absolutely locally with derivatives and defines a regular cusp form. It satisfies , ‖hᵥ(1) − 2^(− 8)v‖₁₄ ≤ (3)/(4) 2^(− 8)‖v‖₁₄, ‖hᵥ(1)‖₁₄ ≥ 2^(− 10)‖v‖₁₄., (E3) In particular v ↦ hᵥ is injective. For W in CP-M2, , hᵥ|₁₄W = hᵥ, Λ_(hᵥ)(s) = Λ_(hᵥ)(16 − s)., (E4) The Cayley image (4) of the constant ball seed v is ϕᵥ , since 1 − q = 2(z + 1)^(− 1) . The product of the two denominator factors in ϕᵥ|γ is L_(γ)(z) in the indicated order, proving E2. The constant-seed construction AS1 gives convergence with derivatives and regularity. Its lift is a matrix coefficient of the weight-fourteen discrete series, which is integrable because 14 > 4 ; Muić's cited theorem gives cuspidality for this congruence lattice. Summing over the spin inverse image gives twice E1; the even central character allows the displayed effective-group sum. For the nonzero bound, work briefly at the ball center o_(L) = (1,0,0,0,0) . Torsion-freeness makes γ ↦ γo_(L) injective. For γ ≠ 1 write γo_(L) = (2N − 1,2z₁,2z₂,2z₃,2z₄), |z|² = N(N − 1), N ≥ 2. Each integer coordinate has absolute value at most N − 1 ; choosing three leaves at most two choices for the fourth. There are therefore fewer than 16N³ possible orbit points. For a ball lift, |d_(γ)|² = N , and the summand at the center has norm N^(− 8)‖v‖₁₄ . The tail is at most 16∑_(N = 2)^(∞)N^(− 5) ≤ 16(2^(− 5) + ∫₂^(∞)t^(− 5)dt) = (3)/(4). The center value transforms by hᵥ(1) = 2^(− 8)Fᵥ(0) , proving E3. The spatial sign change q ↦ − q lies in W₂ and normalizes ker χ . A ball lift is k = diag ( − 1,1) ; it fixes the constant seed under slash. Reindexing the absolutely convergent Poincaré sum gives Fᵥ|k = Fᵥ . Since CkC^(− 1) = W , this proves the first identity in E4; CP-M2 proves the second.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-E3 · The (a,a) Period as a Surface Mellin Integral
text: CP-E3 Proposition CP-E3. The (a,a) Period as a Surface Mellin Integral Let h = h_(X¹⁴) , E₁₂ = Sym¹² ℂ⁴ , and choose the element with half-space lift a = (0, − i; − i, − 2) ∈ G. Then a ∈ Γ , a∞ = 0 and a²∞ = i/2 . With c_(h,∞) from M19, , c_(h,∞)(a,a) = − P_(h,1/2,i)(0)., (E5) Writing ω_(θ) = cos θ + i sin θ and Z₁₂(rω) = ∑_(j = 0)¹²r^(j)Bⱼ(ω) , its value is , c_(h,∞)(a,a) = (4i)/(14 ⋅ 13)∑_(j = 0)¹²∫₀^(π/2)Bⱼ(ω_(θ))[∫_((1)/(2)sin θ)^((1)/(2 sin θ))h_(XY)(rω_(θ))r^(j + 1) dr]dθ., (E6) The formula is an equality in the 455 -dimensional coefficient space E₁₂ . The Lorentz transformation A₁B₁₂ has zero color and ball lift ( − 1 + i, 1; 1, − 1 − i). Conjugation by C gives the displayed half-space lift. Its fractional action sends ∞ to zero and zero to i/2 . Thus the ideal triangle in M19 is [∞,0,i/2] , with the opposite orientation to T_(1/2,i) = [0,∞,i/2] . This proves E5. Finally Φ_(2ϵQ(i))(p) = − (4i)/(14 ⋅ 13)p_(XY). Substitute this into M20 at s = 0 and reverse the sign from E5 to obtain E6. The dimension is ((15)/(3)) = 455 .

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP3 · Cusp Forms Satisfy the Parabolic Cocycle Condition
text: CP3 Proposition CP3. Cusp Forms Satisfy the Parabolic Cocycle Condition If f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) , then [Ω_(f)] ∈ Hₚₐᵣ²(Γ ,Eₘ) . In particular its triangle-integral two-cocycle satisfies (7). Move the cusp to infinity, transport the group and form, and write f for its cusp-frame representative. Work on a translation cover of the cross-section at fixed height y . Untwist the flat coefficient monodromy by writing its tangential restriction in the periodic frame α(x) = ρ(nₓ)^(− 1)Ω_(f)(x,y). The connection in that frame is d_(N) = d + ∑_(j = 1)³Nⱼ dxⱼ, where the Nⱼ = dρ(∂_(xⱼ)) commute and are nilpotent. Equivariance of the two-form construction implies that α(x) is a fixed linear function of F_(f)(nₓa_(y)) at this height: translating by nₓ translates the tangent coframe and multiplies the flat coefficient by ρ(nₓ) . Hence (2) says its zero Fourier coefficient is zero. Also d_(N)α = 0 . For a nonzero Fourier mode ℓ ∈ Λ^(∗) , choose j with ℓⱼ ≠ 0 . Choose r with Nⱼ^(r) = 0 . The operator Aⱼ = 2πiℓⱼI + Nⱼ has inverse Aⱼ^(− 1) = (1)/(2πiℓⱼ)∑_(a = 0)^(r − 1)( − (Nⱼ)/(2πiℓⱼ))^(a). For d_(N,ℓ) = ∑ₖdxₖ ∧ (2πiℓₖ + Nₖ), H_(ℓ) = Aⱼ^(− 1)ι_(∂_(xⱼ)), the identity ι_(∂_(xⱼ))(dxₖ ∧ ω) + dxₖ ∧ ι_(∂_(xⱼ))ω = δⱼₖω , together with commutation of the Nₖ , gives d_(N,ℓ)H_(ℓ) + H_(ℓ)d_(N,ℓ) = Aⱼ^(− 1)Aⱼ = I. Thus for each closed mode α_(ℓ) , the one-form β_(ℓ) = H_(ℓ)α_(ℓ) satisfies d_(N,ℓ)β_(ℓ) = α_(ℓ) . Choose j with |ℓⱼ| = maxₖ |ℓₖ| ≥ ‖ℓ‖/√(3) . The finite inverse formula gives ‖H_(ℓ)‖ ≤ C‖ℓ‖^(− 1) for sufficiently large ‖ℓ‖ . Smoothness of α on the torus gives ‖α_(ℓ)‖ ≤ C_(M)(1 + ‖ℓ‖)^(− M) for every M ; the same rapid decay holds for β_(ℓ) . Hence β(x) = ∑_(ℓ ≠ 0)β_(ℓ)e^(2πiℓ(x)) and all its derivatives converge uniformly, and d_(N)β = α . For the finite-index inclusion Λ ⊂ Γ_(ξ) , restriction followed by cohomological transfer satisfies cor ∘ res = [Γ_(ξ) : Λ ]I . Multiplication by this positive integer is invertible over ℂ , so restriction is injective. The full cusp-stabilizer class therefore vanishes. The de Rham/group-cohomology comparison and AC5 give (7).

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP-C1 · The Complementary Chirality
text: CP-C1 Proposition CP-C1. The Complementary Chirality Let n ≥ 2 and f₊ ∈ Sₙ^(−)(θΓ ) . The form Ω_(f₊)⁺ is closed, satisfies γ^(∗)Ω_(f₊)⁺ = ρ(γ)Ω_(f₊)⁺ for γ ∈ Γ , and satisfies ∗ Ω_(f₊)⁺ = Ω_(f₊)⁺ . The corresponding minimal compact type is Vₙ ⊠ V₀ . The identity r ∘ γ = θ(γ) ∘ r and the representation identity ρ(θ(γ)) = Rₘ(D₀)ρ(γ)Rₘ(D₀)^(− 1) give γ^(∗)Ω_(f₊)⁺ = Rₘ(D₀)^(− 1)r^(∗)θ(γ)^(∗)Ω_(f₊) = ρ(γ)Ω_(f₊)⁺. The constant coefficient map and pullback commute with the flat differential, proving closedness. The map r is an orientation-reversing isometry of the half-space, so ∗ r^(∗) = − r^(∗) ∗ on two-forms. Since ∗ Ω_(f₊) = − Ω_(f₊) by AC3, the pulled-back form is self-dual. Conjugation by D₀ exchanges the two factors of K and carries rational parabolics and their unipotent radicals to those for the transported rational structure. Change of variables in the constant-term integrals preserves their vanishing; conjugation also preserves polynomial growth and central finiteness. Thus the transported space has the claimed cuspidality and compact type.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Construction CP-D4 · Unnormalized Double-Coset Operators
text: CP-D4 Construction CP-D4. Unnormalized Double-Coset Operators Choose the finite left-coset decomposition Γ αΓ = ∐ᵢΓ αᵢ . On the two cusp-spinor spaces set , T_(α)^(−)f_(−) = ∑ᵢf_(−)|ₙαᵢ, T_(α)⁺f₊ = ∑ᵢf₊|ₙθ(αᵢ),, (19) where f₊ ∈ Sₙ^(−)(θΓ ) = Sₙ⁺(Γ ) and θ is defined in CP-C1.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP8 · Hecke Equivariance with Number-Field Coefficients
text: CP8 Proposition CP8. Hecke Equivariance with Number-Field Coefficients For the data of CP-D4, T_(α) preserves H_(L) and is L -linear. The operators T_(α)^(±) are independent of the representatives in (19) and preserve Sₙ^(±)(Γ ) . For every smooth f : ℋ → Vₙ and every a ∈ G , , Ω_(f|ₙa) = Rₘ(a)^(− 1)a^(∗)Ω_(f)., (20) Write Φ (f_(−),f₊) = [Ω_(f_(−)) + Ω_(f₊)⁺] for the isomorphism of CP5. Then , Φ (T_(α)^(−)f_(−),T_(α)⁺f₊) = T_(α)Φ (f_(−),f₊)., (21) Consequently Φ^(− 1)(H_(L)) is an L -form of Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) ⊕︎ Sₙ⁺(Γ ) stable under every operator in (19). Rational elements commensurate an arithmetic group: in an integral faithful representation, clearing the finitely many denominators of α and α^(− 1) gives a principal congruence subgroup contained in the intersection. Thus the coverings have finite degree. The coefficient identification is well-defined because for δ ∈ Γ_(α) , ρ_(m,L)(α)^(− 1)ρ_(m,L)(αδα^(− 1)) = ρ_(m,L)(δ)ρ_(m,L)(α)^(− 1). Pullback, this identification, and trace are all L -linear. Both covering maps are proper. Pullback therefore preserves compact support, as does trace, whose support is contained in the image of the original support. These maps commute with the map from compactly supported to ordinary cohomology. Hence (17) preserves its image, which is H_(L) by the compact-core argument of CP2 over L . We verify the differential-form formula before passing to cohomology. Put j = ι(J(a,z)) and r = |J(a,z)| . The identities used in AC2–AC3 are Z(az)j = R(a)Z(z), a^(∗)S = r^(− 2)j^(− t)Sj^(− 1). By (18), f(az) = r²j^(⊙ n)(f|ₙa)(z) . Contracting with a^(∗)S cancels the scalar and two tensor factors, leaving a^(∗)Φₙ(f) = τₘ(j)Φₙ(f|ₙa). Multiplication by Zₘ(az) now proves (20). In particular, closedness and AC3 show that slash preserves regularity. The cocycle identity for J gives (f|ₙa)|ₙb = f|ₙ(ab) . Left multiplication of a representative by Γ therefore does not change its summand. Right multiplication by Γ permutes the left cosets, proving automorphy of (19). To check cuspidality, each summand is automorphic on a finite-index congruence subgroup of Γ . Its group lift is g ↦ F_(f)(αᵢg) . Left translation commutes with right differentiation, so central finiteness is preserved; H(αᵢg) ≤ H(αᵢ)H(g) preserves moderate growth. More explicitly, put Δᵢ = Γ ∩ αᵢ^(− 1)Γ αᵢ and use the coefficient norm and compatible quotient Haar measures. Then ∫_(Δᵢ \ G)‖F_(f)(αᵢg)‖ₙ² dg = [Γ : αᵢΔᵢαᵢ^(− 1)]∫_(Γ \ G)‖F_(f)(g)‖ₙ² dg < ∞. This is the same finiteness as the Petersson norm, by (HF), the invariant density in CP1, and compact equivariance. On the common finite cover for ⋂ᵢΔᵢ , the inequality ‖∑ᵢvᵢ‖ₙ² ≤ r∑ᵢ‖vᵢ‖ₙ² for r summands proves that the sum still has finite norm, hence so does its descent to X . CP1 makes it cuspidal. The same argument applies to the reflected group for the plus space. Choose representatives γᵢ of Γ_(α) \ Γ , so αᵢ = αγᵢ . On equivariant differential forms, the trace in (17) is , T_(α)ω = ∑ᵢRₘ(αᵢ)^(− 1)αᵢ^(∗)ω., (22) Indeed the sheet [γᵢz] contributes pullback by αγᵢ and the coefficient transport Rₘ(γᵢ)^(− 1)Rₘ(α)^(− 1) . Applying (20) term by term proves Ω_(T_(α)^(−)f) = T_(α)Ω_(f) . For the plus space, use r ∘ a = θ(a) ∘ r and Rₘ(D₀)^(− 1)Rₘ(θ(a))^(− 1) = Rₘ(a)^(− 1)Rₘ(D₀)^(− 1) in the formula of CP-C1. This proves the corresponding identity for Ω⁺ . Passing to cohomology proves (21). Finally combine (15) with CP5 to obtain the stated L -form.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Corollary CP9 · Hecke Eigenvalues Lie in a Number Field
text: CP9 Corollary CP9. Hecke Eigenvalues Lie in a Number Field Let Γ , n ≥ 2 , L , and H_(L) be as in CP7, and use the normalization in CP-D4. Let 0 ≠ f ∈ Sₙ^(ε)(Γ ) , with ε ∈ { − , + } . If T_(α)^(ε)f = λ_(α)f , then , det (λ_(α)id_(H_(L)) − T_(α)|_(H_(L))) = 0., (23) In particular λ_(α) is algebraic over ℚ . If {T_(α) : α ∈ A} is a commuting family of these operators and f is a simultaneous eigenvector, then , L_(f) = L(λ_(α) : α ∈ A), (24) is a finite extension of L . Let v = [Ω_(f)] for the minus space and v = [Ω_(f)⁺] for the plus space. By the cuspidal injection AC7 and its reflected version, v ≠ 0 ; by CP3 and reflection, v ∈ H_(L)⊗_(L)ℂ . Formula (20) and the trace calculation give T_(α)v = λ_(α)v . Thus λ_(α) is a root of the characteristic polynomial of the L -linear operator T_(α) on the finite-dimensional space H_(L) . This proves (23), and algebraicity over L implies algebraicity over ℚ . For (24), let T_(L) ⊆ End_(L) (H_(L)) be the unital L -algebra generated by the commuting family. It is finite-dimensional because it is an L -subspace of End_(L) (H_(L)) . Its action on the nonzero common eigenline ℂv defines an L -algebra homomorphism χ_(f) : T_(L) → ℂ . Its image is a finite-dimensional L -algebra contained in a field. Multiplication by a nonzero element of that image is injective, hence surjective by finite-dimensionality, so the image is itself a field. It contains exactly the L -algebra generated by the eigenvalues, and therefore equals L_(f) . This proves [L_(f) : L] < ∞ .

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Half-Space and Regular Spinors
text: Half-Space and Regular Spinors Discussion We first describe the domain and the coefficient space. Regularity is a differential equation on that space; automorphy is a transformation law under a discrete group. The two conditions define the space ℳₙ(Γ ) of regular automorphic forms.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: The Domain and Group Action
text: The Domain and Group Action Write a quaternion as z = y + x , where x = x₁i + x₂j + x₃k is purely imaginary. The domain is the quaternionic half-space ℋ = {y + x ∈ ℍ : y > 0}. We use the following realization of Sp(1,1) : G = {g ∈ GL₂ (ℍ) : g^(∗)H₀g = H₀}, H₀ = (0, 1; 1, 0). Here g^(∗) means quaternionic conjugate transpose. A matrix g = (a, b; c, d) acts by gz = (az + b)(cz + d)^(− 1), J(g,z) = cz + d. The base point is 1 ∈ ℋ . Its stabilizer is the maximal compact subgroup K = C{diag (u,v) : |u| = |v| = 1}C^(− 1), C = 2^(− 1/2)(1, 1; − 1, 1). We label the two compact factors by this conjugation and write σ(k) = J(k,1) for the second factor. The action and its relation to the ball are established in Quaternionic Half-Space and Siegel Domains.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Polynomial Coefficients
text: Polynomial Coefficients Fix an integer n ≥ 1 . The coefficient space is Vₙ = Symⁿ ℂ² = {∑_(j = 0)ⁿpⱼX^(n − j)Y^(j) : pⱼ ∈ ℂ}. Thus a function f : ℋ → Vₙ is a polynomial in the auxiliary variables X,Y , with coefficient functions on ℋ . These auxiliary variables are distinct from the coordinates y,x₁,x₂,x₃ of the domain. For a complex 2 × 2 matrix A , the symmetric-power action is (τₙ(A)p)(X,Y) = p(((X,Y)A)₁,((X,Y)A)₂). We represent quaternions by complex matrices through Q(y + x) = (y + i x₁, x₂ + i x₃; − x₂ + i x₃, y − i x₁), and use I₁ = Q(i) , I₂ = Q(j) , I₃ = Q(k) and ϵ = (0, 1; − 1, 0) . The symbol i denotes the complex scalar imaginary unit; i,j,k denote quaternion units. The map Q is called ι in the earlier articles. The coefficient norm is ‖p‖ₙ² = ∑_(j = 0)ⁿ((n)/(j))^(− 1)|pⱼ|². This is the symmetric-tensor norm induced by the usual Hermitian norm on ℂ² . Consequently τₙ(Q(u)) is unitary when |u| = 1 , and its operator norm is |u|ⁿ for nonzero u .

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Regularity and Automorphy
text: Regularity and Automorphy Definition CP-H2. Regular Spinors Let n ≥ 1 be an integer. A smooth function f : ℋ → Vₙ is a regular spinor of weight n if , (∂_(y)I_(2 × 2) + ∑_(a = 1)³Iₐ∂_(xₐ))(f_(X); f_(Y)) = 0., (HS1) Here f_(X) = ∂f/∂X and f_(Y) = ∂f/∂Y are derivatives in the auxiliary polynomial variables. For a smooth f : ℋ → Vₙ and g ∈ G , use the slash notation , (f|ₙg)(z) = |J(g,z)|^(− 2)τₙ(Q(J(g,z)^(− 1)))f(gz)., (HS2) The denominator identity gives (f|ₙg)|ₙh = f|ₙ(gh) . For the weights n ≥ 2 used below, the covariance calculation in the two-form construction shows that the slash action preserves regularity. These facts allow regularity and a group transformation law to be imposed together. Definition CP-H0. Regular Automorphic Forms Let n ≥ 1 be an integer and let Γ ⊂ G be a discrete subgroup. A regular automorphic form of weight n for Γ is a smooth function f : ℋ → Vₙ satisfying both conditions: f is regular. f|ₙγ = f for every γ ∈ Γ . The complex vector space of these forms is denoted by ℳₙ(Γ ) = {f ∈ C^(∞)(ℋ,Vₙ) : f is regular and f|ₙγ = f for all γ ∈ Γ }. Discussion The notation ℳₙ(Γ ) imposes the differential equation and transformation law. Growth and cuspidality will be specified separately below, as is usual when passing from automorphic functions to spaces with prescribed behavior at the cusps.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Growth and Finiteness Conditions
text: Growth and Finiteness Conditions The growth condition uses the ordinary Euclidean norm on ℍ² : ‖(v₁,v₂)^(t)‖ = √(|v₁|² + |v₂|²), |a + bi + cj + dk| = √(a² + b² + c² + d²). For a matrix g ∈ G , its operator norm is the largest stretching factor for this positive norm: ‖g‖ₒₚ = sup_(v ≠ 0) (‖gv‖)/(‖v‖). Set H(g) = max {1,‖g‖ₒₚ,‖g^(− 1)‖ₒₚ}. The indefinite form preserved by G has value 2 Re (v̄₁v₂) ; it is distinct from the Euclidean norm used to measure growth. For differential operators, write g = Lie (G) and g_(ℂ) = g⊗_(ℝ)ℂ . Right differentiation is given by D(T)F(g) = (d)/(dt)F(g exp (tT))|_(t = 0) (T ∈ g). It extends complex-linearly and multiplicatively to the universal enveloping algebra U(g_(ℂ)) . Its center is denoted by Z = Z(U(g_(ℂ))) . Elements of Z therefore act as invariant differential operators on F . Definition CP-D0. Growth and Finiteness Conditions Let V be a finite-dimensional complex normed vector space and let F : G → V be smooth. Moderate growth. The function F has moderate growth if there are an integer A ≥ 0 and a constant C > 0 such that , ‖F(g)‖ ≤ CH(g)^(A) (g ∈ G)., (MG) Z -finiteness. The function F is Z -finite if , dim_(ℂ) span {D(z)F : z ∈ Z} < ∞., (ZF) Uniform moderate growth. The function F has uniform moderate growth if there is an integer A ≥ 0 such that, for every u ∈ U(g_(ℂ)) , there is a constant Cᵤ > 0 with , ‖D(u)F(g)‖ ≤ CᵤH(g)^(A) (g ∈ G)., (UMG) Right K -finiteness. The function F is right K -finite if dim_(ℂ) span {g ↦ F(gk) : k ∈ K} < ∞. Discussion Moderate growth is a polynomial bound. Uniform moderate growth uses one exponent for every derivative, although the constants may depend on the derivative. The definition of a cusp form below requires moderate growth and Z -finiteness; the rapid-decrease theorem then supplies the decay used in period integrals. These conventions agree with [5, §2].

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Finiteness as a Differential Equation
text: Finiteness as a Differential Equation Discussion For classical Maass forms, the familiar spectral condition is a Laplace eigenvalue equation. The condition here has the same differential-equation interpretation, with two commuting central operators. The complexified Lie algebra is sp₄(ℂ) , and the center of its universal enveloping algebra is a polynomial algebra on generators C₂,C₄ of degrees two and four. Put D₂ = D(C₂) and D₄ = D(C₄) . The [7] gives these generators; a finite test for the definition follows. Proposition CP-Z1. A Finite Differential Test for Central Finiteness [7, 0.2.7–0.2.9] Let V be a finite-dimensional complex vector space, let F : G → V be smooth, and choose algebra generators C₂,C₄ of Z . Write Dⱼ = D(Cⱼ) . Then F is Z -finite if and only if there are nonzero polynomials p₂,p₄ ∈ ℂ[t] such that p₂(D₂)F = 0, p₄(D₄)F = 0. In particular, a joint eigenfunction of D₂,D₄ is Z -finite. Discussion Thus finiteness can be established by differential identities, without enumerating an infinite algebra. In a fixed homogeneous bundle these become equations for the coefficient functions on half-space, including the connection terms. They are not simply the ordinary scalar Euclidean Laplacian applied componentwise. For the weight- n quaternionic discrete series, the infinitesimal character is (n,1) in the Cartan coordinates of the weight dictionary. Normalize C₂,C₄ so their Harish-Chandra polynomials are λ₁² + λ₂² and λ₁²λ₂² . A lift belonging to this representation then satisfies D₂F = (n² + 1)F, D₄F = n²F. This follows by evaluating those polynomials at (n,1) . In particular the matrix-coefficient construction of the weight-fourteen Poincaré series establishes its central finiteness through these eigenvalue equations. For a separately proposed function, the differential identities or its membership in the representation must still be established; regularity is not being used here as an unproved substitute for central finiteness.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Vanishing Constant Terms
text: Vanishing Constant Terms Let G/ℚ be a simply connected semisimple group of rational rank one, with G(ℝ) ≃ G , and let Γ ⊂ G(ℚ) be a torsion-free congruence lattice. Put X = Γ \ ℋ . For an integer n ≥ 2 and f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) , its group lift is , F_(f)(g) = |J(g,1)|^(− 2)τₙ(Q(J(g,1)^(− 1)))f(g1)., (1) The lift satisfies F_(f)(gk) = τₙ(Q(σ(k)^(− 1)))F_(f)(g) , so it is right K -finite. Indeed, k1 = 1 and the denominator cocycle gives J(gk,1) = J(g,1)J(k,1) . Here rational cusps are Γ -orbits of proper rational parabolic subgroups P_(ξ) = M_(ξ)A_(ξ)N_(ξ) ; N_(ξ) ≃ (ℝ³, + ) is the unipotent radical. The quotient Haar measure is normalized to have total mass one. Definition CP-D1. Regular Automorphic Cusp Forms Let Γ be a torsion-free congruence lattice in the rational-rank-one group fixed above. For n ≥ 2 , a regular automorphic cusp form of weight n is a form f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) whose lift satisfies all three conditions: F_(f) has moderate growth, measured using ‖ ⋅ ‖ₙ . F_(f) is Z -finite. At every rational cusp its constant term vanishes: , ∫_((Γ ∩ N_(ξ)) \ N_(ξ))F_(f)(ug) du = 0 (g ∈ G)., (2) The space of regular automorphic cusp forms is denoted by Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) . Discussion Defining the constant term on the group makes it independent of the cusp coordinates. In a frame adapted to a cusp, it is the average over the three translation variables. The minus sign in Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) labels the anti-self-dual two-form constructed below. Proposition CP0. Growth in a Cusp Frame Let Γ ⊂ G be discrete, let n ≥ 1 , and let f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) have a group lift F_(f) of moderate growth with exponent A . Choose s_(ξ) ∈ G with s_(ξ)∞ = ξ and set f_(ξ) = f|ₙs_(ξ) . Then , F_(f)(s_(ξ)nₓa_(y)) = y^((n + 2)/2)f_(ξ)(y + x)., (HF) For every compact Q₀ ⊂ Im ℍ there is C_(ξ,Q₀) > 0 with , ‖f_(ξ)(y + x)‖ₙ ≤ C_(ξ,Q₀)y^((A − n − 2)/2) (x ∈ Q₀, y ≥ 1)., (H) Proposition CP1. Cuspidality and the Petersson Norm [5, Thm. A, Thms. 2.23–2.24] Let G/ℚ be a simply connected semisimple group of rational rank one with G(ℝ) ≃ Sp(1,1) , and let Γ ⊂ G(ℚ) be a torsion-free congruence lattice. Let n ≥ 2 and let f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) have a group lift of moderate growth that is Z -finite. Then f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) if and only if , ‖f‖_(Γ ,n)² : = ∫_(Γ \ ℋ)y^(n − 2)‖f(y + x)‖ₙ² dx₁dx₂dx₃dy < ∞., (3) For each rational cusp ξ , choose s_(ξ) ∈ G with s_(ξ)∞ = ξ , set f_(ξ) = f|ₙs_(ξ) , and let Λ_(ξ) ⊂ Im ℍ be the lattice giving s_(ξ)^(− 1)(Γ ∩ N_(ξ))s_(ξ) = {n_(λ) : λ ∈ Λ_(ξ)} . Its average A_(ξ)(y) = (1)/(vol (ℝ³/Λ_(ξ)))∫_(ℝ³/Λ_(ξ))f_(ξ)(y + x) dx is independent of y . Finite norm implies A_(ξ) = 0 at every cusp. For a cusp form and every L ≥ 0 there is C_(ξ,L) such that , ‖f_(ξ)(y + x)‖ₙ ≤ C_(ξ,L)y^(− L − (n + 2)/2) (x in a fixed translation cell, y ≥ Y_(ξ))., (RD)

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: The Closed Two-Form and the Ball-Coordinate Dictionary
text: The Closed Two-Form and the Ball-Coordinate Dictionary For n ≥ 2 put m = n − 2 , Eₘ = Sym^(m) ℂ⁴ . If g is a quaternionic matrix, let R(g) be its complex block matrix obtained by applying Q to each entry, and put ρ(g) = Rₘ(g) = Sym^(m) R(g) . Define Z(z) = (Q(z); I_(2 × 2)), Zₘ(z) = Sym^(m) Z(z), S = ϵ(dQ^(∗) ∧ dQ), , Φ_(K)(p) = (K₁₁p_(XX) + 2K₁₂p_(XY) + K₂₂p_(YY))/(n(n − 1)), Ω_(f) = ZₘΦ_(S)(f)., (HS3) Here K is a symmetric 2 × 2 matrix with scalar or differential-form entries; the same contraction defines Φ_(K) in either case. Proposition CP-C2. The Closed Covariant Two-Form Let n ≥ 2 and let f : ℋ → Vₙ be smooth. For regular f , dΩ_(f) = 0 and ∗ Ω_(f) = − Ω_(f) , in the orientation dy ∧ dx₁ ∧ dx₂ ∧ dx₃ . For smooth f and g ∈ G , , Ω_(f|ₙg) = ρ(g)^(− 1)g^(∗)Ω_(f)., (HS4) In particular γ^(∗)Ω_(f) = ρ(γ)Ω_(f) for f ∈ ℳₙ(Γ ) . Proposition CP-H1. Exact Comparison with Ball Conventions Let q ∈ B = {|q| < 1} , z = Cq = (1 + q)(1 − q)^(− 1) , and let f_(B) be a ball-model spinor of weight n . Its half-space representative is , f(z) = 2^(− (n + 2)/2)|1 − q|²τₙ(Q(1 − q))f_(B)(q)., (4) For Γ = CΓ_(B)C^(− 1) this gives an isomorphism of regular automorphic cusp spaces with the transported rational structure. It satisfies , C^(∗)Ω_(f) = ρ(C)Ω_(f_(B)), ‖f‖_(Γ ,n)² = 2^(2 − n)‖f_(B)‖_(Γ_(B),n)²,, (5) where the ball norm is ∫_(Γ_(B) \ B)(1 − |q|²)^(n − 2)‖f_(B)(q)‖ₙ²dv(q) . If h^(B) is the coefficient metric of AC6, its transported half-space metric is h_(z)^(ℋ)(v₁,v₂) = h_(C^(− 1)z)^(B)(ρ(C)^(− 1)v₁,ρ(C)^(− 1)v₂), v₁,v₂ ∈ Eₘ. Discussion All constructions below use the half-space normalization (4). The ball formulation remains useful for compact-type decompositions and centered Poincaré seeds; CP-H1 gives the exact conversion, including the scalar that affects periods. Group cohomology is transported by the constant coefficient map ρ(C) , so the change of coordinates does not change the underlying correspondence.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Fourier Modes at a Cusp
text: Fourier Modes at a Cusp Proposition CP-M1. Polarized Fourier Expansion cf. [3, §3.1, Lemmas 1–3] Let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) , and assume infinity is a rational cusp with translation lattice Λ ⊂ ℝ³ . Put w = n + 2 and Λ^(∗) = {λ ∈ ℝ³ : ⟨ λ,μ ⟩ ∈ ℤ for every μ ∈ Λ }. There are vectors A_(λ) ∈ Vₙ such that , f(y + x) = ∑_(0 ≠ λ ∈ Λ^(∗))A_(λ)e^(− 2π|λ|y)e^(2πi ⟨ λ,x ⟩)., (M1) If (a_(λ),b_(λ))^(t) spans the positive eigenspace of the Hermitian matrix i Q(λ₁i + λ₂j + λ₃k) , then A_(λ) is a scalar multiple of (a_(λ)X + b_(λ)Y)ⁿ . Moreover , ‖f(y + x)‖ₙ ≤ C_(f)y^(− w/2), ‖A_(λ)‖ₙ ≤ C_(f)^(′)|λ|^(w/2)., (M2) The Fourier series and all its derivatives converge locally uniformly for y > 0 . Discussion All nonzero lattice directions occur in M1; the positive radial frequency is |λ| . Opposite directions have different polarization lines. Summing by |λ| can therefore discard directional information even when the complete Fourier expansion determines the form. The relation between Fueter regularity and polarized exponential modes also appears in [3, §3.1]; the symmetric-spinor calculation used here is the proof above.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Complete Mellin Transforms and Inversion
text: Complete Mellin Transforms and Inversion Proposition CP-M2. The Height Mellin Transform Let n ≥ 2 and let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) be a regular automorphic cusp form. Suppose 0 and ∞ are rational cusps of Γ . Let Λ be the translation lattice at infinity, let A_(λ) be the Fourier coefficients in the polarized expansion, and put w = n + 2 . Define Λ_(f)(s) = ∫₀^(∞)f(y)y^(s − 1) dy, D_(f)(s) = ∑_(0 ≠ λ ∈ Λ^(∗))A_(λ)|λ|^(− s). The first integral is entire in s ∈ ℂ . The series converges absolutely for Re s > w/2 + 3 , and in that half-plane , Λ_(f)(s) = (2π)^(− s)Γ (s)D_(f)(s)., (M3) Here Γ (s) = ∫₀^(∞)e^(− t)t^(s − 1)dt for Re s > 0 . With W = (0, 1; 1, 0) , one has , Λ_(f)(s) = Λ_(f|ₙW)(w − s), (M4) and , Λ_(f)(s) = ∫₁^(∞)(f(y)y^(s − 1) + (f|ₙW)(y)y^(w − s − 1)) dy., (M5) Discussion The series D_(f) is vector-valued and has positive real frequencies. When a scaling makes |λ|² integral, it can be grouped into ∑_(N)B_(N)N^(− s/2) . The construction and functional equation require no Hecke-eigenform assumption. An Euler product would be additional arithmetic structure, requiring a suitable scalar or algebra-valued coefficient system and multiplicativity. If W does not normalize Γ , M4 relates forms on conjugate lattices. In the eigencondition f|ₙW = ηf , it becomes Λ_(f)(s) = ηΛ_(f)(w − s) . Proposition CP-M3. Directional Complete Transforms Let n ≥ 2 and let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) be a regular automorphic cusp form, where 0 and ∞ are rational cusps of Γ . Write Λ for the translation lattice at infinity, A_(λ) for its Fourier coefficients, and w = n + 2 . Let ω = ω₀ + ω be a unit quaternion with ω₀ > 0 . Then ℳ_(f)(s;ω) = ∫₀^(∞)f(rω)r^(s − 1) dr is entire. For Re s > w/2 + 3 , , ℳ_(f)(s;ω) = (2π)^(− s)Γ (s)∑_(λ ≠ 0)A_(λ)(|λ|ω₀ − i ⟨ λ,ω ⟩ )^(− s)., (M6) The complex power uses the logarithm in the right half-plane. Its inversion law is , ℳ_(f|ₙW)(s;ω) = τₙ(Q(ω^(− 1)))ℳ_(f)(w − s;ω^(− 1))., (M7)

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Incomplete Mellin Integrals Give a Primitive
text: Incomplete Mellin Integrals Give a Primitive Let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) and assume infinity is a rational cusp. For y > 0 , x ∈ Im ℍ and s ∈ ℂ , define , M_(f)(s;x;y) = ∫_(y)^(∞)f(t + x)t^(s − 1) dt., (M8) Expand the polynomial map Zₘ(y + x) : Sym^(m) ℂ² → Eₘ as Zₘ(y + x) = ∑_(j = 0)^(m)y^(j)Pⱼ(x), Kₐ = 2ϵIₐ. Set , α_(f)(y + x) = − ∑_(a = 1)³∑_(j = 0)^(m)Pⱼ(x)Φ_(Kₐ)(M_(f)(j + 1;x;y)) dxₐ., (M9) Proposition CP-MC1. The Incomplete-Mellin Primitive Let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) and assume infinity is a rational cusp. The integral M8 is entire in s , and dα_(f) = Ω_(f) . It has the Fourier expression , M_(f)(s;x;y) = ∑_(λ ≠ 0)A_(λ)e^(2πi ⟨ λ,x ⟩)(2π|λ|)^(− s)Γ (s,2π|λ|y),, (M10) where Γ (s,u) = ∫ᵤ^(∞)e^(− t)t^(s − 1)dt for u > 0 . Discussion Here the word “incomplete” refers to the lower endpoint y . The horizontal point x need not be a boundary cusp. The arguments 1,…,n − 1 in M9 come from the polynomial coefficient embedding Zₘ ; the surface parameterization below gives a different list, 2,…,n .

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: From a Two-Form to a Cocycle of Periods
text: From a Two-Form to a Cocycle of Periods Proposition CP-M4. Triangle Periods and Their Relations Assume infinity is a rational cusp. Fix o ∈ ℋ and let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) . For g,k ∈ Γ , let [o,go,gko] be the oriented geodesic triangle and put , c_(f,o)(g,k) = ∫_([o,go,gko])Ω_(f) = ∫_(∂[o,go,gko])α_(f)., (M11) It satisfies , ρ(g)c_(f,o)(k,l) − c_(f,o)(gk,l) + c_(f,o)(g,kl) − c_(f,o)(g,k) = 0., (M12) Changing the base point changes c_(f,o) by a coboundary (δa)(g,k) = ρ(g)a(k) − a(gk) + a(g). Its class in H²(Γ ,Eₘ) is the class of Ω_(f) and determines f uniquely in Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) . Discussion A two-cocycle is a function of a pair of group elements. In a finite cellular description, its coordinates belong to two-cells, with compatibility equations from three-cells; they are also subject to changes by one-cochain coboundaries. The collection of incomplete-Mellin integrals in M11 is therefore organized by M12 into one cohomological object. For the classical full modular group, the corresponding differential form has degree one. In even weight, pass to PSL₂(ℤ) = ⟨ S,T : S² = (ST)³ = 1 ⟩ . A one-cocycle P with P(T) = 0 is determined by P(S) , because P(gk) = P(g) + ρ(g)P(k) . The relators still impose (1 + ρ(S))P(S) = 0, (1 + ρ(ST) + ρ(ST)²)P(S) = 0. These follow by applying the one-cocycle law to the two relators. Thus the single period polynomial retains the cocycle equations. This compression depends on the full modular group and its cusp normalization; it is not a property of every Fuchsian lattice. The quaternionic surface construction displays the higher cohomological degree explicitly.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Period Functions on Group Generators
text: Period Functions on Group Generators Proposition CP-M5. A Function-Valued Period Cocycle cf. [1, Thm. I.7.5, §§III.1, III.8]; [2, Thm. B] Let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) , assume infinity is a rational cusp, take α_(f) from CP-MC1, and fix o ∈ ℋ . Put A = C^(∞)(ℋ,Eₘ) with left action (T_(g)F)(z) = ρ(g)F(g^(− 1)z), and regard Eₘ as its submodule of constant functions. Define , b_(g)(z) = ∫_([o,z])(g^(∗)α_(f) − ρ(g)α_(f)), B_(g)(z) = b_(g)(g^(− 1)z), B̄_(g) = B_(g) mod Eₘ., (M13) The first integral is path-independent and the functions are real-analytic in the interior. They satisfy , b_(gk)(z) = b_(g)(kz) + ρ(g)bₖ(z) − b_(g)(ko),, (M14) , B̄_(gk) = B̄_(g) + T_(g)B̄ₖ., (M15) The constants κ_(f)(g,k) = b_(g)(ko) form an Eₘ -valued two-cocycle and , c_(f,o) = δa_(f) + κ_(f), a_(f)(g) = ∫_([o,go])α_(f)., (M16) For the connecting map of 0 → Eₘ → A → A/Eₘ → 0 , , ∂[B̄] = [κ_(f)] = [Ω_(f)]., (M17) The class [B̄] is independent of the primitive and its normalization, is zero after restriction to each cusp stabilizer, and determines f uniquely in the cusp space. Discussion The connecting map in M17 has a concrete meaning: choose representatives B_(g) of the function classes, take their group coboundary, and obtain constant coefficient vectors. Those constants recover the surface periods up to a coboundary. For a presentation Γ = ⟨ s₁,…,s_(d)|ℛ ⟩ , one function class per generator suffices for M15. For each relator r₁⋯r_(ℓ) = 1 , the functional equation is , ∑_(j = 1)^(ℓ)T_(r₁⋯r_(j − 1))B̄_(rⱼ) = 0, B̄_(s^(− 1)) = − T_(s^(− 1))B̄ₛ., (M18) These follow by repeated use of M15. They provide a function-valued description of the same form detected by the surface-period class. An independent analytic characterization of which generator functions arise from regular cusp forms remains a further question. Function-valued parabolic cocycles also occur in the classical Maass-form theory of [2], with different coefficient modules.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Cusp-Normalized Surface Periods
text: Cusp-Normalized Surface Periods Proposition CP-M6. Moving the Vertices to Cusps Let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) . For a rational cusp η set , c_(f,η)(g,k) = ∫_([η,gη,gkη])Ω_(f),, (M19) with value zero on degenerate triangles. This integral converges absolutely and satisfies M12. If a_(η,o)(g) = ∫_([η,o,go])Ω_(f) − ∫_([η,gη,go])Ω_(f), then c_(f,o) − c_(f,η) = δa_(η,o) . Moreover c_(f,η)(g,k) = 0 if either g or k fixes η . Proposition CP-M7. The Mellin Transform of an Ideal Triangle Let f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) and suppose 0,∞,au are cusps of Γ , where a > 0 and u is a unit imaginary quaternion. Orient T_(a,u) = [0,∞,au] by dy ∧ dt in z = y + tu . Put P_(f,a,u)(s) = ∫_(T_(a,u))(|z|/a)^(s)Ω_(f). This is entire and P_(f,a,u)(0) = ∫_(T_(a,u))Ω_(f) . Set ω_(θ) = cos θ + u sin θ, Zₘ(rω) = ∑_(j = 0)^(m)r^(j)Bⱼ(ω), Kᵤ = 2ϵQ(u), ℳ_(f)(v;ω;l,b) = ∫ₗ^(b)f(rω)r^(v − 1)dr. Then , P_(f,a,u)(s) = a^(− s)∑_(j = 0)^(m)∫₀^(π/2)Bⱼ(ω_(θ))Φ_(Kᵤ)(ℳ_(f)(s + j + 2;ω_(θ);a sin θ,a/ sin θ)) dθ., (M20) For a unit imaginary v perpendicular to u , put g_(a,u) = (0, av; a^(− 1)v, 0). It belongs to G , and the transforms satisfy , P_(f|ₙg_(a,u),a,u)(s) = − ρ(g_(a,u))^(− 1)P_(f,a,u)( − s)., (M21) Discussion For a fixed interior angle, the Fourier expression for the finite radial integral is a difference of incomplete gamma integrals. In particular, with μ_(λ)(ω) = 2π(|λ| Re ω − i ⟨ λ,Im ω ⟩ ), each mode contributes A_(λ)∫ₗ^(b)e^(− μ_(λ)(ω)r)r^(v − 1)dr. On compact angular subintervals the sums can be integrated term by term. At the cusp endpoint θ = π/2 , M20 is defined by the convergent integral of the original cusp form; an exchange with the Fourier sum needs an additional uniform estimate. At s = 0 , M20 uses the radial arguments 2,…,n . These values form the cocycle. For a freely varying s , the weighted form need not remain closed: d(r^(s)Ω_(f)) = sr^(s)d log r ∧ Ω_(f) . Thus M21 is a functional equation of surface transforms; M12 is the cocycle relation for their period values. The two assertions have different domains.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: A Nonzero Weight-Fourteen Example
text: A Nonzero Weight-Fourteen Example The following example specifies the lattice as well as the form. It uses an effective orientation-preserving group of hyperbolic four-space. At the even weights below, the central sign in its spin cover acts trivially on both spinors and flat coefficients. Thus all formulas are independent of a choice of sign for a lift. The group-cohomology comparison is unchanged by this finite central kernel over ℂ . Construction CP-E0. The Colored Reflection Group Let L = diag ( − 1,1,1,1,1) and ℍ_(L)⁴ = {v ∈ ℝ⁵ : v^(t)Lv = − 1, v₀ > 0}. Write e₀,…,e₄ for the coordinate vectors. For ν^(t)Lν = 1 , put r_(ν) = I − 2νν^(t)L . Set Aᵢ = r_(eᵢ), Bᵢⱼ = r_(e₀ + eᵢ + eⱼ) (1 ≤ i < j ≤ 4), W₂ = ⟨ Aᵢ,Bᵢⱼ ⟩ . Let ē₁,…,ē₄ be the basis of F₂⁴ . Define χ : W₂ → F₂⁴ by χ(Aᵢ) = ēᵢ and Pair (i,j) Color χ(Bᵢⱼ) (1,2) ē₁ (1,3) ē₃ (1,4) ē₄ (2,3) ē₂ (2,4) ē₁ + ē₂ + ē₃ (3,4) ē₁ + ē₂ + ē₄ Put Γ_(L) = ker χ . Identify v ∈ ℍ_(L)⁴ with the ball point q = (v₁ + v₂i + v₃j + v₄k)/(v₀ + 1), and then with z = Cq ∈ ℋ . Let Γ ⊂ G/{ ± I} be the resulting group acting on ℋ . Proposition CP-E1. Geometry and Congruence of the Example Group [4, §4, pp. 9–10] The color map in CP-E0 is a homomorphism. Its kernel is orientation-preserving, torsion-free, and has index 16 in W₂ . It contains the principal level-four subgroup W₄ = {g ∈ W₂ : g ≡ I (mod 4)}, [Γ_(L) : W₄] = 64. A fundamental domain is the regular ideal 24-cell obtained from the chamber P = {v ∈ ℍ_(L)⁴ : vᵢ ≥ 0, vᵢ + vⱼ ≤ v₀ (i < j)} by all sixteen spatial coordinate-sign changes. The boundary points 0,∞,i/2 are cusps of Γ . Proposition CP-E2. An Explicit Nonzero Poincaré Series [6, Lemma 4-2(i)] For v ∈ V₁₄ define the half-space seed and its periodization by , ϕᵥ(z) = 2⁸|z + 1|^(− 2)τ₁₄(Q((z + 1)^(− 1)))v, hᵥ(z) = ∑_(γ ∈ Γ)(ϕᵥ|₁₄γ)(z)., (E1) For either lift γ = (a_(γ), b_(γ); c_(γ), d_(γ)) , this is , hᵥ(z) = 2⁸∑_(γ ∈ Γ)|L_(γ)(z)|^(− 2)τ₁₄(Q(L_(γ)(z)^(− 1)))v, L_(γ)(z) = (a_(γ) + c_(γ))z + b_(γ) + d_(γ)., (E2) The series converges absolutely locally with derivatives and defines a regular cusp form. It satisfies , ‖hᵥ(1) − 2^(− 8)v‖₁₄ ≤ (3)/(4) 2^(− 8)‖v‖₁₄, ‖hᵥ(1)‖₁₄ ≥ 2^(− 10)‖v‖₁₄., (E3) In particular v ↦ hᵥ is injective. For W in CP-M2, , hᵥ|₁₄W = hᵥ, Λ_(hᵥ)(s) = Λ_(hᵥ)(16 − s)., (E4) Discussion E1–E2 specify the form without a Fourier-coefficient computation. For reproducible spin lifts, associate to a Lorentz vector ν = (ν₀,…,ν₄) the complex matrix C(ν) = (ν₀I_(2 × 2), − Q(ν₁ + ν₂i + ν₃j + ν₄k); Q(ν₁ + ν₂i + ν₃j + ν₄k)^(∗), − ν₀I_(2 × 2)). For an even reflection word, its product gives a ball spin lift, up to central sign; conjugate by R(C) to obtain the half-space lift. This prescription follows from the Clifford identity C(ν)² = − ν^(t)Lν I and its reflection-conjugation formula. At weight fourteen the two choices of sign give identical terms. The form h_(X¹⁴) is a specified nonzero cusp form; no Hecke-eigenvector choice is built into its definition. Proposition CP-E3. The (a,a) Period as a Surface Mellin Integral Let h = h_(X¹⁴) , E₁₂ = Sym¹² ℂ⁴ , and choose the element with half-space lift a = (0, − i; − i, − 2) ∈ G. Then a ∈ Γ , a∞ = 0 and a²∞ = i/2 . With c_(h,∞) from M19, , c_(h,∞)(a,a) = − P_(h,1/2,i)(0)., (E5) Writing ω_(θ) = cos θ + i sin θ and Z₁₂(rω) = ∑_(j = 0)¹²r^(j)Bⱼ(ω) , its value is , c_(h,∞)(a,a) = (4i)/(14 ⋅ 13)∑_(j = 0)¹²∫₀^(π/2)Bⱼ(ω_(θ))[∫_((1)/(2)sin θ)^((1)/(2 sin θ))h_(XY)(rω_(θ))r^(j + 1) dr]dθ., (E6) The formula is an equality in the 455 -dimensional coefficient space E₁₂ . Discussion This example involves thirteen radial Mellin arguments, 2,3,…,14 , with angle-dependent endpoints. Its height transform has the complete functional equation s ↔ 16 − s . The surface transform has the separate inversion equation M21, and its period value obeys the group relations M12. These are three explicit structures available for studying the same cusp form. The cusp-normalized representative in E5 is cohomologous to the interior-base-point representative by CP-M6. The nonvanishing result E3 proves that the full cohomology class is nonzero; it does not by itself assert that this particular (a,a) coordinate is nonzero. Formula E6 gives the coordinate exactly, without a numerical evaluation or an identification with special values of a scalar L-function.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: The Parabolic Condition for the Constructed Period Class
text: The Parabolic Condition for the Constructed Period Class Use the ordinary cohomology conventions and interior and parabolic cohomology. In the following statement, equation (7) is the subgroup-coboundary criterion. Proposition CP3. Cusp Forms Satisfy the Parabolic Cocycle Condition If f ∈ Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) , then [Ω_(f)] ∈ Hₚₐᵣ²(Γ ,Eₘ) . In particular its triangle-integral two-cocycle satisfies (7).

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Both Chiralities
text: Both Chiralities Let D₀ = diag (1, − 1) , θ(g) = D₀gD₀ , and r(z) = z̄ . Equip θΓ with the rational structure transported from that of Γ by θ . Define the complex vector space Sₙ⁺(Γ ) : = Sₙ^(−)(θΓ ) , with the following realization by differential forms on Γ \ ℋ . For f₊ ∈ Sₙ^(−)(θΓ ) set , Ω_(f₊)⁺ = Rₘ(D₀)^(− 1)r^(∗)Ω_(f₊)., (9) Proposition CP-C1. The Complementary Chirality Let n ≥ 2 and f₊ ∈ Sₙ^(−)(θΓ ) . The form Ω_(f₊)⁺ is closed, satisfies γ^(∗)Ω_(f₊)⁺ = ρ(γ)Ω_(f₊)⁺ for γ ∈ Γ , and satisfies ∗ Ω_(f₊)⁺ = Ω_(f₊)⁺ . The corresponding minimal compact type is Vₙ ⊠ V₀ . Discussion The plus space is not defined by complex-conjugating the coefficients of the minus space. Already at n = 2 , complex conjugation preserves anti-self-duality. Orientation reversal is the required operation. For a general lattice, θΓ need not equal Γ , and no equality of the two dimensions is assumed.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Hecke Operators and the Period Map
text: Hecke Operators and the Period Map Fix the data and identification (13) of CP7. For α ∈ G(ℚ) put Γ_(α) = Γ ∩ α^(− 1)Γ α, Y_(α) = Γ_(α) \ ℋ, and define finite covering maps p₁ : Y_(α) → X, [z] ↦ [z], p₂ : Y_(α) → X, [z] ↦ [αz]. Let ℰ_(m,L) be the local system on X associated to ρ_(m,L)|_(Γ) . Multiplication by ρ_(m,L)(α)^(− 1) defines a coefficient identification I_(α) : p₂^(∗)ℰ_(m,L) → p₁^(∗)ℰ_(m,L) . On H²(X,ℰ_(m,L)) set , T_(α) = (p₁)_(∗)I_(α)p₂^(∗),, (17) where (p₁)_(∗) is the cohomological trace, defined by summing over the sheets of the finite covering. For a = (a₁₁, a₁₂; a₂₁, a₂₂) ∈ G , write J(a,z) = a₂₁z + a₂₂ and define , (f|ₙa)(z) = |J(a,z)|^(− 2)τₙ(ι(J(a,z)^(− 1)))f(az)., (18) Construction CP-D4. Unnormalized Double-Coset Operators Choose the finite left-coset decomposition Γ αΓ = ∐ᵢΓ αᵢ . On the two cusp-spinor spaces set , T_(α)^(−)f_(−) = ∑ᵢf_(−)|ₙαᵢ, T_(α)⁺f₊ = ∑ᵢf₊|ₙθ(αᵢ),, (19) where f₊ ∈ Sₙ^(−)(θΓ ) = Sₙ⁺(Γ ) and θ is defined in CP-C1. Proposition CP8. Hecke Equivariance with Number-Field Coefficients For the data of CP-D4, T_(α) preserves H_(L) and is L -linear. The operators T_(α)^(±) are independent of the representatives in (19) and preserve Sₙ^(±)(Γ ) . For every smooth f : ℋ → Vₙ and every a ∈ G , , Ω_(f|ₙa) = Rₘ(a)^(− 1)a^(∗)Ω_(f)., (20) Write Φ (f_(−),f₊) = [Ω_(f_(−)) + Ω_(f₊)⁺] for the isomorphism of CP5. Then , Φ (T_(α)^(−)f_(−),T_(α)⁺f₊) = T_(α)Φ (f_(−),f₊)., (21) Consequently Φ^(− 1)(H_(L)) is an L -form of Sₙ^(−)(Γ ) ⊕︎ Sₙ⁺(Γ ) stable under every operator in (19). Discussion The normalization in (17)–(19) is a sum, with no division by the covering degree. Both the coefficient transport and this normalization matter when comparing with Hecke operators in other conventions. The rational elements here belong to G(ℚ) . Similitude Hecke operators extend the coefficient and slash actions, with separate cohomological and integral normalizations.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Algebraicity of Eigenvalues
text: Algebraicity of Eigenvalues Corollary CP9. Hecke Eigenvalues Lie in a Number Field Let Γ , n ≥ 2 , L , and H_(L) be as in CP7, and use the normalization in CP-D4. Let 0 ≠ f ∈ Sₙ^(ε)(Γ ) , with ε ∈ { − , + } . If T_(α)^(ε)f = λ_(α)f , then , det (λ_(α)id_(H_(L)) − T_(α)|_(H_(L))) = 0., (23) In particular λ_(α) is algebraic over ℚ . If {T_(α) : α ∈ A} is a commuting family of these operators and f is a simultaneous eigenvector, then , L_(f) = L(λ_(α) : α ∈ A), (24) is a finite extension of L . Discussion The algebraicity proof requires the injective period map and its Hecke equivariance; it does not require the surjectivity in CP5 or the exclusion of Eisenstein classes from interior cohomology. A Hecke-stable cohomology space over a number field is sufficient even if it contains additional classes. The L -structure in CP8 belongs to the sum of both chiralities. It does not by itself give an L -structure on each summand, or imply that the periods of an individual eigenform are algebraic. For odd n , CP7 even rules out a ℚ -model of the coefficient representation of this complex dimension. At n = 2 the coefficients are trivial and one may work over ℚ throughout. The n = 1 Hardy limit has no coefficient system E_(n − 2) in this construction. SH3 proves algebraic integrality for integral positive similitudes with a specified coefficient normalization. SH4 gives central counterexamples to an unrestricted integrality claim. Likewise, a scalar renormalization of each operator by an algebraic number preserves algebraicity of individual eigenvalues, but a common finite field for infinitely many operators requires control of all those normalization factors. Formula (24) applies to the explicit normalization above.

title: Cusp Forms, Mellin Transforms and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Further Arithmetic Questions
text: Further Arithmetic Questions Discussion The Mellin construction and weight-fourteen example above give explicit spinors and triangle periods. Further arithmetic questions include effective dimensions at n = 2,3,4 , explicit Hecke spectra, comparisons with adelic Hecke generators at each level, and the arithmetic of periods within each chirality. An integral coefficient lattice for the matrix-order semigroup is constructed in SH3. The Poincaré and theta-lift constructions provide places to start. Neither the correspondence nor the dimension formula asserts that every cusp form is an Arakawa theta lift.

title: Classical Cuspidal and Parabolic Cohomology
heading: Proposition CP2 · Parabolic Cohomology Is Interior Cohomology
text: CP2 Proposition CP2. Parabolic Cohomology Is Interior Cohomology [4, §§8, 15]; [5, Thm. I.7.5, §§III.1, III.8]; [7, Prop. 4.2.17, Cor. 4.2.18] Let G/ℚ be a simply connected semisimple group of rational rank one with G(ℝ) ≃ Sp(1,1) , and let Γ ⊂ G(ℚ) be a torsion-free congruence lattice. Put X = Γ \ ℋ and Eₘ = Sym^(m) ℂ⁴ , with m ≥ 0 . Then , Hₚₐᵣ²(Γ ,Eₘ) = H_(!)²(X,ℰₘ) : = im (H_(c)²(X,ℰₘ) → H²(X,ℰₘ))., (8) Truncate the finitely many cusps to obtain a compact manifold X̄ with boundary ∐_([ξ])Y_(ξ) . Each Y_(ξ) is a compact flat three-manifold with contractible universal cover and fundamental group Γ_(ξ) . The cusp collars identify the interior of X̄ with X ; the inclusion of a compact core into X is a homotopy equivalence. Extend ℰₘ over X̄ using the same monodromy representation. The relative exact sequence contains H¹(∂X̄,ℰₘ) → [δ []] H²(X̄,∂X̄;ℰₘ) → [j []] H²(X̄,ℰₘ) → [res []] H²(∂X̄,ℰₘ). Compact-support/relative comparison identifies the second term with H_(c)²(X,ℰₘ) ; homotopy invariance identifies the third with H²(X,ℰₘ) . Under these identifications j is j_(c) . The aspherical boundary components identify the last term with ⨁_([ξ])H²(Γ_(ξ),Eₘ) , and their inclusions identify res with the restriction map in (6). Exactness gives Hₚₐᵣ² = ker (res) = im (j_(c)) = H_(!)². The same sequence gives ker (j_(c)) = im (δ) , specifying exactly where compactly supported classes can disappear in ordinary cohomology.

The Lie algebra acts diagonally on V ⊗ Eₘ . Its differential, evaluated on T₀,…,Tⱼ ∈ p_(ℂ) , is (dω)(T₀,…,Tⱼ) = ∑_(i = 0)^(j)( − 1)ⁱTᵢ ⋅ ω(T₀,…,T̂ᵢ,…,Tⱼ). The hat denotes omission of an argument. Denote the cohomology of this complex by H^(j)(g,K;V ⊗ Eₘ) .
