title: Automorphic cohomology and geometric realization
heading: Overview
text: Research What survives of the modular-curve construction on a quaternionic quotient, including a real family of abelian varieties and the obstruction to a Jacobian realization. Automorphic cohomology and geometric realization Discussion For the quaternionic ball, flat coefficients, closed differential forms, periods, and Hecke correspondences survive. Even a real-analytic family of polarized abelian varieties can be constructed, as GE3 shows. The obstruction is to interpreting this homogeneous construction as a holomorphic algebraic family over the ball quotient. The arithmetic realization presently available through LG3 instead uses the different geometry of a Siegel modular threefold.

title: Automorphic cohomology and geometric realization
heading: Proposition GE2 · No invariant almost complex structure on the ball
text: GE2 Proposition GE2. No invariant almost complex structure on the ball For G = Sp(1,1) , K = Sp(1) × Sp(1) , and B = G/K , one has End_(K) (T₀B) = ℝ id. Consequently B has no G -invariant almost complex structure. Identify T₀B with ℍ , where (a,b) ∈ K acts by v ↦ avb^(− 1) . A real-linear map commuting with all left multiplications by unit quaternions commutes with left multiplication by all quaternions. It is therefore right multiplication by c = A(1) . Commuting also with right multiplication by every unit quaternion forces c to be real. An invariant almost complex structure would give such an endomorphism with square − id , impossible for a real scalar.

title: Automorphic cohomology and geometric realization
heading: Proposition GE3 · A torus family with polarized fibres and Hecke isogenies
text: GE3 Proposition GE3. A torus family with polarized fibres and Hecke isogenies cf. [1, Ch. I, Thm. 2.8] Let D/ℚ be a definite quaternion algebra, O an order in D , V_(ℚ) = D² , Λ = O² , and h(v,w) = v̄₁w₁ − v̄₂w₂. Let G = Sp(h_(ℝ)) ≃ Sp(1,1) , let K = Sp(1) × Sp(1) be its block-diagonal compact subgroup, and put B = G/K . Let Γ be a torsion-free finite-index subgroup of the rational isometries of h preserving Λ . Choose a nonzero u ∈ O of reduced trace zero, put u² = − d with d ∈ ℚ_(> 0) , and write i = u/√(d) in D ⊗ ℝ ≃ ℍ . Define ψ(v,w) = Trd_(D/ℚ) (uh(v,w)), J₀(v₁,v₂) = ( − v₁i,v₂i). Extend ψ to V_(ℝ) by real bilinearity. For x = gK ∈ B , set Jₓ = gJ₀g^(− 1) . Then: ψ is a nondegenerate alternating rational form, integral on Λ , and Jₓ is well-defined. The complex torus Aₓ = (V_(ℝ),Jₓ)/Λ is a polarized abelian variety of complex dimension four, with Riemann form ψ . The quotient A = Γ \ (B × (V_(ℝ)/Λ )) ⟶ Γ \ B, γ(x,[v]) = (γx,[γv]), is a real-analytic family with fibres Aₓ and locally constant first homology Λ . If α ∈ M₂(O) is invertible over D and satisfies h(αv,αw) = νh(v,w) with ν ∈ ℚ_(> 0) , then [v] ↦ [αv] is a holomorphic isogeny Aₓ → A_(αx) , and its pullback multiplies the Riemann form by ν . For an order in a quaternion algebra, reduced traces and norms are integers and conjugation preserves the order. Thus ψ(Λ ,Λ ) ⊂ ℤ . Since ū = − u and h(w,v) = overline(h(v,w)) , invariance of reduced trace under conjugation and cyclic permutation gives ψ(w,v) = − ψ(v,w) . The operator J₀ squares to − 1 and commutes with the block-diagonal compact group K , proving well-definedness of Jₓ . Direct multiplication gives ψ(J₀v,J₀w) = ψ(v,w), ψ(v,J₀v) = 2√(d) (|v₁|² + |v₂|²) > 0 (v ≠ 0). For the first identity use h(J₀v,J₀w) = − ih(v,w)i and cyclicity of trace. These identities also prove nondegeneracy of ψ . Because g preserves h , it preserves ψ , so the same compatibility and positivity hold for every Jₓ . The Riemann bilinear criterion makes each complex torus projective, of dimension dim_(ℝ) V_(ℝ)/2 = 4 . The formula J_(γx) = γJₓγ^(− 1) makes the fibre complex structures and polarizations descend to the smooth torus bundle. Analytic local sections of G → G/K show real-analytic dependence on x . Finally α/√(ν) ∈ G , so J_(αx) = αJₓα^(− 1) . Since αΛ ⊂ Λ has finite index, the induced complex-linear map is an isogeny. Its polarization formula is ψ(αv,αw) = νψ(v,w) .

title: Automorphic cohomology and geometric realization
heading: The quaternionic differential-form construction
text: The quaternionic differential-form construction Discussion Let M = Γ \ B , where B = Sp(1,1)/(Sp(1) × Sp(1)) , and retain the hypotheses of AC7 for cuspidal injectivity. For n ≥ 2 , put m = n − 2 and Eₘ = Sym^(m) ℂ⁴ . The explicit construction gives f ⟼ Ω_(f) ∈ Ω²(M,ℰₘ), d_(∇)Ω_(f) = 0, and hence a Hecke-compatible class in Hₚₐᵣ²(Γ ,Eₘ) . The decomposition n = (n − 2) + 2 has a precise local meaning. For the relevant rank-two spinor bundle S^(−) , Symⁿ S^(−) ⟶ Sym^(n − 2) S^(−) ⊗ Sym² S^(−) ≃ Sym^(n − 2) S^(−) ⊗ Λ_(−)²T^(∗)M_(ℂ). The moving inclusion S^(−) ↪ ℰ₁ then gives the flat-coefficient two-form. Here Λ_(−)² denotes the anti-self-dual two-forms for the stated orientation. The maps, connection derivatives, and closedness calculation are AC2–AC5. This is a decomposition into a coefficient tensor and a real differential two-form. It does not itself identify a holomorphic Hodge bundle or a Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism. In particular, the Hodge star on two-forms in real dimension four has square + 1 : its self-dual/anti-self-dual splitting is not the complex structure supplied by the Hodge star on one-forms of a Riemann surface. Proposition GE2. No invariant almost complex structure on the ball For G = Sp(1,1) , K = Sp(1) × Sp(1) , and B = G/K , one has End_(K) (T₀B) = ℝ id. Consequently B has no G -invariant almost complex structure. Discussion This is the homogeneous obstruction: the quaternionic symmetric space cannot be the Hermitian symmetric domain of a Shimura datum. It does not claim that every individual quotient admits no conceivable unrelated complex structure. It does rule out the direct analogue with the natural transitive group action and homogeneous Hodge bundles.

title: Automorphic cohomology and geometric realization
heading: A real family of polarized abelian fourfolds
text: A real family of polarized abelian fourfolds Proposition GE3. A torus family with polarized fibres and Hecke isogenies cf. [1, Ch. I, Thm. 2.8] Let D/ℚ be a definite quaternion algebra, O an order in D , V_(ℚ) = D² , Λ = O² , and h(v,w) = v̄₁w₁ − v̄₂w₂. Let G = Sp(h_(ℝ)) ≃ Sp(1,1) , let K = Sp(1) × Sp(1) be its block-diagonal compact subgroup, and put B = G/K . Let Γ be a torsion-free finite-index subgroup of the rational isometries of h preserving Λ . Choose a nonzero u ∈ O of reduced trace zero, put u² = − d with d ∈ ℚ_(> 0) , and write i = u/√(d) in D ⊗ ℝ ≃ ℍ . Define ψ(v,w) = Trd_(D/ℚ) (uh(v,w)), J₀(v₁,v₂) = ( − v₁i,v₂i). Extend ψ to V_(ℝ) by real bilinearity. For x = gK ∈ B , set Jₓ = gJ₀g^(− 1) . Then: ψ is a nondegenerate alternating rational form, integral on Λ , and Jₓ is well-defined. The complex torus Aₓ = (V_(ℝ),Jₓ)/Λ is a polarized abelian variety of complex dimension four, with Riemann form ψ . The quotient A = Γ \ (B × (V_(ℝ)/Λ )) ⟶ Γ \ B, γ(x,[v]) = (γx,[γv]), is a real-analytic family with fibres Aₓ and locally constant first homology Λ . If α ∈ M₂(O) is invertible over D and satisfies h(αv,αw) = νh(v,w) with ν ∈ ℚ_(> 0) , then [v] ↦ [αv] is a holomorphic isogeny Aₓ → A_(αx) , and its pullback multiplies the Riemann form by ν . Discussion GE3 depends on the chosen lattice and imaginary quaternion u . It supplies abelian varieties as fibres and isogenies above the usual Hecke correspondences. It is not a universal algebraic family over a number field: the base is a real manifold, and the construction gives a smooth, varying complex structure only in the vertical directions. No arithmetic model of this family or Galois action on the base cohomology follows from it. Its rational first-homology local system has rank eight. After complexification, D ⊗ ℂ ≃ M₂(ℂ) splits D² ⊗ ℂ into two standard four-dimensional summands. Thus the complex coefficient representation used for spinors is closely related to this torus bundle, but it must not be called a rational rank-four first-cohomology bundle without additional descent data.

title: Classical Automorphic Geometry and Hodge Weights
heading: Proposition GE1 · The Hodge bundle and the two units of modular weight
text: GE1 Proposition GE1. The Hodge bundle and the two units of modular weight [2, Thm. 10.13.11] Let N ≥ 5 , let Y = Y₁(N)_(ℂ) , let X = X₁(N)_(ℂ) be its smooth compactification, and let C = X ∖ Y be the reduced cusp divisor. For the universal elliptic curve π : ℰ → Y , let ℋ_(dR) = R¹π_(∗)Ω_(ℰ/Y)^(∙), ω = π_(∗)Ω_(ℰ/Y)¹. Write ω also for its canonical extension over X . The Hodge filtration and the Kodaira–Spencer map give 0 ⟶ ω ⟶ ℋ_(dR) ⟶ ω^(− 1) ⟶ 0 on Y, ω^(⊗ 2) ≃ Ω_(X)¹(log C). For every integer k ≥ 2 , Sₖ(Γ₁(N)) = H⁰(X,ω^(⊗ k)( − C)) ≃ H⁰(X,ω^(⊗ (k − 2)) ⊗ Ω_(X)¹). The first exact sequence is the degree-one Hodge–de Rham sequence, with its quotient identified by the principal polarization and relative Serre duality. The Gauss–Manin connection followed by projection induces ω ⟶ (ℋ_(dR)/ω) ⊗ Ω_(Y)¹ ≃ ω^(− 1) ⊗ Ω_(Y)¹. For the fine elliptic moduli problem this map is an isomorphism; its extension across the cusps is exactly the cited Kodaira–Spencer theorem. Thus ω²( − C) ≃ Ω_(X)¹ . Tensoring by ω^(k − 2) and taking global sections proves the assertion, using the definition of cusp forms as sections vanishing on C .

title: Classical Automorphic Geometry and Hodge Weights
heading: Theorem GE-J · The weight-two Jacobian quotient
text: GE-J Theorem GE-J. The weight-two Jacobian quotient [6, Thm. 7.14]; [3, §2, p. 4] Let f ∈ S₂(Γ₁(N)) be a normalized cuspidal newform, let E_(f) be its Fourier-coefficient field, let J = Jac (X₁(N)) over ℚ , and let T ⊂ End_(ℚ) (J) be the Hecke algebra. Put I_(f) = ker (T ⟶ E_(f)), B_(f) = I_(f)J, A_(f) = J/B_(f), where I_(f)J is the connected abelian subvariety generated by the images of the endomorphisms in I_(f) . Then dim A_(f) = [E_(f) : ℚ], codim_(J) B_(f) = [E_(f) : ℚ]. In particular, if E_(f) = ℚ , then A_(f) is an elliptic curve over ℚ . The construction and its newform multiplicity-one input are imported from the cited classical theorem. To see the dimension mechanism, the cotangent space of J is H⁰(X₁(N),Ω¹) = S₂(Γ₁(N)) . The cotangent space of the newform quotient is the span of the Galois conjugates of f , one dimension for each embedding of E_(f) in ℂ . Its dimension is therefore [E_(f) : ℚ] . Since A_(f) is an abelian variety defined over ℚ , dimension one gives an elliptic curve with its identity as rational origin.

title: Classical Automorphic Geometry and Hodge Weights
heading: Proposition GE4 · The Siegel Hodge bundle and the cohomological degree
text: GE4 Proposition GE4. The Siegel Hodge bundle and the cohomological degree [4, Prop. 5.10.1]; [7, Thm. 1.4] Let S be a fine Siegel modular threefold over a number field, with universal principally polarized abelian surface π : U → S . Let ℍ = R¹π_(∗)ℚ on S(ℂ) and let ℱ = π_(∗)Ω_(U/S)¹ be its rank-two Hodge bundle. Then Ω_(S)¹ ≃ Sym² ℱ, Ω_(S)³ ≃ (det ℱ)³. For m ≥ 0 , the automorphic bundle of Siegel weight (m + 3,3) is Sym^(m) ℱ ⊗ (det ℱ)³ ≃ Sym^(m) ℱ ⊗ Ω_(S)³. For m ≥ 1 , H³(S(ℂ),Sym^(m) ℍ) is a subquotient of H^(m + 3)(U_(S)^(m)(ℂ),ℚ) . The analogous statement holds for geometric étale cohomology over the number field, equivariantly for its absolute Galois group. For m = 0 , the corresponding group is H³(S) itself. The polarized Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism gives Ω_(S)¹ ≃ Sym² ℱ . On a diagonal change of basis with eigenvalues a,b , the determinant of its action on Sym² ℱ is a²(ab)b² = (ab)³ . This proves the canonical-bundle identity and hence the automorphic-bundle formula. For πₘ : U_(S)^(m) → S , relative Künneth identifies ℍ^(⊗ m) as the direct summand of R^(m)π_(m ∗)ℚ of degree one in each factor. Rational symmetrization gives its direct summand Sym^(m) ℍ . This construction also exists in the geometric étale local systems. If implemented by permuting factors on the total cohomology, the degree-one Koszul signs must be included. The Leray spectral sequence has terms H^(a)(S,R^(b)π_(m ∗)ℚ) and converges to H^(a + b)(U_(S)^(m),ℚ) . Multiplication by a fixed integer r > 1 on the abelian fibres acts by r^(b) on R^(b) . A differential dₜ , t ≥ 2 , changes b to b − t + 1 , so its source and target have different eigenvalues and it is zero. Thus the spectral sequence degenerates, and its (3,m) term is a subquotient in total degree m + 3 . The same argument applies étale. The relative motivic construction underlying these coefficient summands is the external theorem of Ancona recalled in Wildeshaus Theorem 1.4.

title: Classical Automorphic Geometry and Hodge Weights
heading: Proposition GE5 · The Hodge–Tate obstruction to first cohomology
text: GE5 Proposition GE5. The Hodge–Tate obstruction to first cohomology [1, Thm. 2.2.3, §2.4] Let n ≥ 2 and let r be a four-dimensional de Rham representation of the absolute Galois group of a number field, with Hodge–Tate multiset {0,1,n,n + 1} at one embedding. For every integer Tate twist t , neither r(t) nor r^(∨)(t) is isomorphic to a subquotient of the first étale cohomology of an abelian variety, or its dual, over a finite extension of that field. The Hodge–Tate weights of first cohomology of an abelian variety are two consecutive integers, with the sign determined by the cyclotomic convention; its dual has the opposite pair. Every subquotient has weights drawn from that pair. The difference between the largest and smallest weights of r is n + 1 ≥ 3 . Integer twisting translates all weights by the same amount; duality reverses them; finite extension does not remove the weight multiset at an extending embedding. The difference therefore remains n + 1 and cannot be at most one.

title: Classical Automorphic Geometry and Hodge Weights
heading: The classical weight shift
text: The classical weight shift Proposition GE1. The Hodge bundle and the two units of modular weight [2, Thm. 10.13.11] Let N ≥ 5 , let Y = Y₁(N)_(ℂ) , let X = X₁(N)_(ℂ) be its smooth compactification, and let C = X ∖ Y be the reduced cusp divisor. For the universal elliptic curve π : ℰ → Y , let ℋ_(dR) = R¹π_(∗)Ω_(ℰ/Y)^(∙), ω = π_(∗)Ω_(ℰ/Y)¹. Write ω also for its canonical extension over X . The Hodge filtration and the Kodaira–Spencer map give 0 ⟶ ω ⟶ ℋ_(dR) ⟶ ω^(− 1) ⟶ 0 on Y, ω^(⊗ 2) ≃ Ω_(X)¹(log C). For every integer k ≥ 2 , Sₖ(Γ₁(N)) = H⁰(X,ω^(⊗ k)( − C)) ≃ H⁰(X,ω^(⊗ (k − 2)) ⊗ Ω_(X)¹). Discussion The bundle ω consists of invariant cotangent vectors of the elliptic fibres. Its square is the cotangent bundle of the modular curve, with the cusp correction. The Gauss–Manin connection is essential to this identification. The rank-two local system ℍ = R¹π_(∗)ℚ has this Hodge filtration. The geometric coefficient underlying a weight- k eigenform is Sym^(k − 2) ℍ , and the relevant cohomology is Hₚₐᵣ¹(Y,Sym^(k − 2) ℍ) . For k > 2 , Scholl's [5, Thm. 1.2.1] realizes it by a projector in degree k − 1 of a compactified (k − 2) -fold fibre product of the universal elliptic curve. Thus the general construction already uses higher cohomology rather than a quotient of a Jacobian. Theorem GE-J. The weight-two Jacobian quotient [6, Thm. 7.14]; [3, §2, p. 4] Let f ∈ S₂(Γ₁(N)) be a normalized cuspidal newform, let E_(f) be its Fourier-coefficient field, let J = Jac (X₁(N)) over ℚ , and let T ⊂ End_(ℚ) (J) be the Hecke algebra. Put I_(f) = ker (T ⟶ E_(f)), B_(f) = I_(f)J, A_(f) = J/B_(f), where I_(f)J is the connected abelian subvariety generated by the images of the endomorphisms in I_(f) . Then dim A_(f) = [E_(f) : ℚ], codim_(J) B_(f) = [E_(f) : ℚ]. In particular, if E_(f) = ℚ , then A_(f) is an elliptic curve over ℚ . Discussion A single complex eigenline need not define an abelian subvariety over ℚ . The full Galois orbit is used. The kernel has codimension one precisely in the rational-coefficient case of this construction, not for every weight-two newform.

title: Classical Automorphic Geometry and Hodge Weights
heading: Geometry after transfer to the split group
text: Geometry after transfer to the split group Proposition GE4. The Siegel Hodge bundle and the cohomological degree [4, Prop. 5.10.1]; [7, Thm. 1.4] Let S be a fine Siegel modular threefold over a number field, with universal principally polarized abelian surface π : U → S . Let ℍ = R¹π_(∗)ℚ on S(ℂ) and let ℱ = π_(∗)Ω_(U/S)¹ be its rank-two Hodge bundle. Then Ω_(S)¹ ≃ Sym² ℱ, Ω_(S)³ ≃ (det ℱ)³. For m ≥ 0 , the automorphic bundle of Siegel weight (m + 3,3) is Sym^(m) ℱ ⊗ (det ℱ)³ ≃ Sym^(m) ℱ ⊗ Ω_(S)³. For m ≥ 1 , H³(S(ℂ),Sym^(m) ℍ) is a subquotient of H^(m + 3)(U_(S)^(m)(ℂ),ℚ) . The analogous statement holds for geometric étale cohomology over the number field, equivariantly for its absolute Galois group. For m = 0 , the corresponding group is H³(S) itself. Discussion For the transferred spinor family, m = n − 2 , so the split geometry places the coefficient cohomology in total degree m + 3 = n + 1 . This explains the weight n + 1 of LG3. Boundary conditions and Hecke eigenspaces must still be imposed using the published cuspidal/intersection-cohomology construction. GE4 alone does not isolate an individual eigenform. The transfer matches Hecke systems on the quaternionic quotient and the Siegel threefold. It supplies no canonical map identifying their degree-two and degree-three cohomology groups or their periods. In particular, the real family in GE3, whose fibres have dimension four, is a different construction from the universal abelian surface used in GE4. An étale cohomological realization is also weaker than an explicit Chow motive cut out by an algebraic idempotent on a smooth projective variety. Wildeshaus's intersection-motive theorem requires derived highest weight (a,b) with a > b > 0 . Our coefficient (m,0) is outside that range for every m . Its relative coefficient motive is covered by Theorem 1.4, but the absolute intersection-motive conclusion cannot simply be imported. This is a limit of that particular theorem, not a nonexistence assertion about motives in these weights. Betti Hodge weights in this geometric discussion use ordinary cohomology. When comparing with the arithmetic-Frobenius Galois normalization of LG3, duals and the specified central twists must be respected. They do not change the cohomological-degree explanation or the Hodge–Tate obstruction below.

title: Classical Automorphic Geometry and Hodge Weights
heading: Why an abelian-variety quotient is the wrong target
text: Why an abelian-variety quotient is the wrong target Proposition GE5. The Hodge–Tate obstruction to first cohomology [1, Thm. 2.2.3, §2.4] Let n ≥ 2 and let r be a four-dimensional de Rham representation of the absolute Galois group of a number field, with Hodge–Tate multiset {0,1,n,n + 1} at one embedding. For every integer Tate twist t , neither r(t) nor r^(∨)(t) is isomorphic to a subquotient of the first étale cohomology of an abelian variety, or its dual, over a finite extension of that field. Discussion At n = 2 , a geometric pure realization would have Hodge types (3,0),(2,1),(1,2),(0,3) , each with multiplicity one. These are of Calabi–Yau-threefold type as Hodge numbers; this observation does not produce a Calabi–Yau threefold, and the separate transfer qualification at n = 2 in LG3 remains in force. The useful geometric questions are consequently about higher cohomology, algebraic correspondences, and period comparisons. An explicit relation between quaternionic two-form periods and the Siegel realization would add information beyond the existence of an algebraic Hecke spectrum. Neither an algebraic cycle realizing that comparison nor a compatible identity of periods has been constructed here.

title: Sources and further reading
heading: Overview
text: Expository Literature on Fueter regularity, quaternionic elliptic functions, lattice sums, and number-theoretic connections. Sources and further reading This guide collects literature for the foundations, elliptic functions, representation constructions, and special-value formulas. It focuses on Fueter-regular and monogenic functions. Works using other analytic settings are identified separately where relevant. The notes record the scope of reading, not a verdict on correctness. “Metadata” means publication details were checked; “abstract” or “selected passages” identifies how much mathematical content was inspected. No entry here represents a completed proof audit. The initial selection dates from 17 October 2026. Article-local bibliographies, added on 29 October 2026, identify sources at the statements and proofs that use them; this reading guide supplements those citations.

title: Sources and further reading
heading: Attribution of the construction
text: Attribution of the construction The quaternionic Weierstrass construction is due to Fueter. A directly inspected reference is Kraußhar (2001), §4, p. 1019, equation (12): the regularized derivative lattice sum is displayed there, with its quaternionic case credited to Fueter (1939), reference [16]. Read the passage. A detailed comparison with Fueter's original formulas is still needed, especially for the zeta normalization and quasi-period conventions. The proofs in this wiki concern the exact formulations displayed here; a historical citation does not verify those proofs.

title: Sources and further reading
heading: Further comparisons
text: Further comparisons A detailed historical comparison of E-C1 and E-C2 with Fueter's original definitions remains useful, especially for kernel normalization, left/right conventions, and the zeta subtraction. The 1945 multiplication note is a separate starting point for the arithmetic action. The convergent harmonic theta and critical-value formulas now appear in TH1–TH5. Order-one regularization, arithmetic multiplication, and a direct relation between the ball and lattice representations remain open. The references here distinguish the published inputs from those questions.

title: Sources and further reading
heading: Langlands and Galois representations
text: Langlands and Galois representations Work Role and precise use Reading so far Mirko Rösner and Rainer Weissauer (2024), Global liftings between inner forms of GSp(4), J. Number Theory 263, 79–138. Author version, arXiv v2. Proposition 8.3 checks the quaternionic cohomological weight; Proposition 10.1 allows the split packet change; Theorem 11.5 gives the general-type transfer used in LG3. Retained v2, 21 June 2023, 59 pages. §§1, 8–11 and selected §12 statements inspected; pp. 35 and 46–47 contain the crucial restrictions. Theorem 11.4 is for the compact real inner form and is not used for Sp(1,1). Full trace-formula proof not independently audited. Ariel Weiss (2022), On the images of Galois representations attached to low weight Siegel modular forms, J. London Math. Soc. 106, 358–387. Author version, arXiv v5. §§2.1–2.2 give the archimedean parameter/weight convention; Theorem 3.1 and Remark 3.2 give cohomological Galois existence, normalization, Hodge–Tate weights, purity and irreducibility. Retained final author version, 9 December 2021, 25 pages; §§2–3 inspected and theorem page 6 visually checked. This is a primary research paper summarizing the earlier existence theorems; their complete proofs are not reverified here. Taylor; Laumon; Rainer Weissauer. Richard Taylor, On the ℓ-adic cohomology of Siegel threefolds, Invent. Math. 114 (1993), 289–310; Gérard Laumon, Fonctions zêtas des variétés de Siegel de dimension trois, Astérisque 302 (2005), 1–66; Rainer Weissauer, Four dimensional Galois representations, Astérisque 302 (2005), 67–150. Original geometric construction underlying the cohomological case of Weiss Theorem 3.1. Attribution and bibliography read in Weiss; original construction proofs not inspected in this investigation. Pierre Deligne (1971), Formes modulaires et représentations ℓ-adiques, Séminaire Bourbaki 1968/69, exposé 355, 139–172. Two-dimensional Galois representations of holomorphic cuspidal eigenforms, used as the external input in LG5. Classical theorem imported as a named dependency; its original proof and modern p-adic Hodge-theoretic refinements have not been audited here.

title: Sources and further reading
heading: Moduli spaces, universal families, and motives
text: Moduli spaces, universal families, and motives Work Role and precise use Reading so far Nicholas Katz and Barry Mazur (1985), Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves, Annals of Mathematics Studies 108. Theorem 10.13.11 gives the logarithmic extension of the elliptic Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism used in GE1. The theorem and preceding construction on printed pp.334–335 inspected through the accessible scan; complete book proof not audited. Kenneth Ribet (1992 preprint; 2004 publication), Abelian varieties over Q and modular forms, in Modular Curves and Abelian Varieties, 241–261. Classical association of abelian varieties to weight-two newforms and the GL₂-type context for GE-J. Retained arXiv v1, 18 pages; §2, especially p.4, explicitly states the newform quotient construction, its dimension, and its source in Shimura Theorem 7.14. The original general proof has not been audited here. A. J. Scholl (1990), Motives for modular forms, Invent. Math. 100, 419–430. §1.2, especially Theorem 1.2.1, places parabolic coefficient cohomology in a projector summand of Kuga–Sato cohomology. Author-hosted 10-page version retained; introduction and §§1.0–1.2 inspected. The desingularization and full projector proof have not been audited. Damien Robert (2023 draft), Theory of abelian varieties and their moduli spaces, draft 7 March 2023. §5.10, especially Proposition 5.10.1, gives the polarized Kodaira–Spencer map and its Siegel analytic model; used in GE4. 119-page author draft retained; printed pp.59–60 inspected. Underlying Faltings–Chai and Andreatta results are cited there rather than independently audited here. Jörg Wildeshaus (2019), On the intersection motive of certain Shimura varieties: the case of Siegel threefolds, Annals of K-Theory 4, 525–558; arXiv v3. Theorem 1.4 recalls Ancona's relative motivic construction from the universal abelian surface. Theorem 1.6 and its regularity restriction prevent an unjustified application of the absolute intersection-motive theorem to coefficients (m,0) . 36-page v3 retained; introduction and §1 through Theorem 1.6 inspected. Full boundary computation not audited.

title: Sources and further reading
heading: Half-space geometry and Mellin period functions
text: Half-space geometry and Mellin period functions Work Role and precise use Reading so far David A. Vogan, Jr. (1981), Representations of Real Reductive Lie Groups, introductory chapter, §0.2. The Harish-Chandra isomorphism identifies the center of the enveloping algebra with Weyl-invariant polynomials. Used for the two central generators and the finite differential test. The map, isomorphism statement and infinitesimal-character convention in 0.2.7–0.2.9 inspected. The degree-two and degree-four generators follow from the signed-permutation Weyl group in type C₂ ; the finite-span criterion is proved in the article. Jouni Parkkonen and Frédéric Paulin (2019), Counting and equidistribution in quaternionic Heisenberg groups. §§3 and 6 give Siegel-domain, horospherical and Heisenberg conventions, compared with QH1–QH3. The model, metric (8), coordinates (18) and Heisenberg law inspected. The arithmetic counting theorems are not used. The matrix and Cayley identities in QH1–QH3 are proved directly. Denis Constales and Rolf Sören Kraußhar (2002), Representation Formulas for the General Derivatives of the Fundamental Solution to the Cauchy–Riemann Operator in Clifford Analysis and Applications. Z. Anal. Anwendungen 21, 579–597. §3.1, Lemmas 1–3: Fourier plane waves and Clifford regularity. Related to the spinor Fourier calculation CP-M1. Introduction pp.580–581 and those lemmas inspected. The symmetric-spinor and cusp estimates used here are proved in CP-M1. Roelof Bruggeman, John Lewis and Don Zagier (2013 author version), Period functions for Maass wave forms and cohomology. A comparison for function-valued parabolic cocycles and automorphic reconstruction. Introduction pp.3–6 and Theorem B inspected. Its group and coefficient modules differ from those of CP-M5; that quaternionic construction is proved separately. Dubravko Ivanšić, Hyperbolic structure on a complement of tori in the 4-sphere, author version. §4 describes the ten-reflection level-two group and ideal 24-cell, used in CP-E1. It attributes the reflection-group identification to Ratcliffe–Tschantz, The Volume Spectrum of Hyperbolic 4-Manifolds, Experimental Mathematics 9 (2000), 101–125. PDF pp.9–10 inspected. The original Ratcliffe–Tschantz full proof was not independently audited. The particular color kernel, congruence condition and nonvanishing estimate are calculated in CP-E1–CP-E2.

title: Review of Parabolic Cohomology and Compact Support
heading: Overview
text: Scope and evidence for the review of the cusp restriction exact sequence and its proof. Review of Parabolic Cohomology and Compact Support The mathematical baseline of the article received an independent AI review on 18 October 2026. A separate reviewing agent first read the exposition without the author's research notes, then checked the argument and the cited source passages. The final check of that baseline found no unresolved mathematical or editorial defect within the scope below. The current editorial revision is described separately below. This records an AI review, rather than a review by a human mathematician or a proof-assistant verification.

title: Review of Parabolic Cohomology and Compact Support
heading: Reviewed Content
text: Reviewed Content The review covers the definitions of interior cohomology and parabolic cohomology, and the cusp restriction exact sequence, each in formulation version 1. It includes both presentations of the proof, the torus-cusp example, and the conditional application to automorphic cohomology. The checks addressed the group and flat-bundle coefficient conventions; compatibility of subgroup restriction with restriction to cusp cross-sections; the relative and compact-support comparison in both directions; the connecting map; and the cutoff construction. The concise and expanded proofs were checked to follow the same argument.

title: Review of Parabolic Cohomology and Compact Support
heading: Sources and Scope
text: Sources and Scope The reviewer inspected the cited passages in Brown's Cohomology of Groups, Bott–Tu's Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology, and Martelli's revised An Introduction to Geometric Topology, version 4, September 2025. The article's bibliography gives the precise locations. The extension of the constant-coefficient comparison to flat coefficients is supplied in the article and was included in the review. The finite-volume cusp theorem, existence of good covers, and small-chain comparison are imported foundational results. The review did not audit every theorem on which these sources depend. It concerns the topological comparison with interior cohomology; an identification with cuspidal automorphic cohomology would require additional spectral results.
